The thing about this game is that they picked a very hot topic in the gaming community and had a humorous premise to go with. Social justice warriors, the infamous scourge of the internet gaming community, who have recently done their part to ruin everything as we used to know it.
Except, the problem is that in this game, the trolls exemplify one of the logical fallacies in the standard school of "logic",  which itself is used ad nauseam in the game, referred to as "No middle ground"  It's very clear that there is heavy bias painting the SJW as the hero, when the reality is (despite the disjointed and non-existent arguments presented by the trolls [caused by  the game deciding the "troll's" next moved based solely on a random number roll associated with a set of statements]) BOTH sides in the game are trolls, and some of the statements that were used for the troll side's dialogue are actually reasonable, if not the outright truth. Even so, they don't make any sense because they are random, so it's not as if you are battling a "troll" that's actually presenting a real argument.
This was probably done on purpose, but for a game it doesn't work. When you argue with a real retard on the internet and they say something non sequitur, that's the end of it. Unfortunately the game doesn't end.
Once you get past the humor of "lol, I earned the favor of the necromancer and he used me to achieve his goal of becoming a lich", this game plays no differently from any of a dozen flash games - hentai or not - where you just have to use a list of pre-determined moves to try and reduce the enemies health gauges while keeping your own at manageable levels. But you don't even get to see♥♥♥♥♥♥afterwards.
As someone else said in their review, I wish I could give it a thumb sideways. Regardless of your opinion about SJWs, the game is shallow, inconsistent, and boring.

In recent years, debating on-line in the name of "justice" has not only become a norm throughout the internet, but also the center of hot button topics in pop culture and news organizations. Of course, it was only a matter of time before someone tackled the concept of keyboard warriors and turned it into a game. Enter:
. Nonadecimal Creative present this casual independent RPG/Simulation title that pits one of these social justice individuals against hordes of trolls looking to wreak havoc in r/. You are the voice of sanity in this offering, but if is as positive a message about society today, or does it just paint itself to be nobler than thou in the most insulting of ways possible?
As stated, you take on the role of your every day social justice bringer behind a computer screen. You take on various trolls, largely ignorant or rabbid ones, utilizing health and mana in the form of sanity and reputation. Each are affected by your opponents choice of words, or even by your own actions like a direct "lunge" at someone's character. The more you assert how right you are over your opponent, the more the Social Justice Knights, mythical beings that represent sanity and reason in the game's internet world, smile upon you. The better they look upon you, the more they alter the battle at hand, positively or negatively. But, once one of your bars are depleted, the game is lost, and your name enters the Hall of Justice for all to see, leaving you to start anew through standard Rogue-Like rules.
While
stands as a great idea in theory, the execution greatly misses its own point. First, you need to understand the goal of this game. The following is a quote taken directly from the title's Steam store page under the "About" section:
In the actual game itself, you play the role of someone who is meant to support the greater good, taking on all trolls in your path to do so. Your foe, who looks exactly like you, says something one might consider stupid, which, from my time with this game, was mostly about women or women's rights, to which you have to point out why the troll is wrong. However, this is largely an opinion-based system, and not all the things the trolls say are entirely inaccurate. The same goes for your characters legitimacy as far as statements go. This goes on until the arguments change for a brief amount of time, such as tackling racism, before just shooting right back into inequality with the ladies once more for no reason other than probably running out of talking points on said topic.
The game is also played through the use of four different attacks, which the type of move is named differently upon the choice of your standard stock
characters (and just as similar sound track) ranging from Rogue, Mage, Paladin, and Cleric. Each one also offers different incentives with additional random knights appearing to do things like give you a riddle, attack the opponent, or bestow some sanity or reputation to keep you alive. There is a necromancer, but he's basically worthless outside of giving you one last shot you won't really benefit much from other than one more shot at the troll who's opinion differs from yours.
There's also a level system, though it seems absolutely pointless as you stand as much of a chance taking on and defeating an enemy a few levels higher than you compared to one a level or two lower than you. This leads to another issue, which ends up being balancing, and an ineffective combat system all together. In the games I played trying to figure out what attack best worked with what comment, I would lose after four, maybe five trolls, the latter if I was lucky. However, while taking a break in this review, I went ahead and played as the Rogue and, for the sake of curiosity, just kept spamming the enter key over and over. By doing so, not only did my character take down a foe six levels higher with four hits, but this was the longest battle waged, having reached the tenth troll. This means nine enemies, four of which sub-bosses, were decimated by spamming one single button, and the only reason the character was defeated was because the Troll Warlord boss knocked down nearly all of the three-fourths filled sanity bar in one shot, leaving very little chance for my warrior to survive.
As far as the gameplay itself goes, you basically just choose a text prompt until you win or loose. While this aspect does stick with the traditional J-RPG template, but, the game is literally just that. You can take the high road with facts, block, share your foe's statement to your followers, or just attack by degrading yourself to insults, repeat until you defeat the enemy, immediately fight the next. Having a choice of topics to fight for so players can choose something they may be passionate about, or perhaps choosing their own text instead of just an attack name with the next scripted set of lines coming up, would have allowed a little more variety outside of staring at the eight-bit zombie-looking slacker you don't care anything about. Maybe if you could customize him (her?) beyond the name input would help build the slightest bond to your character.
But the final nail on the coffin for
is the inability to play as the troll. You are committed to just being the good guy in a game about opinions, meaning you should be allowed to play devil's advocate as well. This would further push the theory that we're all just spinning our wheels in the mud by bickering about these topics to assert who's♥♥♥♥♥♥♥(literal or metaphorical) is bigger, all the while landing attacks that basically counter the point of your character. If anything, this title airs more on the side of preachy by focusing only on the positive, helpful, or beneficial aspects of the arguments that your character alone makes, and tearing down any the opponent might have that actually may be factual or far more grounded in reality than our faceless main character. Even the most spiteful on-line arguments can sometimes have a middle ground, one specific thing people can agree on to end things amicably, which isn't any sort of option in this game either. Instead, we are left with a "I'm right and that's that" debate anyone stuck in a religious discussion will immediately find themselves wanting nothing more to do with this title.
offers very little to the player overall. The gameplay is weak and as basic as it can possibly get, there's no real variety whatsoever except the same animations on a loop (though the troll slamming the monitor onto the desk is humorous the first few times you win a fight), and, what's more, it kind of misses it's own point. You could argue that Nonadecimal Creative is trying to show even the most well intentioned keyboard warrior is, in fact, an internet troll or bully him/herself. After seeing the depths some of these people go to pick a fight in the name of "justice", even when there's no need for it, they have a point. However, the game isn't presented this way. Instead it's a boring, depressing to look at game or incredibly basic RPG fundamentals, some of which are pointless, and generic topical battles you more than likely won't give a damn about at all. A few plays in and you'll start to wonder what exactly the developer was trying to achieve with this title that is so minimalistic that it actually loses it's gimmicky replay value after your first few deaths.

Having just completed his game, I have to say that it was a very satisfying play.
The immersion factor is fairly good, you do feel like you're trying to solve a mystery while playing the game. The storyline is one of its strong points, with enough loose ends and red herrings to keep you playing just to find out what is going on. In terms of the challenge, the majority of the puzzles are of the point and click variety (Broken Sword) instead of the mini-games vaeriety (7th Guest). The backgrounds and settings are gorgeous- it is obvious that a lot of effort and research has been done for the game, and it shows.
I particularly appreciate that the solutions to the puzzles are logical and make sense, instead of being ludicrously far-fetched so as to increase the difficulty level.
Cons wise- The character animations I feel do not do justice to the excellent voice acting. It can be particularly jarring when, for example, you have to sit through several minutes of conversation with Mrs Miller whose jaw appears to be dislocated. And some of the male characters appear to sidle across the floor in an effeminate manner. Other have mentioned bugs in the game but I personally did not come across any.
Play this game if you want to relax with a good mystery story, lush settings and logical puzzles. A good way to spend a quiet evening.

I wish I could give a thumb sideways. I think the idea is great. As a proof of concept for a starting point to work on a more fleshed out game this could work very well. As it is though, I feel that fails both as a game and as satire.
It's very short. I'm talking a few minutes here. There's too much reliance on a random number generator and after a few tries I just got to the point of not caring what I picked because it all seemed just random anyway. There's also really not a lot to it. It's just Defender picks one of 4 responses to troll, hit enter, roll the RNG, rinse, repeat. That's pretty much it. The same responses tend to show up too so it won't take very long to start seeing repeats of what you already saw.
I'm willing to make allowances for games to be shorter, cruder and have less meat to them if their main point is satire, DLC Quest being a great example of this, but in this case it's just too short and too rudimentary. I really wish there were more to it but there's not.
On the satire end it seems to fall flat too. I think the combination of the satiring the White Knight complex of the so called 'Social Justice Warriors' being too subtle (a quick glance at the forums shows that many people didn't get that they were being satired and not celebrated) along with the opposing side always being portrayed as trolls for the sake of trolling just makes the whole thing not work.
As far as I am concerned, both sides take this subject matter and their role in it way too seriously and could well do with a mirror being held up. While true trolls exist, most people who get involved in these internet crusades do believe they are in the 'right' so not having the ability to choose both sides as a hero (in their own mind) seems to have the effect of making the whole thing come off as a SJW propaganda piece to many. Which it's not; having to 'retreat to a place where everyone agrees with you' is not exactly a quality to be celebrated but it seems many people don't get that far and just write the game off.
If you have to explain your satire then it really hasn't done its job.
Mostly though I just wanted more game. More to do. More from the opposition's perspective. Maybe planning and strategizing outside of the forum 'combat'. Something to make the game play last more than 5 minutes and be less random. Just more. The seed is there but it needs much more than this.
I'd love it if we could get updates or this could get much more fleshed out but as it stands I really hesitate to recommend it at any price. There are 99 cent mobile games that give much more game play than this and if you want Gamergate satire you're probably better off searching Google for an opinion piece article. It would take you longer to read than the time you would spend playing this game anyhow.

It is not surprising that this game stirs up attention.
Its a social commentary, a satire. And it hits where it hurts.
For all those who engaged in internet arguments before, it is a mirror that they have to look into, and what they see is that there is no winner in these bitter arguments on twitter, reddit or wherever they happen. It makes people reflect and they don't like what they see.
From a perspective of someone who doesn't take part in such arguments, its a humoristic experience, that shows the absurdity of the human behavior on the perceived anonymity of the internet. The Social Justice Warriors and the Trolls they fight are one and the same, just with different coloring. In the end there is no winner.
The Gameplay is solid, 4 classes with different abilities, high score table, lots of references, funny and sad at the same time. It's good to be played for short bursts but gets repetitive relatively fast. No bugs encountered.
The asking price is probably too high for the length of the entertainment that might be provided.
Still it is a worthwhile experience,
and it's probably the game people deserve.

Exploration. Human curiosity. Space adventure.
Astroneer is still a project, something different from the classics survival games around nowadays. It's a game that uses a different approach to the "open world" exploration model. When you play it, you can feel from the first moment, the loneliness, the wonder and the excitement to be the only human on an alien planet. Sometimes when you are waiting for energy recharging ( a very interesting game's mechanic ), you are forced* to look around you, and a mix of amazement and fear starts to flow in your blood, even if it is just through a simple screen. I'm not speaking about the graphic*, don't misunderstand my words, there are games far better on that, but what I'm trying to tell is that the concept itself, the music, the game mechanic, the vegetation and landscape colours, creates a perfect scientific-fiction setting hard to find elsewhere.
I will not tell you how the game is, you have to discover by yourself. Imagine to be the next human sent on a planet. You don't know anything, you are sent to get information for the human race on earth. That is, astroneer is waiting for you, are you brave and ready for that?
Yes? Ok then, lets the journey begin!
* You are not forced, I just mean that while you are waiting there is nothing to do some time, at least in the first moments of the adventure, late on you will be very busy!
* The graphic style chosen is quite minimal but so adapt and harmonious that will captivate you from the first moment.

Borderlands 2 has to be one of my all time favorite games. It is affordable (when on sale) and is a lot more fun than many other games on the market. I would highly reccomend this game to anyone who likes video games because of how long you can play it without becoming tired of it, and just because of how fun it really is.
Play with up to 4 friends at any given time as you go through the story mode which is very detailed and has many missions to complete to earn in-game currency, weapons, and exp to level up your charecter to become even stronger than you were before. The fun never ends with 3 game modes, with the loot becoming increasingly better, aswell as the difficulty increasingeach time. The graphics arn't bad for being a couple years old, and the weapons look very cool. There is no thing I really like more than the other in Borderlands 2. The story mode is very fun, earning cool weapons and raiding places for loot is also fun. There is just so much to do, which makes it easy to keep playing without getting bored, especially if you have a short attention span like me.
If you havn't got Borderlands 2 already, you are missing out. You can get it on sale for 5$, or sometimes even cheaper on other sites. If you are going to buy Borderlands 2, I would reccomend buying the GOTY Edition because of all the DLC which makes the game even more fun and interesting, although the game is still very fun without DLC.
*WARNING SPOILERS AHEAD*
The game starts out when you wake up as a vault hunter in the snow with a robot named Claptrap, who will guide you through the game. Vault hunters are very rare, and their mission is to stop Handsome Jack (the main villan in the story). Handsome Jack hates vault hunters and will kill them whenever he has the chance. You soon start to gather some weapons, ammo, a shield, and more. Across the planet of Pandora (the planet everyone is living on) there are Bandits, which will try to kill when when they have the chance. Killing enemys such as bandits will reward you with exp, to help level up your charecter, which will give you more health, and access to more weapons (weapons will require a minimum level to use).The higher level the enemy, the more exp and loot given. Enemys also drops things like weapons too, aswell as health packs to help replenish your health. All around there are chests, some containing better loot than others. These chests contain ammo, guns, health, shields, grenades, certain class mods, relics, and more. Once you start getting better you will face harder enemys, and some bosses here and there. Eventually, you get to Santuary, a town of people who all hate Handsome Jack. You will join the Crimson Raiders, a team trying to take Handsome Jack out. You are assigned to do more missions there. Roland is the leader of the Crimson Raiders. Soon you meet Lilith, Roland's ex, who helps you rescue Roland who has been captured by bandits. Roland and you will become friends, but soon some bad news comes in from Roland's spy, Mordacai. He finds out that Handome Jack has been charging a vault warrior with eridium (an ancient alien rock). This vault warrior will obey its awakener, which Jack hopes to become. If Jack gets ahold of this warrior, he could use it to take anyone who he wanted out, which would be you. In the end, you are about to kill Jack, but before you do, he manages to awaken the warrior. You will have to kill the warrior as your last mission, and let me tell you that is not the easiest thing to do. If you defeat the warrior, you will be able to kill Jack, and save everyone from his evil ways. Once you finish the story mode, you will be able to go to the next mode where you do the story all over again with harder dificulty and better loot.
Overall, Borderlands 2 is too complex of a game to fully cover in one review, but I tried to give you as much information as possible. If you havn't bought Borderlands 2 already, what are you doing? Just buy it. It is worth every penny ;)

Extremely fun hack and slash game, that sits in a beautiful state of edgy. It isn't 12 year old sonic fanboy edgy, it's a fun self-aware edgy that works well. It's characters are good, not amazing but they actually feel real to some degree unlike some games. The game is sadly brought down a bit by enemies and bosses that don't work with the berserking combos you're supposed to do in this game. Later on with the more abilities you have, the easier it is to get a good combo. Getting an A rank is hardly satisfying at the end as all you need to do is avoid attacks. A lot of it relied on the heavy weapons, with shielded enemies and enemies with a shell being weak. One of the few enemies that's taken out by light weapons can be done so passively with the glaive weapon. Each weapon is forced to be used in one situation or another by using invincibility. I don't disagree with making me use heavy weapons a lot, as I love them, but if the other weapons could break through shields better or handle the same enemies, there would of been more variation in my combos in the late game. Sometimes it's not just this weapon type system, there are ninja enemies who can block bullets and melee attacks. The only way I know to attack him, without waiting for him to attack, is by shooting and using demon pull. It takes a while to kill him and isn't fun as i'm only limited on how to fight. It's not forcing me to be more creative with combos or encouraging me to switch up my weapons, but it's doing the opposite by forcing me to use one weapon or not combo and stay safe.
That was a bit of an unorganized rant, but essentially, the game is great but suffers with how it makes the game difficult. It ruins the flow of the game with it's methods and makes fighting some bosses and enemies not fun. One weapon is literally required or is better for the job so much that you keep using it for that one situation. Yes combos are pure fun but late game doesn't let you have that pure fun. It's the ♥♥♥♥ing witch again or it's the colored dudes again.
It is a great recommended game, a very solid and fun Hack and Slash with a combo system that is pure fun. It's late game sadly doesn't blend well with the game's combat, but that can be overlooked for how fun the game still manages to be. On higher difficulties, i can see this game being even funner than on normal. It's a bit short at 8 hours for me, but it's meant to be replayed on even more challenging difficulties and completed.
8/10

Excellent adventure game. This is a wonderful, wonderful game. It is an absolute must for any adventure gamer. I'm halfway through episode one and the game I have played so far is what other developers are selling as complete titles. And I still have many, many hours to go. Very clever game, makes you think, great music, makes you feel like you are inside a captivating mystery novel. (A.C. - Which the game pays respects to, constantly)
HOWEVER
It has very frustrating technical problems. Aside from the difficulty of moving around, the game literally gets stuck at certain screens and since there are no autosaves, you lose a lot of time that you have invested in the game. The first time it happened to me, the screen completely froze and I had not saved it so I quit and did not return to the game for months. Now that I have returned and progressed more, I am once again stuck in a screen that I cannot get out of. And this will also make me lose hours of work.
FINAL VERDICT
It's most certainly much, much better than any other adventure game out there for the past few years but the bugs may make you go crazy.

Fantastic game!  Obvious issues aside (bugs, optimization, etc) this game is really solid for pre-alpha or alpha.  Starting off is intuitive enough.  The game gives you some direction on where to click, how to build and gather, etc.  But it doesn't completely hold your hand.  No tool-tips for the things you build means you need to just build and try stuff out.  Resources are easy to gather so you can build and experiment without feeling like you made anything that you can't use.
Great balance of resources in a starting area, but then pushing you to explore to get more resources.  Smoothing tool works well. Updates come fairly often so you know the dev's are continuing to work on it.

This is already, despite being in alpha, a decent space crafting game.  Most of the mechanics are easy to use and understand and there is a fair amount to do.  You can explore, gather, craft, dig, etc.  You can build forts.  You can travel to other worlds.  Reminds me of Grav, in many ways, but with a mutable environment, and without any mobile enemies.
The only real blot is that, while single player works really well, multiplayer tends to be buggy and require workarounds for players function.  Sometimes it's hard to connect.  It doesn't tell you when you've successfully connected.  Anytime a player connects, there's a huge lag spike.  There's a bug with being able to slot items that pops up occasionally that we finally discovered could be fixed by the effected player jumping into the pod and back out.  Occasionally, resources and terrain features are visible to one person, but not another.
Despite all that, however, the game shows enormous potential, and is already fairly addictive.

Exploration. Human curiosity. Space adventure.
Astroneer is still a project, something different from the classics survival games around nowadays. It's a game that uses a different approach to the "open world" exploration model. When you play it, you can feel from the first moment, the loneliness, the wonder and the excitement to be the only human on an alien planet. Sometimes when you are waiting for energy recharging ( a very interesting game's mechanic ), you are forced* to look around you, and a mix of amazement and fear starts to flow in your blood, even if it is just through a simple screen. I'm not speaking about the graphic*, don't misunderstand my words, there are games far better on that, but what I'm trying to tell is that the concept itself, the music, the game mechanic, the vegetation and landscape colours, creates a perfect scientific-fiction setting hard to find elsewhere.
I will not tell you how the game is, you have to discover by yourself. Imagine to be the next human sent on a planet. You don't know anything, you are sent to get information for the human race on earth. That is, astroneer is waiting for you, are you brave and ready for that?
Yes? Ok then, lets the journey begin!
* You are not forced, I just mean that while you are waiting there is nothing to do some time, at least in the first moments of the adventure, late on you will be very busy!
* The graphic style chosen is quite minimal but so adapt and harmonious that will captivate you from the first moment.

I got Euro Truck Simulator 2 on sale back in June 2015, and I can say it was worth it on sale. I've been wanting to make a review on it for a while now - actually, for longer than I've wanted to make a review for American Truck Simulator - but the problem is, no matter what I write, it won't do the game justice - I can't fill the "Good" section enough.
-
Seriously, it's easy to lose hours upon hours in here. Turn on the ingame radio, put a podcast on, or just cruise and listen to the engine.
-
So what if there's sunflowers everywhere. It's pretty.
-
The game makes itself easy to mod, in a system not unlike VALVe games (well, except CSGO). Only, instead of a "custom" folder it's a "mods" folder in your documents. However, on the in-game part of modding, the game differs in one way, for the better: There is an in-game mod manager. Go nuts.
-
Seriously, it's pretty extensive. Lamb stomachs, tyres, fireworks, petrol, ammunition, sulphuric acid... and that's just scratching the surface. They handle mostly the same, though.
-
Turn off your truck's governor (sadly, changing it requires mods) or make it rain 24/7. The settings there cater to all sorts of people, from the diehard fans with the 18-speed shifters in real life, to the casual folks that just want to shift into drive and go.
-
Try it. Go ahead.
-
All you'll see in the game is a moderate rain at best that barely warrants the use of your wipers on the low setting. No snow, no heavy downpour, just a moderate shower at worst (that I wouldn't even consider turning on my wipers on my little station wagon in real life for).
-
, surprisingly. You can get great frames out in the countryside, but you'll feel it when you near a city.
-
Generally speaking, the traffic AI is pretty good, but sometimes they make you wonder what in the actual ♥♥♥♥ is happening - stopping on the highway, merging into your trailer, stuff like that. Instances of that are few and far between, but they do happen from time to time.
-
This is averted in the Scandinavia DLC (and I don't drive much in France), but the cities that you deliver goods to feel like giant industrial districts. There's very little in the way of stores or little houses, or even pedestrians.
-
None at all. Meaning, you can't downshift and hear it echo, or blow the airhorn and scare the pants off of everyone. (Blowing the horn doesn't actually do anything in this game, anyway, as far as I can tell.)
If you can get past the simplicity of this game, I'd say go for the demo and see how you like it. There's a bit of DLC, but the main three you would really want are the three area DLCs - the France one that just came out, the Going East DLC, and the Scandinavia DLC; all of which expand the world.
All-in-all, I'm going to say it's worthy of an A-.

Some DMC fans saw this game as a dissapointment and overall step back for the series. Going on about how bad the new dante is and how dumb the story is, but people dont play a hack and slash for the story. What matters is gameplay and this game delivers in that aspect not only more than any other game in this series, but any other game in the genre as a whole.
Good level design, enemies that are fun to fight, and nearly unlimited combo potential. Being able to not only swap weapons on the fly, but start a chain of attacks with one weapon and end it with another is something I found very fluid and fun. The aerial combos are especially satisfying. Something about being able to keep multiple enemies airborn for minutes at a time while still keeping the combo fresh feels great to me. The flow of combat in this game is unrivaled, it is just simply the best hack and slash when it comes to how well the attacks chain together. Also it has a great soundtrack that fits the game well.
Dont let some angry DMC fans fool you, this game is a ton of fun. I wholeheartedly recommend this game to any fan of the hack and slash genre as well as any action game fans in general.  So what are you doing reading this? Go and get those SSS ranks!

If you enjoy constantly being pitted against players far above your skill level without your say and losing many, many matches before you even get a grip on how the game works, then this is your game. The matchmaking system is so flawed, it has effectively driven away anybody who might pose a fair, but not punishing, challenge against you.
Because of the matchmaking, this game has two difficulties in essence: Stupid Easy and Stupid Hard. Pick your poison.
The gameplay itself doesn't have much to it. Just level up contacts, shoot at some players once in a while, and do the same set of fetch quest, ram raid, or deathmatch objectives pretty much every mission. That is the meat of the game, and it's not subject to negotiation The game is based around PvP, and normally, it would be something you could have a bit of fun with after gathering up a few friends and duking it out in the streets like you're supposed to. But then we come back to the matchmaking issue, which takes the aspect of 'fair competition' and chucks it straight out the window.
It's also not a very well optimized game. I can accept when a game is simply too intense for my PC to handle, but this game certainly shouldn't be on the list of "I need to turn A LOT of settings down before I can play" games. I'm not running on a potato, either. It's just terribly optimized. So, word of warning, do not expect to run this at high and get smooth frames on anything less but the most rugged of gaming rigs with a lot of resources to burn.
The best thing I can say about it, really, is the customization. It truly is the one aspect that takes this mediocre game a step up into the realm of competitively mediocre. 'Course, don't expect to make any particularly insanely awesome character outfits without dropping real money or grinding the game's endlessly monotonous objectives, all while battling the world's worst player matchmaking system.
Until this game gets its crap together with the supposedly upcoming engine update, I can't recommend this title, even in its free-to-play format. Play it if you want, but prepare to get annoyed.

Enjoyed the game, but found that the 'twist ending' actually messed the story up for me a little. When you're role playing a character, it's annoying to then suddenly lose all control of who that character is and what he's doing. I felt like I had control of the characters and could choose who they were - at least to some extent - and the ending felt more than a little forced. Nonetheless, I did enjoy the game. The voice acting was really good for the most part, and the story was entertaining. It also had the unique quality that you felt like it could actually happen, almost. Most games like this rely on fantastical magical boxes that couldn't ever actually work. This game really stuck to the 'real world' even though the crime was of the complicated fiction variety.

Really enjoyed this little game. A fairly uncomplicated, unfussy point-and-click adventure that is relatively short and not hugely challenging (compared to some absolutely evil puzzles that can be found elsewhere in this genre) but nonetheless, the story is interesting and fun to try to solve as you go along, the voice acting and scripting is really good and the soundtrack is great too. There's an occasional glitch here and there when the characters are walking around and get temporarily stuck on their surroundings which gets a little tiresome, plus the controls aren't the most intuitive, but since the game is so charming overall, I put it down to being a quirk.
I'd recommend sticking this on your wishlist and getting it when it appears on sale - my opinion is that, despite really enjoying The Raven, I think £25 is a little steep for what is a casual, lightweight point and click adventure. I picked it up when it was 75% off and I think I got a bargain.

The good:
Some nice environments and decent character design.
The bad:
Stiff, laborious dialogue. I played it in English with no subtitles, it's a German game so perhaps the original German is better...

Illogical puzzles. I can't even begin to describe these 'puzzles'.
For a detective/investigation game, the player does absolutely no figuring out of anything.
Very little interactivity - just click and listen to characters talk for minutes.

For example, if you say that your character is a brony, then you would most likely only fight trolls. If your an anti brony, you would focus on bronies, while fighting others. I was also hoping for a free roam element where you could go to amazon which would be the merchants where you could buy items to fix up your sanity levels or your PC. It could also have quest too.
Sadly, this game is just battling a few type of trolls, from the popular trolls to the rabid trolls. It gets boring real fast and doesn't really have much replay value. On top of all of this, according to the disscussions, the developer is calling people who dislike the game, "trolls". I hate trolls, but I guess that i'm one of them in the eyes of the developer.

Super Meat Boy is a very well designed game, and I love how the game looks, and feels when it is played, but I unfortunately cannot say that it has aged well. When using an operating system that Super Meat Boy was designed for, .e.g. Windows 7 or older, it works perfectly. However, running the game on Windows 10, or even new versions of Mac OS X results in a huge amount of crashes, even when doing simple things like changing the resolution. It is still playable, but it is definately something to consider before buying the game. I would recommend Super Meat Boy to anyone, but because of the current bugs, I would suggest only buying the game if you can get it on sale, or through a third party site at a discount.

While I love platformers, I genuinely find the controls of Super Meat Boy to be lacking. I statement one might find ironic, as they're extremely simple - however, controlling your character in the air is agonizingly difficult. There's an odd momentum, and a lag thereof when it comes to moving against one's current trajectory.
All said, I still recommend this game. It's a very early 2000's style of goofy internet/gaming humor that's mostly lost nowadays. And the game was the first by E.M., who later developed The Binding of Isaac - which is an incredible game. This is a game worth beating, but not worth completing.

You will enjoy this game if you like:
-Creating an efficient, profit maximizing base.
-Cross breeding.
-Capturing wild animals (slimes, in this case :P ) and making them enjoy it.
-Making a self sufficient farm.
-Exploring for rare crops that you can take back and multiply.
As an avid player of farming, sandbox, and other simulation games from Harvest Moon to Gnomoria, I really enjoyed this game, even in an Early Access experience.
It appeased to my nature of trying to make the 'perfect' base.  This release (I am on 0.2.4b) had two expansions on the ranch (thankfully, I was worried when I started really getting into the game).
I also love profit.  This game had a satisfying method of cross breeding that helps maximize income.
The world is well designed and I didn't experience any common issues you would find in early access games like crashes or 'stuck in the floor/wall' issues.
As long as the content updates keep coming, this game can be replayed again and again.  There is so much potential to this game.  At this point, it took me about 10 hours of gaming to really dig through all the content that is provided right now.
Keep it coming, Devs, and I will keep playing!

DmC: Devil May Cry really lets Ninja Theory as developers shine in the combat department.  While at first the controls seem overwhelming, as time progresses, the deeply rich and fluid combat system really shines.  However, if you are here for the story and enjoyed former DMC titles than this may not be the title you seek.  The reboot does an excellent job as setting itself as a action/adventure title but draws little more than names and somewhat the look of previous DMC titles.  Then, it takes the persona of Dante and remakes him to more of a modern goth/emo style character that doesn't give a damn about anyone or anything.  Which is fine.  This is a reboot.  But, it is not like the former titles at all.
Overall, the graphic style and the combat make the game stand out while the storyline felt really hollow and this becomes problematic as when you go back to replay missions to unlock secrets or grab higher scores, you have to sludge through that storyline again and again.  Unfortunately, after the second playthrough you will more than likely fill like you've had your fill.  Also, the 40.00 price tag is a little steep for an older title at this point.  I'd wait for a sale but it is worth a pickup at some point if you enjoy fighting games.

I  definitely prefer this game on console (I have 233 hours on console), but only because i'm not good at first person shooters on PC. Aside from that, I love this game. It is the most unique game I lave ever played, with the graphics and the wide variety of interesting characters and guns. The game uses a mechanic that generates thousands of random guns, which is very well structured. There is a rarity scale for the guns, that goes from white (the most common) to green and then to  blue, purple, and orange (legendary guns). Legendary guns are usually not randomly generated, as there are few enough to where the developers just made them themselves.
The game has an eccellent story, one that I refuse to spoil, but I will say that the events of the first borderlands caused a rare mineral called eridium to start growing all over pandora, the planet the game is based on. The growth of eriduim attracted many, the most important being a company called hyperion, led my the villan, Handsome Jack. Jack is my favorite villan of all time, and is known to many for being one of the greatest villans in a video game ever. He's ruthless, he's cruel, he has a great backstory, and he's hilarious. Most villans won't talk to you at all unless you're in a cutscene, but no, this guy will taunt you throughout the entire campaign.
If you want a good in depth video review, go to YouTube and search: Borderlands 2 angryjoeshow. It might be silly at first, but he does get serious after a couple minutes.

As someone who has no experience with the Devil May Cry series, I thought this game was a fantastic time.
* The gameplay is the selling point here, with endless ways to juggle enemies and fluidly switch between movesets.  There's also platforming here and there, but it feels more like an obligation to add variety.  Thankfully the platforming is mostly harmless and very easy.
* The story is pretty laughable overall, but as a person who ironically enjoys bad movies, I think it adds to the fun of the game.

In your second and third playthough though, you've finished learning how the myriad of weapons work, so the game throws tougher enemies at you with more devious combinations. And if Sonic is just another protagonist like every other game has one...well...
I may not have played much of this game, but what I've seen so far go well beyond technical limitations of that time. Camera angles are terrible, the plot seemingly starts of clueless (who the hell is that blue creature and why does the police decides to fire at it without it even being threatening?) and somehow assumes everyone is on board and okay with it. Tails crashes his plane, but has nothing to do with anything. Animations are floppy and glitchy (though that may have been standard for that time) and the hub level annoys me more than anything else (I can't even figure if those people are supposed to be people or statues).
Music's kind of alright, but those voices are really beyond pathetic.
Again: the title may just have aged terribly, and may not have been for me to begin with (Mario 64 was just a 'meh' title for me as well). But it honestly baffles me that it has so much high critic reviews at that time. I don't think I would've liked the game back then. To today's standards...I certainly don't.
Don't let nostalgia sucker you into buying this clunker of a game. Check out Sonic Generations instead!

I'd rate this as a 5/10. I would not recommend this game.
I picked it up on a sale for $6.00. At that price I can live with the issues. But, for future gamers considering this title at the normal price tag of $24.99 ($29.99 for Deluxe) - I do not believe this to be a worthy spend.
The game does a good job with visuals, voice acting, and a decent story line. But, there are two things which have resulted in my negative review:
1)	Be prepared for some frustrating character movements - there are times where you just want your 3rd person character to go to a specific location on the screen and he goes to another one altogether - prompting screen load times. This will happen quite a bit. Patience is king here, but I guarantee you this will happen if you use an XBox 360 controller as I do.
2)	On two separate occasions (once in Chapter 1 and once in Chapter 2) - the game glitches and you will have to restart a long sequence of actions, repeating steps that lead up to the freeze.
On item #2 above - this is extremely tedious and nearly boring. The dialogues all over again because the game sequence got goofed up. I literally restarted the entire chapter and it was 30 minutes of repeating it all over again just because one of the "items" got stuck in a loop. It happened again to me a while ago in Chapter 2 in the museum. Rolling my eyes, I have to go through a few game saves to try and not repeat the entire chapter from scratch.
Hate to be negative (frankly - on any game developers), because I can tell they put allot of energy into this title. It just needs to be cleaned up (code) and the normal price should be no more than $9.99 in my opinion.

The Raven is one of the more enjoyable P&C adventures I've played in the past few years. And probably the best P&C mystery/detective adventure I've ever played. I really enjoyed Testament of Sherlock Holmes as well, but this was better done, in my opinion.
Many, many video games seem to be built by developers, programmers and artists, and then have a story sort of try and glue the pieces together loosely for an enjoyable experience. There is nothing wrong with that. There are a ton of really fun games out there with this formula.
In the case of The Raven, it felt like a team of writers (or maybe just one, I dunno) put together a fine story, and then built a game to wrap around it. For me, this was a departure from the typical game formula and a breath of fresh air. BUT, it won't be for everyone.
You get to play three different characters in the game (two male, one female) as you both try to unravel a mystery, and become a deeper part of it at the same time.
The game play is fairly typical P&C, with a few treats in regard to "repeat performances" at very specific "crossroads" in the game (I won't spoil it).
The game isn't without flaws. There are inconsitent commands when it comes to character movement, occasionally sloppy pixel area matching (when your mouse cursor can either click on an object well outside the object, or not at all). Audio sometimes cuts out, and the cutscenes occasionally get wonky. The game crashed on me a handful of times in the 14 hours I spent playing it. It has some warts when it comes to gameplay mechanics and execution.
But all that being said, it was STILL a joy to play. The character development is among some of the best I've ever experienced in decades of gaming. Dialogue that seems nebulous at times ties in wonderfully by the end of the game. In fact, SO good, that you'll even chuckle at the end at encounters that occurred earlier in the game when you realize the full context of the conversation later.
There is subtle and mature humor in just the right places when you've had enough serious dialogue. There are extremely mature subjects that are covered, and conversations that really pull you in if you've lived for longer than a few decades on this planet. And when I say "mature" I don't mean an ESRB version of it. There's not much in the way of sophomoric language or gratuitious violence. But there are very adult themes that many of us become sadly familiar with (or can laugh about) when we get older. And some we'll never laugh about.
The bottom line is that this is a true adult mystery with several wonderful twists, a killer storyline, some fun (but typical) P&C mechanics, and some fun and mostly logical puzzles.
If you enjoy a strong story in your games (or at all), or enjoy mysteries, or generally enjoy P&C adventures, I can recommend this. If you enjoy all three, then I think this title is a "can't miss" and even a bit underrated.

GSL is incredible for an early access game.The controls on both keyboard and gamepad are incredibly tight. There are a tonne of map variations at the moment, but it wouldn't be a stretch to say this game will be able to include so much more content in the future.
If it looks like something you would want to play in its current state, buy it and help support the development to make it the Rocket League of extreme throwing disc mayhem.

Gyrodisc Super League is Valiant Interactive’s early access and Steam debut. It’s an exciting and vibrant arcade sports game in which players throw a disc from one side of the field to the other and attempt to make the opposition miss the disc to score. Games are played similarly to tennis with singles and doubles matches. The game has the potential to be one of the best couch multiplayer sports games on Steam with the fast, frantic action becoming very addictive and laugh a minute.
I did not particularly enjoy the experience of the single player game. The reason for this is simple. It’s far too shallow at this stage of development. You can play individual matches against an AI opponent and that is it. However, to the developers credit they are aware of this and are incorporating an ‘Arcade mode’ that will include multiple unlockable costumes for each character as well as a selection of mini-game modes that have been inspired by classic arcade games like breakout and space invaders. This sounds good in theory but I’d love for them to include a season mode. I find that these games are so much more exciting when you’re constantly battling to win matches in order to finish on top of the ladder and/or to reach the playoffs so that you can win a tournament. Examples of recent games that feature great arcade season or tournament modes include Rocket League (to be featured later on the Steamified Countdown) and Kopanito All-Stars Soccer which we featured back on January 7. It’s a very basic concept but it adds a lot of replayability to your game.
What is present in the game already is definitely enough for the local multiplayer component of the game. I spent a short time playing this mode and for what it was it was certainly enjoyable. I expect that with future updates there will be even more to enjoy on this mode. It’s definitely going to be the biggest selling point for the game and while its still leaning towards more of a concept than a fully fleshed out entity it is already a lot of fun.
A bit of a disappointment is the fact that the developers have no intention of incorporating an online multiplayer game. This will definitely have an impact on the size of the potential player base that the game will have. However, the action is so fast that any latency issues would make playing the game a nigh on impossibility – at least to an entertaining and enjoyable level so I can certainly understand why online multiplayer may be an impossibility for this title.
At this present stage of development if you have friends to play with then purchase a copy of the game because you will already get your monies worth. If not then I’d wait for arcade mode updates and see if what people are writing about it at that time is something that you would enjoy playing.

Nice Party Game!
Played this with a group of friends and had a blast. The game is very easy to pick up and seems simple at first, but once you start pulling off some of the more complicated shots you start to feel like there's a lot of potential for skillful plays.
You can play with up to 4 people locally, plus there are options to play versus AI with customisable difficulty. The AI on the highest setting is absolutely BRUTAL.
There are a few different arenas to choose from too. The standard arena feels the most balanced but the Hockey arena is probably my favourite, with the opportunity to laugh at the expense of your opponents as they fluff a shot around the back of your goal and watch it ricochet straight into their own.
In general I had no stability issues as well which is always nice for an Early Access game!
If you're into local multiplayer or played Windjammers back in the day then I'd definitely recommend giving this a try.

Gyrodisc is both beautifully simplistic and yet full of depth. The core mechanic builds upon the likes of pong, tennis and air-hockey, but this game is so much more. While anyone can instantly understand the game at a glance, once you sit down for a match against another person the scope of the game begins to dawn on you. The gameplay is fast paced and packed with subtle mind games. Play a lame game and keep control of the centre of the court. Or try an aggressive gambit where you force your opponent to the net and challenge their reactions. If you get the read you can charge up a super move to make them pay for their predictability. It really is a great addition to any party game library, and I know I'll be loading it up to play with friends time and time again.

Ill keep this short and objective. This game is pre alpha, so it is supersaturated with bugs and glitches. Some are funny, some are game ruining, and some are just a complete pain in the♥♥♥♥♥ but its what you would expect from a pre alpha game.
The controls are simple and mostly intuitive, and the terrain forming tool is easy to use, however it is a pain to do any large scale building as constant power generation is required and there are really few options early game. In this game, power is a key resource, but the only quick and reliable way to get it is from solar panels which only work during the extremely short daylight cycle.
For content, I would say this met my expectations for a pre-alpha. There is a research tech tree which gives you an objective for a while, but it is unreasonably short and loses its novelty quickly. I would say the exploring is fun and the new planets + discoveries make the game fun for a good couple of hours, but there no actual non environmental enemies.
If you want a fun little game to explore and create, this game might be for you. If you are looking for a challenge and to survive, and really have your skill tested, this is NOT for you.
One last note, if you and your friends all bought this game to have a good time together like you saw in the trailer, think again. My biggest problem with this game is that it is advertised as a great multiplayer game, however after an attempt at playing this with friends, I realized how TERRIBLE the NET CODE of this game is. Apparently the devs have no idea how to optimize net code, so the game decides to update everything... constantly. Ex: "Ohh, player 2 moved 5 feet to the left? Lets just send them the WHOLE ENTIRE WORLD again to make sure they are in sync." As a result of this, you cannot play with more than one other person without crashing the game or booting someone from your server. Also, this game will hog the entire 10 MB upload connection you have so that no one else on your network can connect to anything (not an exaggeration). This is awful especially because this is advertised as a multiplayer game.
Conclusion: Good game for fun singleplayer exploration, a bad for hardcore challenge seekers, and an awful game for multiplayer.

As far as the "DX" label, I don't agree with it since Sonic Adventure DX was originally a Gamecube game and it was ported to PC before the Sega Dreamcast Collection existed. This version lacks a lot of content that was found in DX, including the unlockable Game Gear games that made playing Sonic Adventure DX on the Gamecube a worth while sit down game. At least the frame rate is more steady in this version of the game compared to the PC port however graphically speaking, the system requirements seem a bit much for porting over an XBOX 360 game to the PC.
If you are a pure Sonic fan and you have to have this game, its a must own for any Sonic Fan, but if you are looking for port perfection, this game lack in that department a little more then you think.....

I have been conflicted in putting my opinion out for Super Meat Boy.  With all the rave reviews and it being one of the supposed hallmarks of indie games that other developers are trying to reach with their own games, it is hard to turn around and say this game is a frustrating pile of crap.  I am certain that with all the oddball characters, like meat boy himself, doctor fetus, and the other unique characters, a lot of the charm is the originality and quirkiness, like japanese pop culture, or Ren & Stimpy.  However, looking past the inventive and strange characters and storyline, the game itself is extremely grindy and repetitive.  Maybe I have just been gaming in the land of autosave too long and can't apprectiate the old-school, recently coined "rogue-like" games.  Maybe I don't have the patience that I did as a kid, but more likely, it is that I am no longer required to have the patience I did as a kid.  When perma-death games and mass repetition is all you can choose from, you put up with it, but in a new age where games are meant to be a more fluid experience pushing through a storyline, it is hard to accept 4 hours of grinding on a particularly hard level just to move forward in the game.  Many rogue-likes get this and make games playable without "sticking points" and crazy difficulty curves.  However in some games, including Super Meat Boy in my opinion, they don't seem to understand that people don't want to replay the same level over and over and over.  Overall, this is likely the only gripe I have about Super Meat Boy, as the story and characters are interesting, the old-school graphics are nice, and it truly is fun on some of the levels that have a more normal difficulty curve.  I guess the only way I will see how the story goes is on Youtube or when TellTale releases a "story-mode" for this game.  This is odd coming from a guy who got so far in Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles for the NES as a kid, but these days, I would have junked it after about 20 minutes in and just replayed Skyrim or something.

Vegans beware, you're in for a scare.  You ever stare at a piece of meat in the supermarket and think to yourself, "Man, wouldn't it be cool if that were alive?".
(...Visit a dairy farm.)
I am certain that at least some decent percent of those reading agree.  And who could blame you?  When such a thing as Super Meat Boy exists, what is there not to love?  Super Meat Boy is a gory platformer with a silent cast of characters except for the main menu announcer you hear once during each playthrough.
There are many practical applications to this game, but before we get into those, let us talk about the game itself.  Now the plot is pretty simple, girl made of bandages is kidnapped by evil fetus, very classic tale, but what differs in this game is that there is jumping.  Platforming in this game is rage inducing, yet with a great sense of satisfaction.  Each and every single death you may suffer at the hands of a circular saw or a pile of salt helps you grow and prosper as a player, (unless you're aiming for those ridiculous no-death achievements, good luck) and as you finally reach the goal of each level, upon completing it, you are serenaded with a symphonic score of your past attempts; you get a recap of all of your previous attempts trying and failing in a replay as one shining victor breaks away from the heap, scoring victory.
The characters, while they do not have any huge dialogue...  Pretty much whatsoever, are charming.  Sometimes you may not understand what they are doing onscreen at all as a result, and that is fine.  Super Meat Boy is in now way a visual novel, it is a platformer that you keep playing on and on.  The cast of characters is certainly an interesting thing to begin with, several other video game characters, mainly from indie games, can aid Meat Boy in his quest, such as the ever buddy-buddy Commander Video or a Headcrab from Half-Life, further hammering in the fact that a third Half-Life is nothing but a sad heap of hopes and dreams that nearly everyone, including me, is still desperately clinging on to.
Depressing realities aside, this game is great for a multitude of other reasons aside from the standard gameplay reasons:
-You can apply this to meat butchery in real life!
-Train to escape from those slow saws in spy movies that never work anyways!
-Pretend to paint a firetruck!
The list goes on.  Super Meat Boy is, in my opinion, super charming.  It is bloody brilliant platforming action.  And it is quite literally a meaty game for such a small platformer.

This may or may not be the crown jewel of the genre defining Devil May Cry series that has captivated so many fans across the globe and across multiple platforms, but this has something quite different deep down the core of its heart. I consider this for two reasons.
Firstly this is the title that declares angelic ancestry of Dante's maternal background while his paternal one remains the traditional demonic ancestry. I think this brings a beautiful balance storywise and open more routes in the current plot and future sequels as well. For example, Dante's ability to use both angelic and demonic weapons adds a nice tactical variation.
Secondly the fusion of modern urban culture to the fantasy world has been seamlessly carried out by the Development Team. The urban settings, visuals, wall grafitti and level design is praiseworthy in this regard. The background of Dante and Virgil are nicely presented in outstanding grafitti art.
Thirdly some well discussed elements from our modern day society like DJ Club cultures, demonic eyes disguised as security camera's prying into a citizen's privacy, population control through demonic chemicals disguised as popular soft drinks and the hypcricy of the modern day media on false political propaganda and even political imprisonment. Some later levels even depict the demonic and brainless nature of the multi billionaire corporate finacial sectors as a dark reflection of our present day economy.
Finally the actions, special moves and boss fights are fantastic as usual and even cooler than the previous titles.
That said, I think this is the Devil May Cry title that picks up the series from its fantasy domain and re-establishes it as a solid, mature and realistic title on par with our present global scenario.

I loved Sonic growing up. I wanted to like this game, I really did. But this is something else. This is what happens when you port a game without caring about the end product or the consumer. This is a giant metaphorical middle finger to everyone that has ever had a moment of joy in their lives while playing a Sonic game.
If you can get it to run you're off to a great start. Even better is understanding the control layout from the crappy diagram of an offbrand imaginary Sega controller when you plug in your 360 gamepad. This game has so many glitches it makes Duke Nukem Forever look like Star Citizen.
I can't jump off of a spring or do a spin without falling through an invisible floor or getting bounced back to the beginning of the map. I mean I can. You are a better man/woman/seal than me. However I cannot continue. I can't carry on with this because I have a life to live and we have to let go of our obsessions. Brilliant game to be honest, mostly all thumbs up. Nice plot twists and interesting characters and conversing with them is enjoyable. Very story rich, and there's a lot of things you can interact with that's got nothing to do with the main story but it's still interesting to see/hear.
The only problem I have with the game is the amount of bugs in it. Using one item to interact with another sometimes doesn't work, and requires a client restart (for me at least). Remember getting furious at point and click adventure games because the object combinations were just too damn illogical and impossible to figure out? Then rejoice! This game keeps everything that made point and click adventures great while eliminating this annoying trait. But that's not the only reason why you should get it.
I just finished this game and I can honestly say that it was one of the best point and click adventures I've ever played. The music score was amazing and it fit the game perfectly, the environments were pretty to look at, colorful and rich (the train and Egypt... *drool*). The difficulty was well balanced - I got stuck now and then, but nothing that couldn't be overcome. But what really makes this game stand out so much are the story and the characters. I won't say much about the story because it would be difficult to keep it spoiler-free, but I'll say a bit about the characters. The character work is one of the best I've ever seen in the games. These are no "accessory" characters that are in the game only because someone has to give you clues - they all have their history, their unique personality traits, they react to each other. And their voice acting is very good. Their involvement in the story and how the things you know change as you progress are surprisingly well executed. And the ending had my jaw drop.
Although I love this game to bits, there were some things that made it a little frustrating for me. I never found out how to cancel a movement, so when you accidentally click somewhere, you can't do anything but wait for your character to finish the walk. The transitions between screens were sometimes difficult to find and sometimes the character flatly refused to walk to the next area, making me walk around for a few minutes, clicking on different parts of the floor. It is also somewhat buggy, the character sometimes got stuck in an object and then teleported to the intended direction, or appeared somewhere else before executing an action. But even though these things were unpleasant, they did not affect the gameplay much.
To conclude - if you're a lover of point and click adventure games, then this is a gem you should defenitely not miss. I finished the game in 12 hours and still don't have all of the achievements, so the game time isn't bad. If you're looking for a great story and believable, memorable characters, the Raven is your man (game).

Vegans beware, you're in for a scare.  You ever stare at a piece of meat in the supermarket and think to yourself, "Man, wouldn't it be cool if that were alive?".
(...Visit a dairy farm.)
I am certain that at least some decent percent of those reading agree.  And who could blame you?  When such a thing as Super Meat Boy exists, what is there not to love?  Super Meat Boy is a gory platformer with a silent cast of characters except for the main menu announcer you hear once during each playthrough.
There are many practical applications to this game, but before we get into those, let us talk about the game itself.  Now the plot is pretty simple, girl made of bandages is kidnapped by evil fetus, very classic tale, but what differs in this game is that there is jumping.  Platforming in this game is rage inducing, yet with a great sense of satisfaction.  Each and every single death you may suffer at the hands of a circular saw or a pile of salt helps you grow and prosper as a player, (unless you're aiming for those ridiculous no-death achievements, good luck) and as you finally reach the goal of each level, upon completing it, you are serenaded with a symphonic score of your past attempts; you get a recap of all of your previous attempts trying and failing in a replay as one shining victor breaks away from the heap, scoring victory.
The characters, while they do not have any huge dialogue...  Pretty much whatsoever, are charming.  Sometimes you may not understand what they are doing onscreen at all as a result, and that is fine.  Super Meat Boy is in now way a visual novel, it is a platformer that you keep playing on and on.  The cast of characters is certainly an interesting thing to begin with, several other video game characters, mainly from indie games, can aid Meat Boy in his quest, such as the ever buddy-buddy Commander Video or a Headcrab from Half-Life, further hammering in the fact that a third Half-Life is nothing but a sad heap of hopes and dreams that nearly everyone, including me, is still desperately clinging on to.
Depressing realities aside, this game is great for a multitude of other reasons aside from the standard gameplay reasons:
-You can apply this to meat butchery in real life!
-Train to escape from those slow saws in spy movies that never work anyways!
-Pretend to paint a firetruck!
The list goes on.  Super Meat Boy is, in my opinion, super charming.  It is bloody brilliant platforming action.  And it is quite literally a meaty game for such a small platformer.

A fun and addicting strategy card game that challenges you to improve your deck and gameplay to earn rewards and move up levels and placement teirs. The game features 3 factions to play with a forth on the way. Each faction has its own upside and downside and multiple metas (Deck Themes) to employ giving you a nearly endless amount of strategies to choose from. The game is played out on a gridded 3 by 7 combat board with units employing different movement capibilities. Think of it as a mini chess game on steroids. Board control and a guiding strategy will be essential for your success at higher levels of the game. Players are seperated into 1 of 7 structured point based tiers based on skill levels that prevent new players from being constantly run over by more experienced players. To level up players will need to complete daily challenges that reward you with currency to buy or craft new cards to improve your deck. To craft a competitive deck will require a little grinding if you chose not to purchase cards outright. Yes there is a P2P option for those wishing to hurry themselves into the mix at the top tiers of the game. There is a good starting tutorial to help players get started and the starter decks that each player is provided a actually well balanced decks that are competitive and capible of winning in any of the first 4 or 5 tiers so building your own deck is not a hugh issue and players have an opportunity to learn gameplay while not being completely overmatched in card strength. Another plus to the game is the avialibility of the developers to help give answers and fix any potential problems. I personally have never experenced another game with this kind of dedication and customer relations that you find here. Hats off to the staff for a great game and constant work in making it an enjoyable experience for all new and old players alike. In closeing I say this -TRY THIS GAME! ITS GREAT!

I will warn you beforehand: This game may be fun, but is flawed. You will be forced to watch the credits roll 7 times (and before you think you can just reset your game to skip them, think again, you will be forced to repeat the last mission for each character if you dont watch the whole credits roll). You will also need to deal with a painstaking camera, which will cause you many cheap deaths. Regardless, this game is fun. You are able to use 6 characters, though Sonic's levels are the longest and have the best level designs. Each character has a unique twist in their gameplay, so there's variety. The game has a fitting music, which are mostly cheese-like guitar riffs. The color palette chosen for the game was appropriate: The characters are colorful, with mostly bright colors. This fits with the lighthearted story, and an overall targeted for a child audience. Doing homing attacks to robots it's fun. The game runs at mostly 60 fps (though you may need to turn some graphic options off depending on your computer, even for an old game). The game will take you around 10 hours, which are mostly fun, though it has some padding and repetitive cutscenes. The game's aesthetic fits this game just fine. The music also improves the whole easygoing feel of the game. The gameplay is kept simple (move, jump, and attack), which suits just fine with this game. Perfect gift for a 10 year old, retro gamers, or any sonic fans. Reccomended if you enjoyed: Sonic adventure 2, sonic heroes, and Sonic Generations.

First of all I want to say that I hate games, chapters in which are released separetely. Let me explain why. The first chapter in such games usually is good. All who want to play this game buy it at this point. And developers gain major portion of profit at this point as well. As a result the second chapter of such games is released on a relaxed note and not as good as the first one. Here flow of money generally almost stops which leads to devil-may-care attitude of developers to the remained chapters. And this is what we see in this game exactly. Ok, gotta get safe... gotta get safe... oxygen running low... just follow the signal into this crater... ROCKS, ROCKS, ROOOOOOCKS!!! Ok, check the crater... check the crater... ARRRRRGH! Another radio!  Ok, oxygen 30%.... calm down.  relax.  Walk... go... last one... this has to be it... let's climb out of the crater... keep going... keep going... stop talking to yourself, you're using up precious ROOOOOOOOCKS!!! AHHHHH!!! RUN AWAY RUN AWAY!!! Ok, calm down and stop yelling... no one on the radio... stop talking to yourself... relax... wait... what is that?  It's the ship!  I'm saved! Oh, it's so great to see you guys!  Stilson, Mills, it's so great to see you guys!  We're gonna wait a bit inside where it's safe, we're gonna go home, I'm gonna see my family again, and we will have cake! I love you gu... WHAT THE ------?!?!?!?!
More serious, You won't like this game if you don't get in the mindset like that.  It's a free game, so give it a little leniency.  If you get in the mindset, it is a great game.  If you don't like walking around dodging rocks trying to survive a meteor storm, it's not the game for you.  Some issues... invisible walls, but again, in the DLC, there are no invisible walls.  Rocks disappearing is weird until you get the twist.  I can understand this not getting added just because its a free game, but things that could improve it... change the oxygen system to, instead of a red flash, even at 99%, say an audio warning every 5 % drop, and maybe more frequent red flashes and heavy breathing as your oxygen gets lower and lower below say, 50%.  Another possible improvement, add a headset option, so the more you breathe or talk or yell while playing, the more quickly oxygen gets used.  Finally, intermitent dust storms, at least on Mars, maybe impact clouds on the moon, reducing visibility to less than 30m.  Something to raise the stakes, raise the immersion.   You could even tie the false signals into recorded messages, or even change the color of signals you reach.  I mean, we know from the start that the radio works, so you should be able to pick up radio signals.
Anyway, that's my 2 cents.

I love the game but this port is terrible.
From what I understand, the original came out on the Dreamcast, then was ported to Gamecube. The PC disc version (the one I own and use) was a port of the GC version, and is good aside from a couple of glitches. Now, since then, the GC version has been ported to XBOX marketplace. Apparently it is this version which was ported to be on Steam. I am not usually one to complain when it comes to video games but this is just absolute garbage.
The first thing I noticed was the lack of fullscreen (well, any graphics options at all). I mean, come on, that is something every single video game should have. I have played many completely unfunded indie games and not one of them I have played has lacked the most basic feature of being able to go fullscreen. The game itself is in a tiny resolution (taking up about 30% of my screen) surrounded by an ugly blue patterned border inside of a window, which is really, really offputting.
The next issue was controls. I plugged in my controller and all of a sudden, the camera was eternally rotating to the right, and there was nothing I could do. This was never an issue in the original PC port. In the end, I decided to use my keyboard as I did when I played through the game back when I was younger.
As you can tell, I didn't get very far. I promptly uninstalled this pile of rubbish and got out my original disc to use that instead. I would suggest you do the same if you want to play this amazing game: one of the best 3D Sonic games and a massive chunk of my childhood that was sadly ruined by one of the worst port jobs I've seen in a long while.

The extra mission are challenging as well and once you finish all of them you get to play as Metal Sonic which is pretty rewarding since the only time you see him in the main game is in a tank.
