This is a review from a Devil May Cry player's perspective. I got here through the FF7 Reimagined game, which was great publicity for a studio that's only made one game and came from a background of infomercial games.
It takes inspiration from DMC ('son of Dante') and has some similar attacks. The chests full of orbs are from God of War. Like DMC it uses directional inputs for uppercuts and ground strikes. However, games like DMC and Bayonetta provide precise feedback to your actions. Here, you need to press attack multiple times to register a combo. It makes pulling off complex moves like the rapid-punch finisher much harder than it needs to be. This probably won't be fixed in this release, but it's something to think about for the next one.
Ranged enemies stunlock you. You can get round this, but they also shoot you while you're in the air, which they shouldn't. DMC gives you a reprieve in the air as it's just as important as rolling/dodging. There's also no jump cancelling. It means you have to button-mash your way past a lot of enemies. There’s no style meter and the rankings only come at the end of the level. Aside from that, I can't seem to rebind controls for the xbox one controller or use the keyboard and mouse while using the controller. It loads quite slowly considering it’s on a nvme ssd.
I might be expecting a lot from a struggling Singapore studio, but it’s still leagues better than a lot of the shovelware that gets put on steam. I wish them luck for the future. If I could offer some advice it would be to stick to human characters. Enemies can look like whatever you want. Angels and demons tend to fill the roster for this type of game. At the moment it’s discounted in the Humble Store.

As the game is still in it's alpha phase, there is a lot to be forgiven. For example, if you pressed to Interact with a crate twice instead of just once, there would be a box saying to Take Out popping out whenever you press Interact with other objects even after the crate has disappeared. Also, when putting the input of numbers at shops or crafting, the keys also activate the inventory slots and items would be equipped. In terms of the literal "landless" gameplay, the open world is considered small and I hope there is a radar on the top right to have a compass to tell the direction besides relying on the sun. Or perhaps having the stars as a guide of direction would make the game more interesting. It would be great to have a speed /acceleration meter on the boat as well so that we can upgrade the boats to move at a higher speed as we craft more items for the upgrades. With a lack of tutorials, and description of items, it was kind of challenging to know what items do and what effects it brings such as the hydro turret and interception tower. Also, hacking for blueprints become confusing as it was not introduced at the start of the game if there is a certain correct answer to using the different servers.
Improvements still needs to be done to the UI layers but it's forgiven as the game is still in its alpha phase. Perhaps it would be better to have much more features/improvements added in for the next upgrade. I keep finding it difficult to get around places such as getting off the boat by the ladder and having to jump off instead. Also, I thought we could move the floating platforms around as we travel but no, it was just there. The doors still have an UI box there which I think you guys placed it there to put the scripts for opening the door.
Overall, the game still needs improvement and it would be more fun if it's multiplayer with a bigger town on the sea. The map also seems limited in terms of what other places there are to explore and the main storyline wasn't really clear. It would be great if Professor Goodwell pops out more often to give some tips or reminders on what to do. I would recommend this game to people who love open world survival on a post-apocalypse setting.

Honestly I did not want to purchase this game at all. I was just after DMC4SE, but this game was on sale in a bundle along with DMC4SE, so I thought, "Why not? I'm a huge fan of DMC anyways. Everyone criticizes it, but I'd like to try it and form an opinion myself." And after having cleared this game on Nephilim mode (I play DMC3 & 4 on the 2nd last hardest modes, with Nephilim here being considered "Hard" mode), I can say that this game is by far much MUCH easier than it's predecessors/ great great grandparents. I was a bit upset that the characters were changed to fit different personalities and identities than the ones from the previous DMC's. HOWEVER, I went into the game expecting nothing and with an open-mind, taking the game in for its own identity, not comparing it to the previous games in the series.
And what did I get? I can honestly say that this game is great, though it does have its flaws and missteps, in my opinion. I'd like to get the CONs out of the way before I move onto the PROs of this game.
______________
Cons:
> Lack of lock-on system (this feature is brought into the game in the Definitive Edition, which is only on consoles)
-> Honestly, this may just be me being *slightly* biased, because I've played the previous games and much dislike how I cannot choose my targets with more control. But then again, the lack of a lock-on system does cause small things like falling off a ledge when trying to escape a boss mechanic, or when trying to perform a specific ability.
> Specific-Weapon-Only-Kill
-> Some enemies you encounter in this game REQUIRE you to use a specific weapon in order to eliminate them, which sort of breaks the possibility of combo-ing the way you'd like, limiting your actions.
> Dialogue (Hand-holding)
-> Sometimes, the game tells you what to do, and how to do it (And I get that this is to help players who are new to the series or get lost easily, but I honestly think it just breaks the immersion and idea of puzzles).
Now, onto the PROs.
_______________
PROs:
> Combat system is great! Sure, if you've played any of the previous DMC games, you would say it's horrendous or much worse in comparison, but, regardless, the combat system is still great. It's fun, has lots of ways to chain combos (though aerial combos are super easy to maintain), and you have many options to choose from, considering the multiple weapons you have equipped all at once.
> Story is intriguing! It's a twist and different approach from the previous DMCs, I know, but give it a chance even if you've already played its predecessors. The characters are different from the characters we all know and love, but each character here also has their own things to love and connect to (EVEN IF DANTE ISN'T SO BADASS ANYMORE D:).
> Graphics are great! I honestly prefer the old engine used to animate DMC, but this one isn't so bad itself. Everything looks pretty fluid, and has its own beauty.
> Seems like it'd have replay value. I did JUST beat the game, but I would play it again on the harder modes that you unlock with having cleared the hardest mode available at the time of playing (ex. Clears 'Hard', unlocks 'Very Hard'. Clears 'Very Hard', unlocks 'Super Hard'.)
Well, that's all I can think about currently. Hopefully this was helpful, and helps you guys make your minds.
However, I don't know if I'd recommend this game at FULL PRICE. I would probably wait for a sale.
TL;DR Would recommend (However, not full price). Has nice features & fun combat. Flawed somewhat, but the PROs override the CONs.
WOULD RECOMMEND.

Excellent start for an early release.  The game is decently fleshed out and is very playable.  It's a nice concept and not too difficult to pick up.  I've played for about 8 hours now just tinkering around with some of the mechanics and crafting and so far have only encountered 1 "game breaking" bug.  I have encountered multiple other bugs but nothing that has deterred my enjoyment or ability to play.  The dev's seem very responsive and appear to take action or explain every bug report/suggestion listed in the discussion area and they are pusing out relatively quick patches/versions.  It is still pre-release/mid-alpha stage though, so if you are looking for a completely polished experience I would tag to follow and wait a while.  If you don't mind a few hiccups while still getting to enjoy the game you should invest and support the dev team so they can make it better.
Pros:
* fairly detailed crafting system to include having sub-components to make larger items
* You don't know every crafting recipe right off the bat; but have to learn them as you go -- you get to pick what you want to learn and then hack a network to gain the blueprints to learn it
* very smooth gameplay (it uses Unity)
* decent story line to get you started
* the game is mission based, but it's also free flowing so you can do them at your leisure or just ignore them and free play
* procedurally generated map and encounters
Cons:
* Crafting is a bit cumbersome and can take some time to build things -  very slow to craft just a few items, but the time decreases for each additional item. If you are making say 100 metal brackets  it will take a bit to make the first 5 or so, but the remaining 95 will happen in less time that it took for the initial ones.
* NPCs are pretty weak at this point in the game - basically give you a short dialog text but no real interaction ** exception are mission related NPCs
* Building system is a bit weak - it's difficult to find the sweet spot to your plaform to add a wall or add in stairs with the rolling of the ocean even in calm waters.
* alpha bugs :)

Three other players and I jump into a car and race for the pick-up location. We are just one corner shy of the destination, when an RPG comes flying in out of nowhere and sends us all into oblivion. The camera pans to a female player that looks like she just finished filming a scene for ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s.
One team member and I spawn at a nearbly location and rush towards the briefcase, which is now being held by gentleman sporting a trendy mohawk, sprinting through the narrow back alleys. We hide behind a wall and wait for the enemy to come closer. Suddenly, my co-player gets annihilated by a sniper, hiding anywhere between two blocks and half a lightyear away. Knowing that I am about to get killed in any moment, I jump into the alley and start spraying the gentleman with bullets. By the time I'm halfway through my magazine, he had already dropped the valuable cargo and started firing towards me. Two deadly shots after that and my lifeless body drops to the ground.
At that point, I see that my two other team-mates arrived with a windowless van, that looked like it belonged to somebody who likes to attract children's attention with candy. The copilot was hanging out the window and before he even got the chance to showcase his rat-a-tat maker, he got eliminated by the same marksman that showed his hunting prowess just moments before I died. The driver managed to leap out of the van, but got mowed down by a machine gun faster than a teenage COD player insults your mother.
We respawned shortly after that and by then, the briefcase was already traveling down a highway. I managed to talk a lovely lady into lending me her beige SUV and my crew jumped inside. The race for pride, honor and briefcase holding privilege had begun. I ran all the red lights on the way, nothing could stop my determination. I even handbraked into a couple of corners and pulled some wild powerslides through them, in a way that would put Sebastien Ogier to shame, all  in hopes to catch up with our opponents as quickly as possible. Two kilometers and three squashed pedestrians later, we are on the tail of a menacingly looking vehicle one could only describe as a weird mishap between a Hummer and a soccer-mom's minivan.
My passengers all stuck themselves through the windows and opened fire on the vehicle in front of us. Unfortunately, the passengers of the car in front of us also decided to do the same thing and bullets were now flying towards our car. I started swerving like a mad man, trying to recall moves from Ken Block's latest Gymkhana video, but two of my passengers had already died. I figured the car was already way beyond repair and that there was no way I could ever return it to its owner in this shape, so I decided to go for broke and attempted to ram the car, hoping that it would spin out. I didn't even manage to get near it, when a huge flame burst out of my engine compartment and just moments after that, the car exploded. My buddy and I were burnt to a crisp and we had to start all over again.
The two team-mates that died first had already managed to secure a van and were honking the horn, trying to get us to enter the van. I told the three of them to go ahead, while I went to switch firearms.
Just as I was leaving the police station, I saw a huge truck stopped at an intersection. Thinking that was probably my best chance at doing anything, I hopped in and slowly but surely pulled away. I was driving in the general direction of the briefcase and was picking up speed. Three blocks after that, I was approaching an intersection at a blistering speed and sheer luck had it that the Hummer minivan just came racing through that said intersection and slammed head on into my truck. The truck had no intention of stopping whatsoever and the incredible amount of inertia started shoving the awful looking vehicle towards a building. Nothing could stop the brute force of my truck smashing the car into the wall, crushing it like a car compactor on steroids. The vehicle exploded and a majestic fireball engulfed the remains of the opposing team.
People came from near and far, cheering as I jumped out of the truck and picked up the briefcase. My team arrived just in time, so I hopped into the van and we drove off, ever so slowly. One wouldn't think, but the van really seemed to struggle hauling the extra weight of the briefcase, even if it seemed to be so light when I was carrying it just moments ago. My team complimented me on my spectacular display of driving skills and before I could respond, the unthinkable happened.
An RPG struck the van. And you guessed it, it was Sasha Grey again. I managed to hold the briefcase for twenty whole seconds before it got abruptly taken away again. I watched Sasha walk up to the briefcase and, just before picking it up, whisper: &quot♥♥♥♥♥♥♥n00b fa*gots".
Needless to say, we lost that match. I never played ABP after that and to this day, I still question my sexuality due to Sasha's deep words.

It stands to reason that if player A buys all available cards and player B does not, player A has the advantage.  This is not the developer's fault nor is it fair to label such a game as "pay to win".   Hopefully, over time, the matchmaking system will match like players, but to judge a game on this aspect alone is naive.  I play the AI and the game is not pay to win.  The AI does not gang up on me with scads of better cards, forcing me to invest real money (but I do plan on buying some cards just to support the developers).  I am evenly matched and can chose difficulty settings which is a huge plus.  Get to know the game on Easy, then advance = great replayability.  For an Early Release, this game is quite polished. This game is an interesting hybrid between a trading card game and a classic board game like chess with a Diesel Punk-WWII theme. The combination makes for an extensive depth to the gameplay. While the game is pleasantly easy to learn, mastery is a different story. The large range of card types, different factions and the unique nature of the gameplay ensures a varied an interesting experience with no two player made decks being the same and with no single deck having universal acclaim to the leader-board.
All the content is accessible for free (with the exception of aesthetics), and there is a tonne of content too, three full factions and a neutral support faction. Also, paying players get no advantage over free players with all the content that they purchase having the same drop rate as that of free to play players. As to the grind of the game, its not too bad, especially in getting you into the mid-ranks. Plenty of initial gold drops and boosts to help you get started, after that it balances off a little, but the crafting system takes over at that stage, helping you make powerful custom decks.
The 3D graphics are decent, not great but clean and well textured. The animations are many and mostly well done. The card art however is amazing and considering the hundreds of cards in-game, all of it is surprisingly unique and enjoyable to look at.
PvP is where this game excels, while the first few matches can be bumpy once you're accurately ranked the system gives you quite evenly matched opponents. If you don't have great cards yet, or want to play with some that you don't have the recently released Arena mode is great. Arena mode levels the playing field and beyond the initial luck and skill needed to craft the deck its all skill based, so you can prove your mettle against far more veteran players with ease.
The development team are very active with the game, in the last six months they've added a constant stream of new content and had two major releases. One was the addition of Arena mode and the other was the Shogun Empire, the first of four planned additional factions. Any changes that negatively effect a card you own when addressing balance is also treated fairly, with you being offered the opportunity to exchange the "nerfed" card for any other of equal rarity.
Overall a very well implemented game with a great twist on the classic real-world gaming for the digital age.

Okay, this is my second look at the game. I explored all the available areas, collected the Slime Key and purchased all the upgrades and ranch expansions.
This game, for the first few hours, is fun.
Even after The Tarr make an appearance. Still fun.
Making slimes evolve/upgrade just to get two plorps (poop) for the price of one. Fun and a learning experience!
After having a few fully upgraded corals and farms set up, I was self sufficient in the first few hours.
Then I explored all the available map. You'd think that the upgrades would help get to those high ledges because they hide secret paths. They don't (yet.)
The corals get crowded after ten to fifteen slimed. Five if they're "largos." So you're limited to how many plorts you can collect by this bottleneck. Unless you want to fill your coral with forty Boom Slimes and laugh as you watch them struggle to eat the few Briar Hens you've been able to breed. Then more power to you.
Things I like:
-The cuteness
-The sense of adventure and discovery
-The openess
-The Tabby Slimes and the Boop! Achievement
Things I'd like to see:
-Expandable corals, gardens and coops
-A mechanic where you use Boom Slimes to clear rubble (basically a reason to collect a slime other than profit)
-A use for all those self upgrades, especially the jetpack
-A way to sort out things you don't want to Vacuum up (possibly an upgrade)
-More Vacpack slots
Things I didn't like:
-Nothing comes to mind since this is early access
8/10 Will come back to later.

I got this game in a bundle and fully admit that I don't usually go for brawlers, and I only played to the end of the first level. But the part I did see did not impress. The game seems to be doing everything it does out of an obligation to copy whatever is popular in other games, even when it doesn't make sense or is half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥
Level design is boringly-linear and could have been a flat line for all it affected combat; they just move you around out of a sense of obligation. There were sidepaths but if you pick the wrong direction the camera locks you out of them. You have a double jump and a glide because they think those things are cool, but there wasn't a single place where you DIDN'T need to use the second jump right away to accomplish anything.
There's a "combo" system and you unlock combos as you go but the most effective strategy so far was to just mash light attack forever and occasionally roll. Speaking of, you unlock moves as you level up solely because that's what all the cool games do these days.
Enemies are boring, with uninteresting attacks that you can't really respond to or avoid except by having higher DPS than them. The first boss was just as bad, albeit with one attack you have to double jump over which staggers him afterward.
Also, story is generic crap and cutscenes drag on too long. And rebinding the controls didn't work.
Technically it's possible that the game could get better later on. But I really doubt it. They gave no impression in the first level that they knew what they were doing as game designers.

At first glance, Dusty Revenge seems like an alright beat-em-up, however, just starting a new game reveals a few glaring flaws.
First off, the volume levels are INSANITY. Music's too low, sound effects are too high, and cutscenes are LITERALLY DEAFENING. Second, when I tried rebinding controls for attacking, none of the custom bindings worked except for light attacks. But that one button still worked even when I reset the keys to default. Great start.
The level design, even for being pretty much completely linear, is not great. There are practically ZERO jumps you can clear without double jumping, even though it looks like you really SHOULD. At this point, you might as well make the level a completely flat line. Not to mention shorter, the first level dragged on for far too long, for how unengaging it was.
But the worst part is the most important one. The combat. Fighting does NOT feel good in this game. The game tries to present itself as a cool character action game, but the combos are lackluster even after a few level-ups (which were clearly just thrown in there for the heck of it), and pressing buttons just isn't responsive. Not to mention the boring, ineffective enemy design. The basic enemies don't telegraph their attacks as clearly as they should, and you don't have nearly good enough ways to respond to them, which causes the fights to devolve into primitive, boring brawls, and the first boss is an exercise in bad design - the launched rockets come down seemingly at random, and the ground pound/line attack is just like all of the ledges in this game: it looks like you should be able to clear them without having to double jump, but you can't.

Astroneer is a pretty good alpha demo, which is good because at the time of this writing, the creators plaster on the main menu and onwards that it is a pre-alpha game.
It's a third person exploration/crafting/survival-lite game, similar in scope to Minecraft (random world generation, ability to switch between multiple different worlds, structure crafting, etc)
Right now it's fairly decent for about 4-8 hours of play. Past that, there's not a ton of depth yet, and no storyline, no quests, no real direction or end-state. You can die, but you just respawn at your nearest oxygen-generation point on the planet. I do like the visual representation of everything, and how modular everything is, that's very cool, but it definitely needs a good bit of not only direction and story, but also optimization. If you have a less than optimal PC, I wouldn't bother with this anytime soon.
Check back in about a year and a half or so.

Right off the bat, Sonic Adventure is a very selective game, not everyone can get behind it and enjoy. The graphics were great for the time but are showing some age. Plus the models are even more shiny than the Gamecube port. The biggest downside however is the ugly purple border around the game, sure there are unofficial patches to fix this but I shouldn't have to resort to 3rd party sofrware to fix problems, they should exist to enhance the experience. The music is still very good and holds up today. It has a lot more variety than Adventure 2's soundtrack, causing more catchy tunes. The voice actors do decent for the 90s and their voices fit perfectly. (With some possible exceptions of Eggman and Tails) The way the voice acting is handled is pretty poor. It seems Sega wasn't fully aware how to do audio mixing and properly syncing mouth movements. Despite the cutscene animations being laughably bad, the writing I feel, is the best in the Sonic series. Just the right amount of cheesiness and seriousness. The gameplay is very good and entertaining, although it is not very well polished. This rerelease is the glitchiest iteration of this game and I wish a patch would be developed to fix several collision issues. Granted, they never got in the way or killed me, but it's incredibly jarring to go top speed and then suddenly stop. The level design again, I feel it's the best the 3D games have had. The levels have one linear (albeit open) path but several alternate routes along the way providing several goodies such as rings and lives. I feel that all the gameplay styles work well for what they are although Big's is really unnecesary and pointless. (Gameplay and story wise) Overall, to me Sonic Adventure is a gem and my personal favorite game. But it is fair to say, this game is flawed, hasn't aged perfectly, and isn't very accessible to non-Sonic fans. I reccommend it, but only if you are curious or are a Sonic fan who hasn't played it already.

Well....... Walking Simulator for sure.. at least at this level of production.
** As a side-note: Just to be clear... the moon isn't a planet, as of writing this review, but give that Congress of Interstellar.. blah blah blah, a few years and it might make the cut...
Anyways on with the review,

So I find myself outside my Lander Capsule which looked like an Apollo Re-entry Capsule rather than what would be feasible for landing on the Moon, so I am not surprised that she crashed on the moon.  Scotty warned us about pushing the engines so hard, and we just kept asking for more and more power.... well guess he's laughing from the other side of... "The Final Frontier".
Back to the scene... A lovely angelic voice explains that I have crashed miles away from my crew, that are equally scattered over the surface of the Moon aka "Planet" and I have little time to find them as I have an Oxygen tank that was not built for extended moon walks.  So personally, I actually will give some points as I liked the voice acting, though she doesn't explain how I crashed and why the sky is so chaotic so all in all she left me a bit "in the dark" (Moon Pun) as to what in the "Other-World" was going on...
Also apparently my HUD in my Visor showed me MANY MORE then 5 NAV points of my team so the voice said it must be damaged, which caused them all to show up with the yellow colored label UNKNOWN TARGET except!!!, for my "Crash Site in Blue, and the DANGER Symbols in Red for RADIATION (at least thats what I guessed as nothing ever says what it means) and an ALERT for the falling rocks, boulders, and small mountains that seemed to be directly targeting me and seemingly coming from EARTH...  ~Dramatic music plays~

Now I will say I actually liked the physics of the rocks as some would come in very fast and bounce back into space... Yes, it's true that on the moon these small asteroids wouldn't bounce like that and would crash and send both my avatar and the regolith (Moon's surface dust, and rocks) flying everywhere until we crashed back into the moon, or escaped the weak gravity of the Moon and headed into space, but overall it was cool to watch them come in and fly out, and some slower ones began to fill the landscape of the moon surface and seemed to be persistent so that was a nice touch... though alone cannot save the game.
Also the EARTH and the SUN are in full view on the Bright side of the MOON... seems a bit off but whatever...
I headed towards one of the UNKNOWN TARGETS.   I picked it cause it was the only one that seemed to be alone and was the 2nd closest to my crash site.  I walked about 2000ish Meters and moon walking is slow business.  Moon jumping was pretty cool at least the first 100 or so jumps then i spent time jury rigging my walk button to stay pressed while i took a nap.  BTW, when you are hit by rocks you take Oxygen damage.. What is that???  We built a shield system that depletes the same thing that we NEED to live!!!! HAHA Bad Engineers!!! BAD!!!  In fact, I lost 20% while the voice spoke to me before she told me about my limited Oxygen.  Sighhhh....
I walked for like 15 or so minutes and I get to within 700 meters and hit some magical bearer... I tried to walk around it for a few minutes, tried to jump over it, but I could not get past it.  It seemed as if Gandalf told me that I too "Shall Not Pass!" and this is when I plug pulled and removed my space helmet... no I actually didn't have a way to do that either, I just used Control+F4 and cried for GASP!
Nice Graphics, and neat (if not realistic) Physics cannot make up for lack of plot, and game-wrecking bugs... GASP is not recommended.

I played this game when it came out and I remember waiting for it like child for christmas (no pun intended).
To this day I'm still playing this game, it just manages to capture the best Batman atmosphere you won't find in any of the other Batman Arkham games from Rocksteady.
THE CITY (FREE ROAM)
- The city is somewhat gothic and you'll immediatly feel like you're in Gotham City. It feels like a city and not too Sci Fi like Arkham City and Arkham Knight. When you walk into an ally and notice all the small details like idling cars, newspapers and everything, it just feels like the Batman universe. Great enviroment.
COMBAT
- The combat is great but obviously don't give you as many moves as Arkham Knight has. But what I really like about the combat in this game, is that you mostly use realistic fighting moves that you can actually visualize Batman using in a real scenario, instead of throwing a thug across the road, like in the other games.
BOSS-FIGHTS
- All I can say is the boss fights are great, no boss battle feels the same. There's really nothing to complain about and you'll understand when you play or have played the game.
VOICE ACTING
- Great voice acting, great talent is brought to the game without having the original voice actors in the game. A lot of emotion is shown in every character. Roger Craig Smith and Troy Baker just did an amazing job, considering the expentations they had to live up to.
CONCLUSION
- I could list a more things about the game that I really like, but I wanna keep it somewhat short.
As far as consequences it doesn't really have any except from the few bugs and glitches you can run into from time to time, but every game has these so...
Game is awesome and I really want to see yet another Batman game made by WB Games Montreal in the future. I really think they manage to create a great Batman experience that makes you feel like you're The Dark Knight serving justice.

The reasons I recommend this game:
This game is literally one of the most interesting and most fun games I have played in a long time. I’m so excited about this game and where it can go in the future. I will probably even buy it for Xbox One just to be able to play it on both platforms. I think this is one of my favorite games of all time. If you get lost, you can use the Astroneer wiki or YouTube to find out more info and what to do. You can do everything you could want in space exploration. You can harvest, research, build, create, explore, and even blast into space to go to different places on your planet or even to another planet. This game is well worth the price and well worth your time. Once you figure out what to do and how things work, you will get hooked on this space exploration. If surviving and exploring on your one isn’t enough, there is even multiplayer! You can work with up to 3 other friends to survive in this amazing universe.
The state of the game:
As with any early access games there will be bugs. I realize there are ALWAYS people reviewing early access games and complaining about the bugs. I know there have been some games that were so bad they are essentially unplayable. I get being mad about that. If you expect NO bugs, don’t get an early access game. There are bugs but nothing unforgivable. I have found that sometimes exiting the game and coming back can fix the bug or issue. When you exit the game to the menu or desktop, you save the game. So, if you’re in the middle of a planet and you lose your goodies, don’t exit! Go to your desktop or ctrl+alt+delet and close the program externally. You will start the game at the last save that way. If you do loose it all, don’t worry because you can get it all again in this expansive game.
Bottom line:
If you want an amazing game with incredibly fun elements and mechanics and aren’t afraid of some normal early access bugs, buy it today! If you’re looking for a finished game with no bugs that is also amazing, buy it on full release. If you buy it now or later, you will love this game. I would recommend not waiting since it’s the kind of game you want to play as soon as possible. The devs are great and are working to update the game regularly. I don’t see this becoming an abandoned Steam game like so many others. I also see this game becoming better and most likely adding content and stuff to do over time. Not a bad investment for my money personally. If you’re still unsure, watch some YouTube let’s plays and get a feel for the game. Thanks for reading and bye!

I was suprised by how fun this game is, building, researching, exploring and modifying your environment (terrain) is primarly what this game is all about at this point. The colorful landscapes are fantastic, and unique while the storms are great to look at and experiance.  The sky is out of this world.  Excellent foundation to build a very interesting game on.  Base building is simple, interesting but somewhat linear (you just place finished objects which you are able to build right away or through research).  I have not experianced a frame drop while playing the game for a few hours but a friend did experiance a considerable frame drop.
Considering the game is in early stages of development, my suggestions for imrovements are:
1. more indepth base building (e.g., being able to build complex structures to live in, make a single planet a more permanent home while being able to build ships for e.g., gathering resources on other planets, or setup secondary bases in case your main one gets wiped out by a disaster)
2. more relaistic life experiance (e.g., what about food, what about dehydration, what about bathroom breaks, what about radiation, what about more dramatic temperature changes, etc.)
3. the game becomes boring after several hours of playing, as the environment becomes predictable, the base building is limited to a small number of pre-designed structures, etc.)
4. enemies would expand the game considerably (e.g., giant worms in tunnels which appear and move rapidly, powerful storms which can damage/destroy structures, meteorite strikes which form powerful aftershocks and deposits thick layers of sediment over your base, tectonic movements which can modify the terrain considerably forming huge ridges, mountains or canyons, poisonous gas vents which can become active, aliens, etc.)

This one was hard. You see, tons of people call this the best Sonic game ever. But the truth is, it hasn't aged very well.
Trust me when I say I'm a Sonic fan (I own more Sonic games then my Steam Profile suggests) and I have to say that everything about this game is good, but old. Firstly, I'll talk about the things I didn't like. The cutscenes were so choppy and filled with atrocious voice acting (c'mon, the Dreamcast was more advanced than what they showed). Some playable character's stories were not very fun and shortened to make people want to play the Sonic storyline.
Now for the things that worked. Running around and controlling Sonic is very fun and easy to learn. It feels fluid and fast, the way Sonic should be. The level design was very interesting, having parts that really showed off the power of the Dreamcast at the time, but now just serve as a good way to break up the gameplay. There's also a great variety of levels, with their own gimicks to keep you coming back time after time. Finally, though not much, the story in each character story line connects, really giving you the impression that this really is an adventure that you are on.
Overall, even with its shortcomings, I still recommend this game to any fan of platformers or Sonic games in general. It will give you many hours of fast-paced fun.

Prison Architect: Riot Simulator
In this game, your goal is to make a working, non-deadly, friendly, money profit prisons. Of course, if you are like me, you'll make a non-working, death house, agressive, deficit prison where everyone is shanked to death.
Don't get this wrong, the game is still loads of fun! It's sort of a Tycoon like game. You start with a small prison you built, and slowly grow it up to take more and more inmates, keep the order, make it functional so no one gets angry, manage your staff and guards tiredness, patroll routes, and make sure no one escapes via a underground tunnel.
I get a kick by making a big complex, filled with 200-300+ prisioners, and seeing it "work". Though there are deaths, I have fun trying to fix it to not have inmates die. Though there are riots, I have fun pacifying the rioting inmates. Though they manage to escape, I enjoy knowing I had a sniper tower that shot to kill one inmate, and the other 3-4 inmates quickly gave up after trying to escape, sending the whole prison to lockdown and a whole prison search for items.
The game is just fun for being chaotic. Plus, you can always try to escape your own prison! Normaly that just envolves a lot of blood and death, sending the prison to a riot as you escape.

Where do i even start to tell you how great this game is. There is nothing more satisfying locking down your prison and watching the chaos unfold, Then to send in a swat team to kill them all. Or finding the Snitches and sending them to Max to see how long they can live for. Yes i think im a bad warden, but thats what makes this game so great, you can run it just how you like. would recommend this game to anyone.

Batman here comes off as more stubborn, aggressive, filled with rage, determined to bring his enemies to justice at all cost. Batman: Arkham Origins is a good game, and, while it has its faults, is a decent entry in the Batman: Arkham franchise. However, it does have its faults, as I stated earlier. The game can be glitchy (for some not even working), but I have not yet come into contact with many, other than a little bit of lag occasionally. The gameplay is good, but not as strong as in its predecessors or in Batman: Arkham Knight, although this could be done purposefully to show Batman's inexperience, as this is only two years into his crimefighting career and he has yet to become the hardened vigilante seen in Rocksteady's games. The story is well-written, but also slow in some parts, and has a major problem that the Most Wanted missions suffer from as well, but I'll get to that later. The voice acting is fantastic, and the dialogue is very well-written. The graphics are decent, but not up to par with its predecessors. The twists and turns in the story, despite how some feel about the main twist in the Gotham Merchant's Bank, I enjoyed, and it has plenty of build-up, even if most people don't notice it. There are even a few heart-wrenching scenes, as well as some very intense and exciting moments. Now, it's time to discuss this game's biggest problem, and it's a problem that has plagued all of the Batman: Arkham Games, even before this game came out, as Batman: Arkham City had a few: Continuity Errors. This section will inlude spoilers, so stop reading now if you haven't palyed or watched the game to its completion. There are dozens of continuity errors in this game, and I'll list many of them for you now: Qunicy Sharp, in the credits of the game and during an audio file, is said to have a plan to reopen Arkham Asylum (orchestrated by Shiva's "Master", Rā's al Ghūl to set-up the events of Batman: Arkham Asylum and Batman: Arkham City, and, unintentionally, Batman: Arkham Knight), yet in Batman: Arkham Asylum Character Bio for Warden Sharp, it says he has been warden for three years, yet Frank Boles had been a guard for eight years, meaning it couldn't have been Quincy who reopened the asylum; Aaron Cash's family photo from Batman: Arkham City is shown, despite him in Batman: Arkham Knight saying that he wasn't a cop yet during the time of the Blackgate Riots, and his family shown should be different, as his baby daughter shouldn't be born yet, as she wasn't present in Batman: Arkham Asylum's photo, and his son should be several years younger, if he was even born yet; Bane does his famous backbreaker onto Batman, and Batman's spine is not broken, despite Bane later doing it breaking Batman's back; Harleen Quinzel meets the Joker at Blackgate, despite them being described as meeting at Arkham Asylum in Rocksteady's games; photos of Killer Croc from Batman: Arkham Asylum and City are featured, despite him not yet looking like he does in those games; the "Identity Thief" newspaper articles from Batman: Arkham City are featured, despite Thomas Elliot not becoming the Identity Thief until six months before Batman: Arkham City; Deadshot fighting Batman, despite Alfred making it seem as if Deadshot has never fought Batman in Batman: Arkham City; Deathstroke appearing in this outfit in both this game and Batman: Arkham Knight, despite appearing in his The New Teen Titans: The Judas Contract outfit in Batman: Arkham City Lockdown; etc. However, despite these problems, I still recommend the game, and give it a 7.5/10.

I put off getting this game for a year because of some bad reviews saying it had input lag and crashed a lot. It was on sale for 60% off today and decided to see if any of this was true. Well I was glad to find out that it wasn't true. Maybe the developers have updated it since the last few discussion board threads and negative reviews because this game plays smoothly for me. No audio problems, no crashes, and definitely no input lag. Unless people are talking about the "lag" between heavy attacks, in which case, that just means you can't buffer your attacks, rather you have to time your button presses.
I absolutely love this game! The animation style is incredible, Dusty's voice is awesome, and being able to level up the combo system keeps the game fresh and interesting. I would have preferred the cutscenes to have real time dialogue and sound fx instead of just Dusty narrating everything, especially since the story is a decent revenge one.
However, that doesn't hamper on my experience too much as I am in love with the game's fighting mechanics. It would have been nice if the pace was quicker, especially since you're controlling animal characters it would have made more sense--but the graduated combo system and the support allies make this a fun and fresh beat 'em up!

The addition of guns also changes the encounter design greatly due to the fast moving projectiles.  Unfortunately they are nearly undodgeable driving the player to avoid engaging with them at all, favoring closing the distance and mashing the win button instead.

Adorable slime farming simulator. You, the rancher, are granted a domain over rpg's infamous starting monsters. These little slimeballs are eccentric and with your sucking contraption device you can ensnare them into your inventory. Take them to your base where shoving them into corrals can help ease your lusting for plort. Poop crystals are the byproduct of a well fed slime, and will turn a pretty profit.
As a beta, this game has captivated me to explore the world of Slime Rancher. I want more. Nay, I need more! As it is now, there are several different types of slime to manage and feed. Including the elusive golden slime, which if you manage to feed will drop a solid gold poop crystal. Instead of slaughtering the poor slimes in any other game, this one lets you capture the little cuties for the fun of harvesting their poop.
I recommend this game not for the current implemented content, but for the concept and promise of much more to come. After a few hours, I have completed most of what the game has at the moment.  On the horizon, however, holds many more species of poop machines ready to be captured. May the Plort be with you, young Slime Ranchers!

No. No. Absolutely awful. I'm sorry, but who thought that combining a precision game with loose as heck flight controls was ever a good idea? I've tried to tolerate this one, I really have. But the introduction of the windmill mechanic (which looks really cool in the trailer, sure) just completely broke me. All atomiks up until that level, and then more deaths on that level than any level prior. Yeah, no. Good riddance, to be honest. This game takes its simple concept and does seemingly everything wrong with it. There's zero satisfaction to be had in completing a level because it feels more like chance than anything. You can't recreate the same plays over and over because of how imprecise the controls are. And the game somehow expects you to be precise regardless? It feels less like gaining any skill and more just memorizing things until you eventually maybe win. And honestly my patience has completely run out.
Also, the soundtrack is obnoxious. More precision games need to take cues from Dustforce and have quiet, relaxing soundtracks instead of blaring noisefests that only make frustration worse. Also, having the shooting sound so loud is... very much not a good idea, it's awful. Game looks okay I guess. Story is... ehh. Kind of there, kind of not. I really can't recommend this game though, it takes everything about precision games and does them as wrong as possible, at least in my opinion.

Now, there are two things to be reviewed:
1°- The game itself
2°- The port (yes, it deserves to be mentioned)
Let's start with the game. Now, Sonic Adventure was released in 1999 for the Dreamcast and, in 2004, it got a remake for the GameCube and PC, entitled Sonic Adventure DX: Director's Cut, the game this port claims to be. At the time, this game was great, with great soundtrack, great level design, great visuals (well, the DX version at least), great gameplay and an all-around great fun. Nowadys, this game is still great, though unfortunally a bit dated. The fact that this game is dated doesn't bother me in the slightest, as this game is very nostalgic for me and I really wanted to replay this, even knowing that it was dated, but the fact that this game is dated may affect some newcomers, as they might be bothered by this game's faults. That's not to say this game is bad nowadays, no, far from that, it's still a great game, though it's now easier to see this game's faults.
Now, to the port. I just have one thing to say about this port, and it is WOW! Just...just wow. To me, it's just incredible the fact that they menaged to do such a port... It's terrible. Why you might ask? Batman: Arkham Origins is a huge problem for me, because I want to finish it, but I'm terrible at it. I have no sense of rhythm, I have terrible reflexes, and I'm terrible at spatial awareness. It wasn't quite so bad in Arkham Asylum, but Arkham Origins is farther down the series.
Nevertheless, Arkham Origins is the ignored middle child of the Arkham series. I remember that it got a lot of flack when it came out, was more-or-less panned when compared with the games that came before, and then forgotten when Arkham Knight came out with its many, many controversies. Which is a shame, because on its own, Arkham Origins is pretty good.
I played the hell out of Arkham Asylum, but I skipped Arkham City. I don't like Zasz (I think they should kill him, ignore him utterly, and slap whomever decided that Zasz has a place in the Batman Universe), I didn't like the story, and I didn't like the ridiculous number of Riddler trophies you're supposed to find in it. I did not want to play it. Arkham Origins seemed to be a better compromise over all of the Arkham games.
Arkham Origins is (as the name suggests) a prequel to the Arkham Universe. It's near the beginning of Batman's crusade in Gotham City, so there's no Oracle, Jim Gordan isn't the friendly commissioner, and there aren't any super-criminals. Cobblepot is a gangster, as is Roman Sionis. There is a Riddler (though he's going by Enigma), but he works the same way, but without the serial killer vibes from Arkham City. They didn't get Kevin Conroy for Batman, but the substitute guy is pretty good (though harsher). Some people have criticized the game for not having that good a story, but I thought that it was pretty good.
The gameplay is definitely very similar to Arkham City, though... refined. Riddler Informers return, but now cannot be knocked out during combat (which is wonderful). There are far fewer Riddler trophies (called Enigma datapacks, as they're now part of blackmail information being collected by Enigma), but there is now a "Dark Knight" system which has levels for combat disciplines, for predator disciplines, for exploration, and for unlocking information. Side missions are called "Case Files". There is a bit of CSI-style sleuthing (using the Detective Mode), that I wish they did more with. You can return to the Batcave for training missions and for combat (and predator) challenges. There is a good amount to do.
The city is big-ish. There are sections which were in Arkham City. You get to enter some of the buildings as part of missions. But the city's empty of people, the only ones on the streets are criminals, or corrupt policemen. You won't get anyone in the cross-fire, but it still feels odd when you stop to think about it.
There are bugs. Or rather, there are still bugs, even though the game is now several years old. Nothing game-breaking, but jarring. Batman will occasionally not glide properly, but flap around like a fruitbat. I once kicked an Enigma informer into the firmament, and the game got stuck. The audio cut out a couple of times in the quick-travel FMV (not that I really cared). The game could've done with some polish.
The game does have some wonderful fights. The plot essentially is that the Black Mask (Roman Sionis) has put out a hit on Batman, hired several big-name assassins to take him out. In the process, Batman also needs to figure out why Roman is acting so out-of-character. As you go through the campaign, you will happen across different assassins (Lady Shiva, Deathstroke and others) and fight them. And those fights are glorious.
I just wish I were better at them.
I got Batman Arkham Origins on sale (and those come along fairly regularly). At the sorts of prices that they're giving this away on, I don't see why this shouldn't be part of every collection.

From the outside, Borderlands 2 looks like it is just your regular FPS game, and in some way it is true, but you'll be doing this game an injustice if you only thought that far.
As a FPS game goes, it's one of the best FPS games I've ever played, and that is saying a lot.
There are many reasons why I praise it, so let's begin.
The graphics are some of the most unique I've seen in a game. Whilst most FPS games try to go for realism, Borderlands 2 can't give a damn about that. Show me screenshots of al the popular FPS games right now, and Borderlands 2 will stick out like a sore thumb. This game has an identity.
The sound design is on point. Weapons made by Jakobs have a very mechanical sound, due to them being very old-school, mechanical weapons. The same can't be said for makes like Hyperion and Maliwan, which are very futuristic and differ greatly in every aspect.
The enemies are amazing in this game. Their taunts and fighting styles are very varied and unique, and sometimes I don’t kill them immediately, just so I can hear what they are going to say next. On the higher levels they can be very challenging too, so you always have to push yourself to stay ahead of the game. Challenging, but just as rewarding.
The soundtrack, oh my GOD the soundtrack! It’s awesome! Each area has such a unique atmosphere and the music simply amplifies that by a factor of 100. If I listen to each song, I know exactly where it is played. It’s one of those soundtracks that you can listen to completely on its own, and it will still be awesome.
The leveling system is very robust and adaptable. Even though you have four playable characters in the vanilla game, the amount of options you can chose from when leveling up can lead to one character having different play styles on their own, essentially increasing the amount of different ways you can play.
The story is satisfactory, but little else. It’s not horrible or the most complex, but it does get you involved and caring for each character. Job done.
In conclusion, I highly recommend you buy this game and KILL JACK!

If I could think of any phrase that would sum up my 47 minutes worth of experience with GASP, it would be Steve Carrell's insightful quote from The Office...
"No, God, please no! No! NOOOOOOOOO!"
GASP is an indie game that simulates the horrors of being stranded on the moon with low oxygen, leaving you a limited amount of time to call for help. However, I believe GASP has one true fatal flaw that buries this great idea deep under the earth's crust. Yes, a few ideas here and there hinder the experience, but I believe this one flaw is the greatest, especially for the gameplay.
In a word, the biggest flaw in GASP is: EVERYTHING!
This is one of the slowest, most horribly boring games I've played in... well, ever. Hell, I've hated my fair share on putrid games like Kane and Lynch 2 and Manhunter but at least those had just a little something in them to make them... memorable. Or have something of value in them!
The game simply sets you on the moon with five destination markers. It's your choice which one to go to, but you have to act quick or your health will give out. And as it says everytime you start a game "If you die... you die." Although, I never died once in GASP. All three times I played I ended up shutting off the game because I thought something was wrong with the game I was playing in particular, but... no. The whole game is just wrong.
First off, the moon is just... dull. It's all grey with shadows here and there with nothing interesting about it or anything imposing that would really set a feeling of dread or tension. Besides that, you move so slow and clunky that it wouldn't matter.
God, the movement is even worse! You can turn just fine, but you really FEEL each godd*** step this astronaut takes, because the camera bobs to the right and left with each agonizingly long step. Each radio is a fair distance away... and with how long it takes, it took me 10 minutes to get to the closest radio. Yeah. Ten minutes. It was nearly twenty to get to the other one.
Now, ten to twenty minutes of awkwardly walking across the moon wouldn't be nearly as bad if there was actually some challenge to it. Fortunately, besides the ticking clock of your oxygen running low, there are also meteorites falling from space with enough speed to hit you and injure you... even though the moon doesn't have enough gravity to attract satellites and give them enough speed. Whenever you jump, you fall slower than the rocks. That makes no sense!
Even THEN, you can still just sidestep and avoid the meteors entirely (though your HUD will constantly annoy you by reminding you that there is, still, a meteor falling nearby). But I learned a very interesting trick to remove all possible challenge in GASP. Ready for it? I'm only gonna say it once. Here it goes.
Just stare at the meteros. That's it.
I just stared at a meteor while it fell near me, and when it got too close... it disappeared. Seriously. I'm dead f***ing serious. I thought it was just a one-time fluke, so I kept staring at the meteors as they fell... and every single one just vanished.
This game is worse than AIDs!
There are a host of glitches in this game that I didn't even mention. One of them during my third playthough significantly slowed my movement down, as if I was pushing an invisible wall, while I was close to the radio.
This game is a dull, horrible designed mess. Whoever made GASP should honestly feel ashamed for how little effort they put into this to make it somewhat fun. It controls horribly, it's filled with glitches, the sounds are just of your breathing and a low humming soundtrack on repeat, and the world is completely uninteresting. This is easily a contender for one of my least favorite games ever. I'm giving GASP a 1/10.
You'll be gasping to get out of this game, when you start it up!

is a major improvement over its predecessor in nearly every way, combining strategic and tactical hauling choices, crew and company management, and satisfying driving into a fantastic package.
+The driving systems, the subtle differences between different trucks, and the learning curve are executed flawlessly. While the original felt stiff, this game gives you the tools to push the limits of your truck as far as you dare. While there is not a robust physics engine (you won't be jumping ramps or getting into huge crashes), the primary focus is on the drive and getting it right. Combining this with plenty of customization options, for performance or just looks, will ensure you are riding comfy. *Note, I am using a 360 controller.
+The different locations throughout Europe feel varied and open.
+The fleet management system is top notch. Hiring drivers and upgrading their individual trucks based on the skills they have is a treat. The bank loan aspect combined with garage expansion makes you feel like you are expanding your empire ever further outward while still allowing you to focus on the driving. It's not a distraction but rather an overall enhancement to the experience; you could also ignore it more or less entirely if it doesn’t interest you.
+Great mod support and active community.
+While I haven’t gotten them yet myself, many of the DLC packs seem to add large swaths of playable area to the game and look to be a good value for the amount of content.
-The game is a few years old and some of the graphics are getting a bit dated. It's not a bad looking game but it wasn't exactly super pretty to start with.
-Some of the road signs are misleading. Speed limits won’t match what your GPS says, highway signs indicate an exit is coming up but sometimes won’t tell you it’s an exit only lane, etc. It looks like modders have made a few patches to help with those issues however.
=Many of the stations are copy/pastes of buildings from other cities. A little more variety would have been nice, but industrial buildings tend to look the same in real life so just a little nit-pick.
=Some of the achievements seem suuuuper grindy, but then again, this is designed to be a game to be played over a long time.
=Controller use in menus is just a mouse emulator. If you’re using a controller it’s probably best to go to K+M when you are handling the fleet management parts.

I wish I could recommend this game, as it has some nice things going for it, but this game simply is not polished enough. I am yet to play this game for more than 15 mins without it crashing or glitching. Every now and then the enemies will just turn into white pixels, which can be a completely jarring experience. The combo system is intriguing as it allows you to air juggle, along with incorporate a number of different weapons in combat. However using the assist character isn't a fine tuned enough feature to use outside of the brief puzzle/platforming parts. I judge early access games on two things:
1. Is it worth the asking price at this time?
2. How much potential does it have?
Though it falls a tad short on 1, it has enough potential to more than cover the asking price.
I wont bother to re-explain the game, there are PLENTLY of lets-play videos of slime rancher out there to more than satisfy those needs. And I would highly recommend looking into a few, because this is a game thats not for everyone.
At the moment, it feels like a finished product in all aspects but content. Everything feels polished and smooth. Objects respond the way you'd imagine them to, I ran into very few bugs and the ones I did were very endearing (3 largos spinning infinitly around a single carrot is always hilarious). And I suffered no fatal errors that were fault of the game (my computer shut down during the middle of gameplay and corrupted the save file, but thats to be expected).
However, as mentioned by many others, it lacks heavily on content. Just going through the game at a nice slow pace and messing around with whatever struck my fancy, it took me about 5 hours before I was just making so much gold income that the game lost its meaning for me and I had already done all the cute things I had wanted to do. And it only takes you about 3 minutes to run from one edge of the map to the other, if that.
The cuteness and friendly atmosphere of the game cannot be denied, and the Tars are always a challenge in large numbers. I always get a huge smile just watching the little buggers be slimes, and I'm considering starting a free range ranch to just see more of it instead of locking them in the prisons of corals.
If your looking for a game to look at adorable things and have a good, fun time, you might consider getting this game. But if your on the fence about it, or if your a speedrun completionist kind of person, perhaps wait for a update or two and check back in.
TLDR:
Is it enough at this time to justify the price tag?
A: Barely. Watch a lets play first and see if its right for you.
Does the potential justify the price tag?
A: Definitely. I'm already very stoked for the next update adding a whole new slime type and area, and by their dev-map it seems it looks about 1 new area/slime per update, with quite a few more content updates to come.

I was bored. Read the terrible reviews of this game. Saw that it was free and only 900MB and I get download speeds on steam of around 7MB/s. Figured I'd try it anyway, since the only thing I had to lose was time I was otherwise wasting on being bored. Everything everyone is saying about this game is true. The chick that comes over comms in the trailer is the only voice you get to hear through the entire game. And that's all she says before she leaves you on your own. What you hear in the trailer is literally the entire game's dialogue. Now, if you want to make a little simulator about walking across the lunar surface in a space suit to try and link up with lost team members before you run out of oxygen, that's fine. But what is with these friggin' meteors? Every half a second you are being accosted by a new meteor that is headed straight for you by some miracle of science and physics. They are the size of a small car. And then one hits you, yes, you take a direct hit from a meteor the size of a small car, and the results are... underwhelming... You know how when in real life a meteor of even a small size is moving at such a tremendous speed that it's like a little nuke going off on impact, with a big, dramatic boom and shake and smoldering impact crater? None of that happens here. You get hit by one of these meteors and your screen goes red for a few seconds almost like the astronaut you are playing as is just going "Ow... ow... ow...". These meteors impact both you and the ground around you ceaslessly and instead of doing anything cool when they hit the ground, they simply bounce around like rubber balls and make no impact on the lunar surface which is for some reason marred with craters from meteors just like this impacting into it for billions of years, though the frequency with which these meteors are impacting has never been seen in reality since the likes of the violent creation of our solar system eons ago. Seriously, stop with the meteors. They are a silly gimmick that actually subtracts from what barely noticeable subtance this game already has. I actually felt a bit offended to see that they wanted to charge me $2.99 to do the same thing on Mars instead of Luna. Do they really expect anyone to buy that? What's worse, has anyone actually bought it? Seriously, don't mess with this game unless you're just in one of those "Got nothing better to do" situations like I was.

I got this in a HB for a dollar (along with two other games), so it's hard to complain.
But, for the full price of $30?  Not worth it by a long shot.
The gameplay is fairly straight forward and simple.
It's a standard action platformer, with the added bonus of "buying" power ups at various points in the game.
Nothing really exciting beyond the standard "use attack type A to beat this enemy, weapon B to defeat that enemy".
Character controls are fairly responsive and smooth.
Camera controls, on the other hand, have much to be desired.
The game insists on you focusing in one particular direction, and it offers stiff resistance to you trying to look around, rubberbanding the viewpoint back to the game's pre-designated focus point.
But the biggest problem with the game is the frequency of the cutscenes... and they're quite long.
In fact, I think I've spent more time watching a cutscene than actually controlling my character.
This game maybe fun to play, but it's not particularly fun to watch.
And the script is atrocious.
It takes itself too seriously, trying too hard to be edgy.
This isn't Dante from the Devil May Cry series.
It's some emo goth kid trying to act like a punk rocker.
It's just painful to watch.
Once again, I can't really complain about the game for the price I got.
But it's not something I'd pay a full price... or even $5 for.
There are simply better alternatives out there.
While the new Dante will never be as cool as the original, the gameplay, music, and environments make it worth it.

I have played the games in release order (Asylum, City, Origins), so this review is based on the game itself and in comparison with the previous entries.
Pros:
- You're the goddamn Batman.
- (DLC only) You can play as Bruce Wayne (whose concentration mode feels weird, but probably necessary) when he was training. You can even play as Bruce Wayne in suit, in "Cold, Cold Heart".
- (DLC only) You can play as Deathstroke (without sword and guns, but still great) (better than Nightwing, Robin and Catwoman from previous games, in my opinion).
- Combat still rocks. Can't say much more. New enemies (Martial artists, venom fighters.), a new gadget dedicated to fighting (Electric gloves). A lot of people say combat's broken since previous games, I fully disagree. It is a bit harder than in Arkham City since enemies tend to be more agressive, particularly during a beatdown, and they can strike from farther than before, but that's mostly fair.
- Stealth still rocks. A lots of new gadgets (Glue bomb, basically a reskin of the Ice grenade from AC. Remote claw, to attach enemies to each other/gargoyles/whatever. Concussion thing which is useless.). Predator maps feel smaller than in Arkham City though.
- Story is great. Arkham City suffered from its size and didn't really succeed in the urgency feeling it wanted, while in Origins, the plot is more simple and straightforward, and works great. (No spoiler)
- ("Cold, Cold Heart" DLC only) The DLC story, while predictable to old Batman fans', is excellent.
- ("Cold, Cold Heart" DLC only) The XE suit in the DLC is probably the best ever seen in the series. "Heat" gadgets are nice too.
- Boss fights really stand out. So far in the series (Haven't played Arkham Knight a lot yet), besides the Freeze bossfight in Arkham City which is the best ever, some of the best boss fights are in Origins. The fight against Deathstroke is a masterpiece on New Game + (or I am the Night) with no counter indication, Copperhead is a nice challenge too, and Bane is finally what he should have been on previous games.
- Bane is finally properly represented, and the end game kinda explains why he "sucks" in Asylum and City.
- The open world is huge, about twice as big as the map in Arkham City, which is fully present in the game. Gotham City covered with ice is really impressive ("Cold, Cold Heart" DLC)
- The goddamn Batcave.
- There's snow everywhere, Batman and enemies leave footprints, that's useless but that's cool.
- A huge lot of additional contents (Suits, artworks, etc).
- Interesting challenges to do in story mode.
- More than a thousand medals to gain in challenge mode.
- A lot of details and backstory for people well-versed in Batman and DC Comics lore.
- New game +.
- "I am the night" gamemode, for added difficulty (Playing the whole game in new game + difficulty, with only ONE life).
- Music is great. Better than Arkham City in my opinion (I don't remember Asylum music).
Cons:
- Combat is not "fair" sometimes: this did not happen in previous games, but if there are a lot of enemies at once, you may be attacked from behind, which means the camera won't show the attacker. It ONLY happens if you have already been punched in the fight. Only way to be sure it doesn't happen is, well, fighting perfectly.
- Electric gloves are way overpowered. Once they're activated, there's no more strategy in fights. Armored enemies, stun baton enemies, martial artists, shielded enemies, enforcers.. Just punch, punch, punch, no need to think.
- Armored enemies used to be in red, in Arkham City, so you could notice them. Now, they're in grey, while most of the enemies are between black and beige. Very often, you won't notice them until you punched them by mistake (thus losing your combo).
- Stealth is cool, but the remote claw is way overpowered. You basically get three free takedowns with absolutely no chance to be spotted, and it can go up to five or six on most maps. It's way too much.
- Concussion detonator or something is useless. More often than not, using it will backfire, since it causes enemies to strike blindly and randomly, thus the camera will never show'em attacking.
- Detective crime scenes. Some people love them, but I don't, there's nothing to do besides looking for red hints.
- In challenge modes, giving medals for custom maps is a terrible idea. There's absolutely no difficulty, it just adds around ten hours doing easy/boring stuff if you really want to unlock everything. It's good for practice, but not for medal material.
- Story challenges are sometimes a pain in the butt, and if you don't do them early enough in the story, you'll have to finish'em in "I am the night" mode, which is difficult enough on its own.
- Unlike what I just said, "I am the night" is not difficult enough, for a simple reason. Despite having only one life, you can restart from last checkpoint anytime if you do it before your health reaches zero.
- In the open world, there are lots of places the batclaw could reach in Arkham City, for some reason here it can't.
- There are BUGS: (I played around 95 hours) I got stuck in the menu three or four times (The keys no longer responded), a couple times as well there were bugs during combat (Most of the time, a KO enemy still standing and walking around, who can't see you, but that you can't punch. If it happens on a challenge map, where the fight can't stop until all enemies are KO, you have to start over), it happened even once on a stealth map (An enemy I stole the weapon from fell from a ladder, which should have knocked him out, but for some reason he stood back up to catch his weapon, and he was a ghost, couldn't see me but couldn't be punched, thus predator map failed). I would say there's an annoying (Makes you restart the whole game) bug every 15 hours and a mildly-annoying (Makes you restart from last checkpoint, or the current challenge) bug every 4 hours.
Overall: If I had to pick a game between Origins and City, it would be City for the challenges, but Origins is excellent as well, and if City didn't exist, Origins would be seen as the great videogame it is.

Sonic Adventure is a game...... A game that is good. It is dated by a LOT, but I still love it. If you can look past the game's flaws, you can find something great here. If you're a hardcore Sonic fan, you probably own this on Dreamcast, Gamecube, and on Steam.

Sure, it's glitchy, it has a horrible camera, the plot and voice acting is a joke, and you have to go fishing to unlock the final boss, but Sonic Adventure is still a cool and really fun game. It's my favorite Sonic game, and considering that Sonic is my favorite game series, I guess this is my favorite video game, period. I'm not sure why I like it so much. It takes a little getting used to, but once you do, the simple objective of getting from point A to point B as fast as possible while smashing any robots that get in your way is surprisingly engaging.
The different characters give different takes on this core objective, and most of them are pretty fun (if not quite as fun as Sonic). The best would probably be Tails (beat Sonic or Eggman to point B), simply because he is so close to breaking the game that you can skip entire sections of the level without touching the ground if you're good enough. Gamma is pretty fun too, as the focus of his levels is essentially "blow crap up." Even Knuckles' treasure hunting levels aren't as much of a drag as they are in the sequel, and feature more opportunities for smashing robots (which you think should be a given; I mean, his name is Knuckles, for crying out loud). The only character whose gameplay is a flat-out failure is Big the Cat. In each level, he fishes for a frog. He doesn't run. He doesn't even smash robots. He just...fishes. It's stupid. But hey, at least his story mode is really short (as are most of the story modes, actually).
And even though the plot is dumb, it's dumb in such a way that it's also cool and fun, and you may even get more laughs out of it than the more recent games that try to be funny on purpose (with mixed results). Oh, and there are also virtual pets called "Chao" in the game, too. I don't know what to say about them. I never really cared about them enough to actually play that part. Some people like it.
Anyways, I'm not entirely sure why I like this game so much. I think it's the simplicity, the fast-paced energy, and the sense of "cool" it has, a combination that not too many games seem to have (not even other Sonic games, aside from the direct sequel to this one). Maybe nostalgia also has something to do with it. Whatever the case, I haven't really played a game like Sonic Adventure. It's not perfect, it may not be for everyone, but if a simple, energetic, and cool game sounds like something you'd like, regardless of a few faults, you might like to try this one.

Kind of like Minecraft, each new game is a new setting and a new solar system to explore. Some people complain that there isn't enough to do or find, but for me it's not about finding new things. For me, each time I play a new game I seem to learn a new, more efficient way of doing things. Each time I play, I get better, faster, and more efficient at building bases. I'm getting better at sculpting...and building bigger and better structures. I'm thankful I got in on this game at just $20. The devs have said they will evaluate the price of Astroneer as they add content, which is dev-speak for "This game will get more expensive as it grows." I like the style and intention of the game but ultimately I cannot recommend anyone go and play this game.
Basically outside of the "Boss Fights", it is your standard platformer. You can punch, fire grenades, andd occaisonally get a small little upgrade for a level thats lets you do things like jump higher or have you grenades leave a smoke trail in the air that lets you walk on it. But these upgrades are not around for very long which is unfortunate because they were kind of nice to have.
The boss fights are interesting and nostalgic but fairly simple and managed to go through the ones I got to fairly quickly.
But for a game with such simple controls it has a surprising challenge to it. There are these little pads that when your character is over them let you jump again. But the distance you get varies by how long you hold the button. I would normally like this but you can't really get an indication of if you did it long enough and most likely you insta die because you held it for to short.
Similarly I HATE the grenade launcher. So hard to tell whether or not it is charging up or not making it hard to hit the flying enemies leaving a really unsatisfying feeling.
The game is only hard because they made the controls awkward to use. I think the idea of playing the villan is cool, but the game just feels like a platformer with different style boss fights.
I tried playing it with a keyboard and with a controller and I absolutely thing a keyboard/mouse is better. Allows you to aim and gives more reliability to the direction of your punches and grenades.

I’ll start by stating that this game is truly addictive and captivating.
Why?
I believe many of those who have tried this game had realized that the combo system is pretty well thought out.
1) The number of variations it has is amazing - For each level your character gains, there would be roughly 3 moves to play around with.
2) It easy to pick up - a leveling system was cleverly put in place so that players get to master their current moves and think of ways to use them before leveling up.
The SUPPORT in this game isn’t anything like a cheap bomb clearing the entire screen of enemies. It allows an alternative way to play this game with clever obstacles that require you to use them.  Trust me, if you play hard you would definitely use them pretty often.
Boss Fight is a gem. Each of them requires a different set of way to defeat them and discovering how to do so is really rewarding.
The story is immersive and I really like the voice. It’s much better than the older trailers and without doubt, the art is amazing.
What can be improved?
Frame rate gets really unstable sometimes with steam overlay.
Minor bugs can be found here and there
Load screen gets stuck occasionally.
If you are a beat-them up lover you should really try this out.
#Also noted that it is their first release,  there are sure to be bugs around but I really like how responsive and active the developers are in dealing with them.
