I picked this up on a whim, and I've since been pretty pleased with what I found.
The first word that comes to mind about the game is "cute." Everything from the weird plants in the environment to the character's death animations essentially screams whimsy. It's like Alice in Wonderland, if Alice wore a giant backpack and ran out of air all the time. The terrain, character, and tools the character uses are all pleasantly chunky and soft-looking, like they're made out of Play-Doh.
The learning curve is extremely attainable. There are only a few controls besides the generic WASD-space and mouse. Q pulls out the backpack and puts it away. E pulls out the terrain tool and puts it away. Alt and Ctrl add and smooth terrain, repsectively. And Tab puts your character into whatever vehicle or dwelling he (she?) is near. SUPER easy. The tutorial is all of two minutes long.
There are no other NPCs available for you to interact with. I don't know if that's just a cop-out so the developer doesn't have to code an AI, but there it is.
As far as gameplay goes, it's pretty solid, but there isn't a whole lot to do yet. You can remove terrain, place terrain, and flatten terrain. You can mine materials, make stuff with them, and then use that stuff to mine different materials. Eventually, you can make a spaceship, go to a different planet, and do that stuff again.
The music is relaxing, which is nice, but there's nothing about it that makes me sit up and go "ooh." It reminds me of the music of Minecraft. Relaxed, floaty, kinda like wind chimes. Good to just have on, but not to sit and listen to.
So, at this point, the game doesn't have a whole lot for the player to do. Yes, it's pretty. Yes, it's cute. Yes, it's fun. But games are a kind of medium that tells a story, or has a goal. Even Minecraft has a "goal" now. Astroneer, thus far, does not.

I don't normally review games; in fact, this is my first ever game review.
That being said, I felt it necessary to talk about why I truly enjoyed this game, especially given what seems to be an outpouring of hate for something that is by no means a poor game.
There's a TL;DR at the bottom if you so choose.
So here's the deal:
Before two weeks ago, I had never touched an ARKHAM game. That style of game just wasn't really my style. But when I saw them on steam for 75% off, I bought all 4 games, DLC and all (roughly 36$ by the end).
I decided to play them in order, obviously, so I started with Asylum. A brilliant game, amazingly put together, awesome mechanics and story (save for the final boss fight, yadda yadda yadda complain complain complain).
I finished that one up to 85% (because homie don't play those challenge maps), but I got all the riddles and trophies and everything. Again, amazingly done.
Then I moved on to City. Also a really well done game, awesome story and side missions, incredible open world, and fantastic portrayal of Batman's enemies. I finished that one to roughly 55% because, again, homie don't play those challenge maps, and also because I haven't quite collected all the trophies just yet. I decided to wait on that so I could finish the stories of all four games.
And that brings us to Origins.
And to be honest, I loved it.
The story was fascinating, to say the least. Personally,
, but I won't complain about that because the twist was interesting (even if it was expected) and the plot was still awesome. The new voice actors did fantastic jobs, and personally I think the visual character design for both Batman/Bruce Wayne and the Joker are the best in Origins over any other ARKHAM game, Knight included. Sure, the game wasn't perfect and I had some bugs while I played, but it was sparse and didn't hinder my enjoyment of the game at all. Mechanics were as good as ever, even if it was nothing new, and the game was fluid and fun to play. I think my favorite part about the game (save the character designs for Batman and Joker, *so byutiful*), were the cinematic cutscenes, because they were truly cinematic, rather than more motion of the character models. It was beautiful and I loved it.
So in the end, despite all the hate for Arkham Origins, I still say it's a great game. Is it my favorite? I dunno, but it certainly isn't my least favorite.
TL;DR - don't listen to the hate about Origins until you play it yourself. It's a great Batman game.

I've played a lot of rhythm games: From Stepmania to Sound Voltex, from Crypt of the Necrodancer to Groove Coaster, from Taiko Drum to Voez.
Even in this early state of the game, you can feel the core experience they were going for. Taking cues from crypt of the necrodancer, Noisz involves tapping to the beat to perform actions. Like CotN, this forces you to make quick decisions on the fly (in this case, shield or hit). However, that's about where CotN ended being a rhythm game. This takes it one step further and creates bullet patterns that express the music.
There's a lot of potential here already, and in the few songs there are, even on easy modes, the potential is already being met.
While the art style is fairly clunky, the game lags a bit on my computer, and there's no visual indicator as to the beat that a lot of rhythm games have, what's there is still incredibly solid, and it really can only go up from here.
$15 may still be a bit steep at this stage, but there is plenty there for both hardcore rhythm gamers/shmuppers who can work on perfecting scores, to newbies who can slowly work their way up to getting better.

Sometimes you find a genre mashup that you never know you needed, Noisz fits that bill.
The core mechanic of the game is phenomenal, as you're dodging between red shots, you'll be absorbing the blue shots withan activatable shield and trying to maintain your combo -- all hectic but very enjoyable.
I'd gladly pay the price for Noisz now for the content included in the first build, looking very much forward to future content to be added and continue to work my way up the difficulty.

Sonic Adventure is a 3D Sonic game. Yup, a 3D Sonic game. They keep making these and they keep hitting the same issues.
Despite this being one of my favourite games on the Dreamcast back in the day, my opinion of game has been tarnished after a recent play through for the Backlog Blitz. Controls are horribly awkward and it feels like you're fighting against the camera angle most of the time. When you're not fighting against the camera angle, you're being sucked into walls or feel like your eyes are melting as the game's orientation warps, zooms and generally hates you throughout.
Gameplay wise you're probably looking at around 7 hours to 100% everyone's story mode, which isn't too bad. Probably even less if you know where you're going and what you're doing.
The game suffers from a slightly vague 'next objective' path - even though it tries to guide you with it's sutble ways.
The one saving grave this game has is the rather decent soundtrack, which I seem to remember being a real strong point throughout Sega games in the 90s.
Overall, I wouldn't recommend going out of the way to play this, but if you're a fan of the Dreamcast and are looking to relive 1999 all over again then this might be for you.
On the plus side the Chao Gardens are still in the game, so you can mess around with those guys for a little while... before you realise how creepy it is.
Can be buggy at times and hasn't aged the best, but if you like Sonic games then you're gonna love this.

Decent game plagued by some really dumb decisions. And no I don't just mean the butchering of the great characters from devil may cry. The game takes some of the best aspects of the DMC games, and just ruins them. The great combat is bogged down by being forced to use certain weapons. For anyone that hasn't played you have 4 weapons, angel, demon, rebellion, and guns. Guns are useless except against literally one enemy that dies in a few hits and is only there to give the guns have a reason to exist. Rebellion is your regular sword which has a good mix of power and speed. The angel weapons tend to be faster but weaker, but can build up power with numerous hits. The demon weapons are slow but powerful. This is pretty standard for DMC, and swapping between weapons was always one of the best parts. But like I said, this game ruins it by FORCING you to use weapons. Don't like the demon weapons? Too bad this enemy can only be hurt by them. Same with angel weapons. So the free combat where you can wail on enemies while switching between weapons is just ruined by these parts where you either use the weapons it tells you to, or die. And it only gets worse when they start mixing the enemies together since if you accidentally knick a red enemy with a blue weapon Dante gets staggered and your combo meter takes a hit, then another when you most likely get hit cause you're staggering. But luckily that's avoided by the lock on feature... oh wait they don't have that cause again they took everything good about the game and threw it away. The Devil trigger doesn't get much better treatment. It's still a huge power boost like in the original games, but now when activated it tosses enemies to the four corners of the earth so you'll be lucky if you have enough time to kill more than a single enemy. The game was a dollar on humble bundle, and yeah I'd say that's a fair price for it. From the characters to the gameplay they just destroyed everything that was good about the game, and what little new ideas that were interesting they still managed to make a headache. The idea of a demon world overlapping our own is great, traversing it is a nightmare of randomly moving platforms, jumps appearing out of thin air, and the camera deciding it wants to look at something else while you're trying to hook to a platform. If you can get it for less than 5 dollars it's worth it, otherwise go with the original series.

Good concept on paper, unrefined execution. Clunky, stiff controls (and not because of a sense of "realism", as though you had some real weight and a rhythm to your walking or running pace. Feels strangely dated and unpolished, despite being two years old. If it's realistic to not have a tooltip for the ammo type that you're pointing at, well... in the real world, you could pick up and READ THE BOX in front of your face, rather than at arm's length. You would also have an idea of how much spare ammo you were carrying; hiding the UI until you hold a button doesn't make the game more "realistic", it's a contrived way of limiting your available information. Could have been implemented another way; you could have to look down at your cargo pants and see how many boxes you have stuffed into your pockets, or visually inspect your revolver or clip to count ammo left. Anyway, I think I would have found this fun if I played it 7 or 8 years ago, but it's hard to hold this up against more modern, standalone titles with more sophistication, or the many other games jumping all over the zombie survival bandwagon.

I think this game is a good start for Starblade.  I think this game touches on some right ideas well but misses hard on others.
Pros:
Artstyle - very similar to those seen in many Wayforward games.  This is a good thing.  The background art sometimes is a bit lacking but overall is good.
Control - The controls are free-aim + sidescroll platforming.  They offer many simultaneous options to control the game.  You have the option to use trigger/bumpers only while using dual sticks or if you prefer face buttons you can use just the right stick to move/aim while always having the left stick available to you for precision aiming w/o moving.
Weapons - Punching things is super satisfying.  Honestly I think the game should have focused more mechanics based around the big robotic arm rather than the projectile based weapons.  Though I think those are quite satisfying to use as well.  There was a level where you are given a grenade whose smoke trails create temporary platforms and that made for some interesting mechancis.
Level Design - Overall level design is well done.  There is a decent variety of enemies who are exclusive to each map and they are deliberately placed in logical places with intended player solutions in mind.   There are a couple of visual language cues that don't communicate well and sometimes you end up dying because of those confusions.  Overall though traversing the levels are at least fun.
Mixed bag:
Narrative - The humor is smirk-worthy.  Other times it's cringe.  At its best you get exchanges with local heroes and their hang ups in life.  At worst you are actually reading the phrase "bust-a-cap".   The dialog is accompanied by this robotic chugging sound for all characters.  I think this was a poor choice.  The art and writing has a lot of personality while this sound constantly going while you read robs much of that personality away.  There has to be a better design choice here.  Others have used simpler methods like single voice lines (laughs, grunts, oohs, and aahs), emotive gibberish also works too, and when all else fails use nothing or subtle blip noises from older games.
Music -   Some tracks do a good job adding to the whole "puckish villainy" motif of the game while others are poor cultural pastiches with gibberish vocals which sometimes grate on the nerves.  Overall this is neither a great or terrible soundtrack.  It's pretty middle of the road.
Boss fights - The first boss fight was a simple "take their weapons and turn it against them".  Cut and dry but clever enough.  Every other boss fights are scenarios that utilize their own exclusive mechanics not used anywhere else in the game.  Don't do this.  Boss fights should be a test of your mastery of the mechanics you've spent the level mastering.  At best you are given a somewhat enjoyable wrecking ball fight based around using physics and motion.  At worst you are frustrated trying to crush a viking with giant fists using dubiously consistent aiming and hit detection.  I know what they were trying to do (you are the bad guy so you are the boss fight) but in terms of player game mechanics this is bad design and it served no benefit to the game.  These types of things should only be bonus stages, not boss fights.
Verdict:
It's far from a perfect game but it's a good start from a budding indy studio.  There's definitely talent and potential exhibited here.  The game itself can use some tweaks and fixes here and there but overall is fun enough.  It's at the very least worth getting when on sale.

The game is a bit of a love letter to a lot of games, but from the bad guy's perspective. The Story is interesting and amusing. There's plenty of references to a lot of games, even a modern ones.  The animation is tight and colorful. As said in various places, there's boss fights, but from the Bad Guy's perspective. Remember the very first boss fight in Sonic the hedgehog 1? the one with the wrecking ball? You get to use it against a sonic-ish character!
While the game might be short, compared to games nowadays, I'd rather have a short good game that I can pick up anytime, than a long one where it takes me awhile to get back to if I am away from it for a period of time.
Now for the pros, cons, and on the fences that I have about the game
Pros
+Humor
+animation of the characters
+ Can use Keyboard and Mouse, or Controller.
+Easy to learn on how to move around and fight in the boss fights.
Cons
-Could use a way to configure the control
-the grenade weapon is a bit tricky to use and can miss a lot when you're in a hurry.
-Could use a way to reload to the last checkpoint.
On the fence
?From what I hear, the boss fight on the good path is really hard
?Could use something like homing missiles or grenades
?Grenade jumping is still a bit tough to use at times for me.
All in all, the game is worth checking out at least once.

Not recomending this game dosn't mean I didn't enjoy it. I'm just.. dissapointed.
I absoloutley love the main character, Crow is a cleaver, well designed, and almost literal representation of the villian trope complete with an arsenal of weapons that would make Dr. Robotnik jealous. Every other princess was adorably drawn and had a little character to them, just, not as much as Crow. They all seemed two dimensional compared to the work put into Crow. The artwork is beautiful  especially in the portraits but when I looked down at the sprites they were cute but... not nearly as well designed as the portraits. What really bothered me was whenever you entered a boss fight the sprites wouldn't change at all. They would just stand where a seat would be and continue their mini animation loop while in the machine.  The music was cute but personally, it kind of layed on top of the level instead of imersing the player into the world they designed. When you are in the dwarf kingdom and the princess decides to make crow her new steed the music just continued on casually, failing to convey any sense of excitement or energy. In the very same level- should you die during the "boss"- you would respawn with the same music playing but it would soon change and fade into the new song. For me that made me feel I hadn't finished the previous portion of the level and and skipped over it in my mind, feeling as if I had just selected a random mini game instead of fighting a boss. The water level is what really did it for me though. It reminded me of a level in the new Donkey Kong Country, where everything is a color sillouette and you have to navigate that way. With this level everything felt so..flat. there was no sense of depth anywhere and everything felt like it was drawn in Microsoft paint. Some of the misc. underwater plants hovered off of the border, and the backgrounds they were placed on felt empty. The Eels felt like a two bit amusment park animatronic, lunging forward and trying to bite you and then mechanically retreating back into the wall. They came off as lifeless and mechanical, seeing where their jaws where hinged as they jumped out. The platforming was enjoyable but the constant repetition of three enemies per level seemed lazy. The fire effects wasen't stylized, it just seemed like it was grabbed from a stock animation website.
I can't stress how much I loved this game but I was incredibly disappointed with the seemingly rushed design. It felt like I was playing a flash game..but not in a good way. I expected artwork comparable to the Shantae games. If the entire game held up to the same style and effort put in as the portraits, I think it could have been an amazing game. But it unfortunately falls short and feels rushed.

Not Recommended if :

Super Meat Boy is a pure 2D platformer created by the dynamic duo of Edmund McMillen and Tommy Refenes. It's greatly inspired by the charm and difficulty of games from the 8 bit era of gaming, however, it isn't at all weighed down by the issues prevelant in games of that time. The game is as simple as running and jumping, there are no power ups or alterations of the game's core mechanics. Super Meat Boy relies on it's level design and tight controls to flesh out the game, and where games of the past would have been tedius, SMB values the player's time. Deaths are quick, and respawns are almost instant. Playing through a world in this game may take you hours at first, but after practice, you can blast through levels in mere seconds. It's a game that you can pick up and play for any amount of time and have a good time, but also one that has hours of content behind it, thanks to hundreds of levels and a ton of unlockables. Super Meat Boy truly is a treat for any fan of 2D platformers looking for a challenge.

Super Meat Boy is one of the hardest games around, forcing you to have more precision than someone doing a heart transplant, and the speed of Usain Bolt on a sugar rush.  This game will do little to hold your hand, and will mock you after you spend half an hour trying to beat a single level with your half a million failed meat boys all going across the screen at once.  Also, invest in a case for your TV, because without one, your mouse might magically fly into the screen.  But luckily, after you get through it all, you feel truly rewarded for completing such a difficult task, right?  And the game makes you feel really good about yourself, too?  Hahaha, yeah no.  Chances are, if you do complete the game, you'll either feel like you just wasted 10-12 hours of your life (and trust me, it will take that long.), or you'll be too sad because of CHAD (we love you, buddy.).  But don't let me stop you, after all, I soldiered on and made it too the end, so why can't you?

My review for One Troll Army
First kudos to the dev team flyanvil for making a fun game.  It is a interesting game, with elements of strategy, tower defense, leveing up fort and gear, managing of resources & selling or buying resources to improve the troll or goblins.  I just recently beat all the main chapter campains.  It was a fun game, it was relaxing as well did not felt stress at all.  When you fight the enemy depending on the level, if you lose you won't be losing nothing in the main chapter campain.
The game, has 3 other modes as well.  There is the Endless mode, Survial mode & Twitch Vs.  I have not try yet the other 3 modes.  But, i maybe might try them.  But in truth, the game will be the same no matter what mode.  The only difference between the survial and twitch vs.  Is that Surival is just you trying to stay alive after every wave, lose and you start all over again.  Twitch vs, is interesting.
I do not know well how the Twitch Vs works.  But from what i have guess and watch a bit.  Is that you join chat in the devs live stream and then as you are watching the live stream while in the twitch chat.  You can play a enemy character to destory the fort or the troll with your allies.  Now again, i do not know prefectly well how it works.   I not sure if it also can be done with another twitch user that isn't a dev can live stream the game, while others join the twitch live stream of that twitch user live stream and be able to play against them in the game as they live stream.
It confusing i agree, but in truth the game is fun and interesting to play.  Maybe not everyday but more like from time to time.  Best thing about the game it is free, because the devs had a event that if players join and play against the devs.  during that month before it release, they can help lower the price or make the game free to play.  Which i am grateful there was gamers that was interested to battle the devs to make the game free.  Kudos to them for doing that, but do not get me wrong i do not mind paying for the games i want to play.  But i was happy that they got to make it free to play

Pros+
+Fun Gameplay
+Graphics
+Fun as being this giant troll that can beat the stuffing out of a enemy

cons-
-After beating the main fort campains, there nothing else to do but play the endless mode, survial or twitch vs.

I feel that this game has potential, but it is still quite unfinished.
Spaera is a tetris-like (or puyo puyo -like) game with different playable characters that each have four individual spells. In the story mode you play against a computer and the spells can be used to hinder opponent or to ease own game. And if you like tetris, then you probably also enjoy playing Spaera once it is finished. But at the moment there are several things to improve.
First I would like to have a story included to story mode and maybe some sort of backstory for the characters to add some depth to this game. After finishing the story mode (which takes about an hour) it feels like the game doesn't have anything else to give. It would be nice to unlock new characters, new game modes, challenges etc, which would add some replay value.
Another thing that bothered me was that you cannot read the spell description during game (which made me cast the spells at random). The spell descriptions can be read in character description before starting the game, but I also want to be able to read them while playing to refresh my memory.
There is short tutorial in this game, and the rules are simple enough to grasp within few minutes.
All in all, at the moment the game is not worth the price, but hopefully this will change after full release.

While the Director's Cut of Sonic Adventure (Or, to use its proper Japanese name, Sonikku no Adobencha) ultimately improves on the original game, it is not without its flaws. For example, Knuckleboy the Enchilada is still plagued by an obscure, yet omnipresent rendering error that causes him to appear red instead of the intended yellow, which severely hampers the game's racial subtext - while he was supposed to represent the Asian continental subconscious, many now incorrectly believe he is the physical manifestation of Native American spiritual beliefs. There are also a lot of translation errors. Some of the more noticeable ones are when Sonikku tells Amy Rose (another mistranslation - her Japanese name actually translates to Horse Horse) about the numerous ghosts haunting his apartment, they use the word "ghouls" instead of "ghosts", which may lead the player to believe he is actually besieged by some sort of zombies. This can lead to some confusion down the line when his apartment actually DOES get beset by an undead horde, as many might believe he was already suffering from that problem, when the evolution from ghosts to zombies is supposed to represent him coming to terms with his bisexuality.
However, at its core, this is still an excellent Visual Novel. While the sex scenes could use some better writing and voice acting, this is still a story that you owe it to yourself to experience.

-Sound effects are missing. Nothing feels right because of the lack of sound effects.
-Difficulty spikes. Certain areas are vastly more difficult than the ones directly before and after.
-Upgrades are pointless. Well, beyond extra health, ammo, and getting rocket fists and triple punch to clear crates faster.
-Pointless level obstacles. Crates come to mind. They take 3 hits without rocket/triple punch, and offer nothing to the stage
-No cutscene skips. Self explanatory.
-Levels are needlessly open. There's a lot of empty space that should be edited out.
That being said, should these all be fixed with patches, which would be easy to do, bar making upgrades useful, I would give the game a solid 8.5/10. Otherwise, I'm giving it a 7/10.

First, a disclaimer: I did back this, at the $25 level.
Now then, this game is kind of borderline on whether I'd recommend it or not.  I love just about everything about the game that isn't the gameplay.  The game could probably have used another few weeks for a bit of tightening and polish, a bit more content, a bit more instruction, a handful of bug fixes, some extra playtesting, that sort of thing.  The rest of it, though; the music is amazing, the level design is good when not requiring precision platforming, and the story and dialogue are all stand-outs.
The TL;DR on this is that I'd recommend it now for people who can look past some mild-to-moderately frustrating gameplay for an actually engaging story and beautiful world with awesome music.  I'd recommend this generally to anyone if it goes on sale.

The cons are a bunch of little issues and a handful of big ones, none of which are really dealbreakers on their own, but can add up to larger annoyances when put together.

I like this game quite a bit. It's a pretty fun action platformer where you basically play as a cartoon supervillain (the guy's big on villainy for the sake of villainy rather than for any particular goal). You've got a 360 degree range with your attacks, which works well most of the time but gets... interesting when you need to attack in one direction while moving in another, and the game doesn't really go out of its way to tell you that you can use grenades to jump to certain collectibles/platforms, though I'm fairly certain you can beat the game without it.
Speaking of beating the game, I haven't yet, because what I presume to be the final boss kicked my rear end till I quit and I haven't gotten the heart up to try again just yet; it seems like it's harder than it's intended to be. That aside, the music's good, the art's good, the characters are likable enough that I felt the need to try and get all possible dialogue, and for the most part I didn't feel like I was being pushed through too many hoops trying to get all the collectibles.
All in all, I've enjoyed my time with the game and would recommend it if you're looking for this kind of an action platformer.

This game is a like a wallpaper generator.
The procedurally generated landscapes are aesthetically pleasing and you will find yourself mesmerized by the dawns and the views atop of the mountains (then you will either fall to your death or asphyxiate, but that is all part of the fun.)
The current focus is exploration for the sake of exploration gathering resources in the process; there are no goals or quests (or storyline for that matter.) There are some vehicles and work stations that have to be unlocked via research but is nothing too demanding.
There are five planets to explore, each one with a different landscape/weather/gravity but the flora is the same across the board and there is no fauna.
The worlds themselves can be shaped to your heart's content (with a few limitations... some of us have tried to make them flat, not quite there yet...)
The minimalist diegetic interface (I recently learned the meaning of that and was eager to find somewhere to use it) does an excellent job of conveying the relevant information without getting in the way although the inventory management can feel capricious at times.
There is no shortage of glitches but most of them are quite comical (who doesn't like to fly around using a chair) and the team is actively working on it even going as far as releasing a patch during the Christmas period.
The game is entertaining even in its current 'bare bones' state and has potential for greatness... and glowing Zebra Balls!
All in all really pleased and looking forward to future developments.

-Yes I read the description

That being said, game devs take note if you are reading; walking simulators are by far probably one of the most simple "games" to make and this can't even do that right. Most Walking Sims have some sort of filler to throw at you, some banter or dialogue, maybe some nice environments to gaze at.

Pretty much it doesn't bode well for any game where I can leave a 1 liter bottle of Coke on the W key, take a bathroom break, and accomplish the monumental task of moving a few hundred meters in a game that legitimately has nothing to offer.

I really wanted to recommend this game, but there is one major game-breaking flaw which simply makes the game unplayable for me.
The game is not optimised to use all of your machines power. By that, I mean even if you have a super computer this game will break once your prisoner count reaches around 5-700. The engine of the game itself simply cannot handle the amount of AI processing required. Google 'Prisoner Architect lag' and you will see my point.
I've sunk a decent amount of hours into the game because building the prison from scratch is so damn fun, the mechanics of this game are excellent, but every time I have to faceth grim reality that you cannot play this for the long term. I am a gamer who likes big things, long term projects. I don't play simcity to end my playthrough when my city reaches 1000 pop. I don't play Total War to end my playthrough when I have conquered one full province. I don't play Football Manager to end my playthrough after half a season. That is how this game feels like.
The fact they have a 1000 Prisoner achievement is laughable, as you cannot obtain it without downloading a steam workshop prison which already has 1k prisoners in it.
The devs have ignored this issue for years. If the lag was fixed, I would reccommend this game all day long. There are ZERO other issues with it in my opinion, other than the fact that post short-term, it is simply unplayable.

I always like to reserve my review for a game only I have completed it once or twice.
Nefarious  brought back memories of playing the Mega Man franchise, especially in the SNES era. This game has catchy 'get stuck in your head' music, and a hilarious, intellegent story. Nefarious is a very self-aware nostalgia trip, as well as a videogame and hero/villan trope savvy adventure that has an abundance of re-play value.
I found myself playing and re-playing the game to:
Find all the crowns.
Get all the vinyl (like a true hipster!)
Get all the upgrades.
Attempt no upgrade runs.
Search for secret passages.
Unlock secret levels.
Attempt speed runs.
Practice on a level or a boss fight so I can work for that better score.
Replaying to choose different options to learn more about the story of this world and the relations of the dynamic cast of characters.
Finding that better ending.
Working towards that 100% clear.
All of the the personal accomplishments that made us re-play many games of the 8-bit ans 16-bit era. My favorite moment was when I accidentally stumbled upon a secret part of a level and I was rewarded with more backstory and a dark plot twist to what I thought was going to be a very lighthearted game. It gets dark. It gets deep. It makes you relect on past gaming experiences.
This game was easy to pick up and hard to put down once you get into the nuances of the story. The game requires skill and practice to get all the goodies (and it leaves you feeling accomplished when you finally do find that one thing you were missing) but it doesn't have a "skill check" that is so hard that will make the rest of the story inaccessable.
I look forward to the continuation of this story and I can't wait to see what sort of updates and additions to this game the future will bring.

I so badly wanted to like this game. The idea that I would be able to experience the other end of one of my favorite things in gaming, the boss. I counted down the days to release. Unfortunately, I can't recommend this game in it's current state.
This game is just a basic barebones platformer with a (albeit very pretty) bad guy theme pasted over it. The levels feel so simple and empty, and don't mix well with Nefarious's gameplay, no option to use a controller or rebind controls along with an out of place wonky aiming system make the game feel very clunky and awkward to play. The music is also nothing to write home about.
On the other hand, the character design and artstyle are great. Everyone is expressive and looks great. They have charming personalities and really interact with eachother well. Also the whole theme of being the bad guy and taking control of the boss is a very unique promising gameplay idea.
Bottom line, Nefarious is not great. It's not bad by any means, but, at the current price and it's current state I feel it's not worth the money. But once it gets updated and its' issues are resolved you can bet I'll come back and continue to wreak havoc as Crow.

Imagine Super Mario Brothers with a sadistic streak and a weird sense of humor.  That’s Super Meat Boy.  When the evil Dr. Fetus (yes, he’s a fetus in a robotic jar) kidnaps Bandage Girl, Meat Boy must spring into action to save her!
The whole point of the platformer genre is to get from point A to point B, and save the princess by downg so.  Super Meat Boy distills that down to one of the tightest games ever made.  Rather than have grand sweeping levels with multiple checkpoints and branching paths, most levels in SMB can be beaten in less than 45 seconds.  But that doesn’t mean they’re easy.  This is a punishing game of dexterity and muscle memory.
The five worlds you’ll explore are full of traps and obstacles.  From buzz saws and rocket launchers to pits full of dirty needles and salt piles, there are countless ways for Meat Boy to die.  And you’ll make plenty of mistakes.  But don’t worry, because you’ll reload at the start of the level in about half a second, ready to try again.  You’ll develop a flow through these levels, as you learn the precise timing to guide Meat Boy through impossible gaps and razor thin openings.  There are secret characters to unlock, bandages to collect, hidden retro-styled levels to explore, and more.  Play as Steve from Minecraft!  Or Commander Video from BIT.TRIP!  Or a Head Crab!
Your reward for all of this is to watch all your attempts overlaid on one another.  One by one, dozens of meat boys will perish in a multitude of ways, but one will persevere and reach Bandage Girl.  You can save these replays for later viewing or sharing online.
The simple graphics allow this game to run on almost any machine, without slowdown.  This is critical in a game that requires such precision.  Though you should cap the framerate to 60 FPS to keep some bugs from popping up.  The music is powerful and energetic, and even though you’ll get frustrated at the game and yourself for your shortcomings, you won’t stay that way for long.  The humor sprinkled throughout the cutscenes and even the main menu constantly reminds you that this game shouldn’t be taken too seriously.
Super Meat Boy belongs in the pantheon of great indie games.  One of the finest examples of the platforming genre, and its a heck of a lot of fun.  Although my thumb hurts after beating it in four days.  I didn’t even do the dark world this time.
Super Meat Boy is available on Humble, Steam, Xbox 360, PS4, PSVita, and will soon be ported to WiiU.

If you're not sure about paying 10 bucks for an Early Access game, do yourself a favor: Click the "Follow" button before you leave and check back when Spaera is finished.
If you grew up loving games like Puzzle League, Mean Bean Machine, and Puzzle Fighter, there's a decent chance you will like Spaera. The mechanics will feel quite familiar: Setting up combos and chains, and then lining up at least three blocks of the
same color to trigger a glorious chain reaction unleashing the much dreaded "garbage" upon your enemy.
However, unlike in most other VS Puzzlers, you will probably not get any crazy accidental chains with blocks just happening to fall into place. Where other games will have blocks freefalling all the way to the bottom, Spaera's blocks will only move down
by one square when the block below them is deleted. This one difference alone makes Spaera a much more skill based game than the classics you might be used to.
(There are other factors that give this game a high skill ceiling, but I won't go into detail now)
There is only one thing that I personally dislike about the core mechanics that I highly doubt will be different in the finished game:
Garbage blocks that you send to your opponent will not drop on top, but be pushed up from the bottom of the board. A player loses, when they have at least 1 block in one of the top 3 rows of their board. However, so long as the player keeps making matches, any block in the 'kill zone' will be deleted, including those pushed into the zone by garbage from below. The only way to lose is by failing to make a match.
As a result, it never feels like one player defeated the other by unleashing powerful combos and spells, it just feels like one of
you made a stupid mistake. So while a game in progress is tons of fun, the end of match can sometimes feel a little unfulfilling.
Overall I recommend Spaera to anyone who mastered the VS Puzzlers of the olden days and is now looking for something a little more challenging.

This game is a like a wallpaper generator.
The procedurally generated landscapes are aesthetically pleasing and you will find yourself mesmerized by the dawns and the views atop of the mountains (then you will either fall to your death or asphyxiate, but that is all part of the fun.)
The current focus is exploration for the sake of exploration gathering resources in the process; there are no goals or quests (or storyline for that matter.) There are some vehicles and work stations that have to be unlocked via research but is nothing too demanding.
There are five planets to explore, each one with a different landscape/weather/gravity but the flora is the same across the board and there is no fauna.
The worlds themselves can be shaped to your heart's content (with a few limitations... some of us have tried to make them flat, not quite there yet...)
The minimalist diegetic interface (I recently learned the meaning of that and was eager to find somewhere to use it) does an excellent job of conveying the relevant information without getting in the way although the inventory management can feel capricious at times.
There is no shortage of glitches but most of them are quite comical (who doesn't like to fly around using a chair) and the team is actively working on it even going as far as releasing a patch during the Christmas period.
The game is entertaining even in its current 'bare bones' state and has potential for greatness... and glowing Zebra Balls!
All in all really pleased and looking forward to future developments.

GASP.
Long winded / semi-comprehensive review.
The game is about 900 mb, give or take, and it didn't take long to install. Once you open the game, you're met with display options, but the graphics aren't impressive even on the highest setting. Starting this game in windowed mode may cause some problems. On the HUD, you're likely to receive some error messages like 'SetNextWeapon is not in VP Input Manager's buttons. You must add it for this button to work.' It obscures your (admittedly worthless) GPS module in the bottom lefthand corner. Poor coding, but jokes on you, there are no weapons.
The menu music is exactly the same as the music in game. A 20 second dark ambience loop that is poorly looped because it clips at its origin. Also, whichever menu option you select will immediately reset the loop.
Now once you hit the play button, there's no backing out of this menu. You must choose Moon, or if you were compelled beyond belief with high expectations into purchasing it, Mars.
Alright, let's get rolling. First off, a really ominous (read: not really) text-based message pops up before you begin your journey, telling you that this game is not designed to hold your hand, and that once you die, you die. However, this is misleading as you can't actually die. More on that later.
On the Comms you hear an androgenyous voice, clearly not at all concerned for your safetly, tells you in a plaintive tone that you've crashed. I should note that the crash is IMPLIED, you don't actually see the crash, as there's no cinematic cutscene or anything. This supposed crashsite is just a poorly moddled white conical shape, tilted to its side on a rock because, you know, it crashed. No damage --  nothing. How exquisite.
The androgynous voice tells you that your oxygen levels are limited and because basically your visor got f*cked up in the crash, and it actually shows you 5 different signals to follow instead of one leading you back to the LZ. It's up to you to run in one direction for an hour to find out which one is the real LZ! He/she offers some coy words of advice, telling you that you should choose wisely and hope for the best, because he/she THINKS the oxygen won't hold out long after he/she told you the oxygen levels are limited in the first place. Wow, as an astronaut I never, ever, in a million light years never would have rationally came to that conclusion. Thanks for all the help.
Controls are pretty straightforward. WASD to move, Spacebar to jump, and RMB to zoom in. Funnily enough, you can either tap the spacebar for a quick jump and fall, or hold down Spacebar to jump to new heights, and glide down until you release the spacebar, at which point you fall flat downward in place. Yep, this is typically how real life moon physics work, as I understand it.
Whoa sh*t! What was that? Giant bouncy balls that are all the same shape falling from the sky? Nobody briefed me on this? Oh they're supposed to be meteor showers that are hellbent on killing the player astronaut at all costs. Just like the developers, we all know the Moon is much bigger and has much more gravity than Earth, so of course it's safe to assume that the planet is getting consistently, CONSISTENTLY pelted with showers, no, blankets of meteors. I began to ask myself if this was indeed the much anticipated Chicken Little walking simulator on the moon that I've been hearing so much about?
You can SEE the meteors spawn in the skybox. On your HUD you get periodic warning text when a meteor is in the vicinity of your player. Each direct hit with a falling meteor reduces your oxygen, yes, your OXYGEN levels by 10% a pop. Oxygen decrements on its own, I didn't bother really counting the time between % points, but I knew I lost a point of O2 because my visor filled with blood. Yes, your f*cking visor gets splattered with blood when you lose an O2 point. Remember the last time you held your breath and blood poured out of your face? Neither do I.
The first signal I reached was a big disappointment. It was just a radio-like object with a light emitter on the ground. I couldn't actually do anything with it, such as interact or pick it up. So I had to walk for another 20 minutes to try and get to the next point on my HUD while "dodging" these space balls.
On my journey I went from %100 Oxygen to %Dead oxygen (no, not joking, this is actually how it's presented). Oh, I guess having a non-existent number like Dead for my O2 reading is nothing to be concerned about, because my breathing maintained its course. It was the same loop I've been hearing for the past 45 minutes, and it continued to haunt me. I began to have fantasies about the tell-tale breathing stopping. It just kept breathing, and breathing, and breathing and the more I heard it, the more it bore into my consciousness. Was I experiencing space madness?
About 800 meters away from another signal, I encountered an invisible wall. I tried another route and got hit with another wall. Then I tried to go in the opposite direction to the northernmost signal and guess what? I hit another invisible wall. Now if you guessed that correctly, your thought process is probably more cogent than anyone involved in the making of this Press-W simulator.
Walking aimlessly at this point, I must have tripped something because the meteors were disappearing about 200 meters from impact on the ground. I could literally sit back and watch the bouncy ball showers spawn above me and attempt to smash me into the ground.
So whether or not you run out of Oxygen or get killed by falling rocks, you never actually die in game. The only way you die is to commit suicide IRL while playing this game.There are Steam achievements in this game. However, only about 1% gutted it out to get any of them. If they'd just add an uninstall achievement, 100% of the players would have it and you'd actually feel as if you had accomplished something.

Are we good there? Ok, now for the details.
I've been following this game ever since I heard about it on the Brawl in the Family webcomic, there was just something about the concept that intrigued me. Having played through, while I felt it was a bit short for such a long wait, I'd say it's still definitely worth the price tag.
The story isn't anything too complex. Kidnap princesses, manage evil empire, use doomsday device to conquer world.  What makes it memorable is the characters. Ranging from Crowe's style, to Princess Mayapple's unbreakable optimism, to Princess Farrah Day's hilarious misunderstanding of the situation, any time a dialogue box pops up, you're in for a treat.
The gameplay feels quite smooth. Jumping from platform to platform is quick and precise; combat is over in one or two punches, and although grenades do have a slight arc in their trajectory, I found that most of the things that I can't hit the first try tend to be unable to fight back. Although I will admit, any time I'm expected to bomb-jump across gaps tends to be extremely frustrating.
The Reverse Boss Battles, probably the most unique concept of the game, unfortunately ended up being the weakest aspect for me. They throw away the smooth platforming for clunky, difficult to aim attacks, and have ZERO explanation. The second reverse boss is an especially bad example of this.
I find that, at the end of it all, although there are these little points that niggle at me, it didn't subtract that much from the experience as a whole. If you're fond of old-fashioned 2D platformers, but wish they had the smoothness that today's generation can offer, give Nefarious a shot.

The controls could stand to be a bit tighter and there are a few bugs here and there, but other than that I find this game to be very enjoyable. The art is beautiful, the soundtrack is fun, and the story and cast are fantastic. Worth the money in my opinion.
My only regret is that we didn't tell Becky what a thorax is.

Nefarious is a platformer where in you play the bad guy (duh).
It's short (only ~5 hours), but the game itself is very satasfying.
It's not without its problems.
Many...
MANY problems...
But if like platformers and good characters, you'll like this game.
From this point on, I'm going to talk about each stage, the mechanics, what works and what doesn't.
I love this game but HO BOY, are there problems.
Lets start at stage one; The City.
It's a decent opening level. Not much else to say on this front. It does a good job of establishing the senario and main characters were going to be follwing, Crow and Mayapple. It does a nice job of introducing the various mechanics used throughout the game.
It does point out what will be a major flaw, though; Crow's damage intication. Crtow's sound effect isn't very audable, the effect isn't very noticable, and the knockback is non-existant when it wants to be.
Could it have been better? Sure, but I can't point to anything specific holding this level back.
Don't worry (Or do), I will later on.
Well, now that were done kiling cops and destroying massive amounts of city property, lets move on to the airship. I will be using these airship interludes to talk about certain mechanics I can't pin to one stage for a good example of. but for now, I'll just say it's nice, compact, and I like how the elevator will not stop at the second floor if you punch "up" again.
If the game had more little things like that strewn about, this review would probably be less negitive.
Now for stage 2, and the stage where we really start to see some of the holes form. The stage itself is fairly forgetable, unfortunetely, but the experiences arn't. Specifically, with the flying enimies here; They are too abundent and too erradic. The reapers in the last stage had far more predictable movement, making hitting them with the grenades a challenge, but not annoying like with the flying bees. The other enemies are fairly standard (and the Manti are actually fun to kill).
Then you rescue Bee princess (I forget her name)and you come to THAT area. An area I have dubbed "Cluster-♥♥♥♥ Collum", Because it is mostly just an upwardpath chock full of enemies. It's not challanging, it's annoying.
Otherwise, Dull stage, Dull power, and... Ok, the princess isn't dull, she has a few good lines, so I can't give this the triple D.
The Reverse boss fight here is a play on the classic eggman wrecking ball machine, but YOU control the ball.
The fight itself, (Minor Spoilers) Is arguabely the best Reverse boss in the game, as it works like it's inteded too, there's no way to cheese it, and it's just fun to wave around the wrecking ball. Dash's mechanic of building up towers to hit your ship is fun and works well with the boss (or... Hero? I'm going to call these hero fights from now on. it'll be easier.)
I wish all the Hero fights were as well designed as dash's.
Back to the airship, and, though I am disapointed none of the minions (not even the obvious backer ones) have new dailouge, Back and Mayapple's dialouge, along with Bee princesse's start to show their characters, and show promise. promise that will be fulfilled.

Nefarious is an action platformer, where you are the villain, but the concept has been taken very seriously (except for the game show revelations, but that's spoiler territory). The "boss" fights are very well done, capturing what it meant to be a villain in it's entirety, making you fill like the gimmick every end of level. The story is also engaging for what it is and the soundtrack, other than some looping issues, convey the theme of the levels and aesthetics very well.
The game ultimately needed a bit more polish, especially with the smoothness of the controls considering how some areas require precision platforming and the lag between the press and the jump does not help at all. Also, triple punch, explosive punch and charge punch do NOT work. You'd need just as many charged/triple/explosive punches to kill an enemy as normal punches.
So unless the problems are fixed, I can't sincerely suggest this game to anyone yet.

Nefarious is a twisted take on villainy, a satire on what it means to be antagonistic. It's not original, but that's where its strengths lie - it's supposed to be the norm, only you have a very different role in the story than you're used to.
It's your standard platforming action: hopping across platforms, grabbing coins and collectibles, punching and blowing up enemies. It's simplicity done well, and it manages to please most audiences to a certain degree - whether you're a casual player, a speedrunner or a completionist, there's something here for you in the gameplay.
The story is nothing truly special overall, but the way the dialogue is written is nothing short of charming. That and, the appreciable hand-drawn art style and generic, yet wholesome and appropriate, music makes this a solid parody game.
If you want a fun platformer that's unoriginal in some ways yet unique in others, give Nefarious a try.

While in need of some tuning in a few places, this game is definitely worth a look. Its strongest point is its characters and world. They feel really well fleshed, and every one of the main characters had clear motivations, as well as a bit of depth to their personalities. Each zone felt thematically distinct and interesting, while also being decently tied to its particular royal in some way.
Where the game does have room for improvement is largely polishing work. I'm playing the v1.0 right out the gate, so this isn't entirely surprising. The end of each stage transitions (sometimes jarringly) between the final boss battle and the grade screen with little to no ceremony. Additionally, it felt like there were some control limitations, as if some artificial difficulty had been inserted to give the game a "classic" feel. It honestly may have just been me being bad at game, though, so this is a minor quibble. Some art assets also felt out of place due to how three-dimensional objects "popped" versus the two-dimensional models, but that's another easy clean-up thing.
In any case, I definitely recommend this title, because the story is fun, it introduces some interesting twists on classic platformers, and I'm very interested to see what the studio now does with the IP in the future.

Nefarious is a game where you play as Crow - a villain character who kidnaps princesses and rides giant robots during boss battles.
While in the beginning, when I just started playing the game it felt kinda cheap in terms of graphics, design, soundtrack seemed kinda odd with all these themes with vocals...But the more I played - the more I enjoyed it. All dialogs in the game and overall character interactions are just golden, by the end of the game I was so attached to almost all the characters and their personalities it was even sad the game ended. Gameplay is simple and yet fun, upgrades add a nice touch to gameplay and one can customize Crow with skills he prefers.
I've always liked villain characters, especially those who have this special charisma about them and Crow does the thing for sure. And while he is trying hard to act as a bad guy there is some good stuff in him in a right amount, so "good stuff" doesn't spoil him as a villain and only adds to the character's greatness.
Also, while there are plenty of games where you play as evil character I wonder why did nobody ever thought of reverse boss battles, where you are the boss - it's just a genius thing that got me interested in the first place. I hope devs will sometime do a sequel, there is so much room for new stuff and ideas.
In the end I can say that I found something special in this little game, something  that captivatd me. Maybe some people won't like it that much but iff you like platformer games like shovel knight, megaman x games etc. I would highly recommend to try this game out.

No More Room in Hell is an intense, brutal zombie game that utilises Valve's famous Source engine. It is also free to play however not in the sense that most free to play games are. It is literally, a game that while a bit lacking on content, is devoid of typical F2P tropes such as pay-to-win microtransactions and game content hidden behind a massive paywall. This game has a very brutal combat system that is a tad slow but really captures the gritty realism that this game provides. Each wonderfully brutal kill that I delivered to a zombie felt very lifelike especially considering that this game runs on the Source engine. There are maybe 8 to 10 levels in this game with locations ranging from a shopping mall to the location of the house in George A. Romero's horror classic Night of the Living Dead. A personal favourite was in Havana which felt gritty and very survival based compared to some of the other levels. It also pumps me up for the upcoming game Dying Light which is set in a simular setting. You can play up to 4 player co-op with your friends which is always enjoyable especially with this genre. However there are some issues that I have with this game. As I stated earlier, it is a bit light on content but that is kinda to be expected considering that you aren't paying a cent for this game. Another issue is the lack of a difficulty option. This doesn't apply to everyone but I went into some levels blind and I was completely overwhelmed at times and its times like these where a difficulty slider or even just a warning of difficulty on the level description would be helpful towards new players. Finally, the game doesn't really break any new ground in the zombie killing genre. This is only a minor complaint considering that this game was likely made by a very small team. With that being said, it would be neat to see small developers innovate in really cool ways. Overall, No More Room in Hell is a frantic, visceral zombie experience that while doesn't exactly take the genre and re-invent it, its a game that grabs you by the throat and bites into your neck with some great combat, varied level design and a true free to play system and is a very enjoyable zombie murdering experience.
FINAL SCORE: 8.5/10

You probably already know about this game so I'll just sum it up real quick and talk about the port.
It's Sonic's first 3d game and it has all the quirks that came with all n64 era 3d games.
It's glitchy, has hilariously bad cutscenes, and has a mash up of gameplay styles that you might not like, but I still think it's fun to play (except for Big's story)

The ports of this game got gradually worse, and this was the last one AFAIK.
They tried to fix it a while back, but it still isn't good.
You have three options:
Grab the original dreamcast version.
Grab the 2004 PC release and mod it
Grab the Steam release and download the BetterSADX mod to turn it into the 2004 PC version.
The PC version can easily become the best version if you install the right mods (BetterSADX, Dreamcast textures/lighting, etc.)
Dreamcast is the way the game was meant to be played, without the DX downgrades.
Any of the options above are the best way to experience this game.
It's still Sonic Adventure though, so you'll either love it or hate it.

If you're looking for a positive review, then you're in the wrong place, HOWEVER, if you're here for a tremendous chicken Stir Fry recipe, THEN LOOK NO FURTHER!
- Serves 4
- 10 mins to prepare and 10 mins to cook
- 325 calories / serving
- Healthy
INGREDIENTS:
- 1 orange, zested and juiced
- 2tbsp soy sauce
- 2tbsp sesame oil
- 250g (8oz) tender stem broccoli
- 5cm (2in) piece root ginger
- 1tbsp sunflower oil
- 1 garlic clove, finely sliced
- 1 red pepper, deseeded and thinly sliced
- 150g Straight To Wok Noodles
- 400g (13oz) chicken fillet, cut into thin slices
METHOD
Step 1 - Mix together the orange zest and juice, soy sauce and sesame oil and set aside.
Step 2 - Blanch the broccoli in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain well and set aside.
Step 3 - Finely shred the ginger. Then heat a large frying pan or wok, add the sunflower oil, heat it until sizzling, and fry the ginger till it's crisp.
Step 4 - When it's done, remove with a slotted spoon. Add the chicken and garlic, and stir-fry until just browned. Remove the meat using a slotted spoon and set aside.
Step 5 - Add the red pepper and broccoli and stir-fry for around 2-3 minutes until it's just tender. Add the soy sauce mixture, bring it to the boil then return the chicken to the pan and heat through. Serve with noodles.But i do love the game ;D

This is a tetris clone but in its current state this game feels like alpha at best. Story mode has no story, buttons are poorly described, mechanics are not explained and the overall gameplay feels like it wouldn't be out of place as part of a knock-off 50-in-1 bootleg CD on my old Pentium 100 nearly twenty years ago. The sfx sound like they were stolen from Keen Dreams and downsampled. It's like they spent most of their budget on the nicely animated title screen and had very little left for the actual game.
The one potentially redeeming thing is each 'character' has a series of spells that can be deployed to stuff up their opponent / improve their own side. But really, it's a small glimmer of promise among tens if not hundreds of issues clearly waiting to be fixed. Avoid.

The game is currently what I would call "Crappy Tetris." You drop blocks similar to the blocks in Tetris, except different parts of the blocks you drop have colors, and this Tetris is realy a "Match 3" game of sorts. You get to pick a character to "play as," which means you see their picture on the left, and you can activate one of four spells during the match, and each character has different spells. I guess getting more matches progresses you along to the better/different spells. I was too busy trying (and failing) to manage my blocks compared to my opponent, the computer, "who" was played by another character. This was the story mode...which as of right now, is just fighting one enemy after the other, with no dialog, no plot, nothing. Fight starts, fight ends, next start fights, etc.
In other words, story mode has no story, and after beating two opponents in a row and succumbing to the third, I had enough of story mode and tried online mode, where I did quickly find another player who ground me into paste like the trash that I am at competitive online gaming without any effort on his or her part. If competitive weird Tetris is the thing you've been dying to have, then you'd probably like this. For anyone not looking for a competitive gaming experience, however, this game's current early access status has nothing of import to offer the single player aficionado, and even if there were more content and the spells were more useful and a bigger part of the game, I still did not particularly enjoy the overall gameplay despite having liked singleplayer Tetris as a kid.

Incredibly fun puzzle battle game in the style of Tetris!
Gameplay - 7/10 - Simple block-stacking, colour-matching, spell-casting fun. The whole game is a 1v1 puzzle battle where players compete to clear blocks faster than their opponent. There's not much to say about it. The mechanics are very simple and easy to learn (even if there's no tutorial - but that's coming soon) yet gameplay is still expansive and requires both planning and snap decision making to win.
Story - 1/10 - Doesn't exist. Characters have snippets of dialogue but not much else. At this moment I will assume this will change by the game's release and void it from my final thoughts.
Visuals - 7/10 - The art style is quite charming, and every character has their own personality that shines in their design. However, there's really not much to the visuals otherwise. Everything else is very basic, but that's not necessarily a *bad* thing.
Audio - 6/10 - I'd like to say that the music is excellent in this game. There's not much of it, but what tracks are there, are very nice to listen to. However, that's about it. The sound effects are pretty boring, and would give each character's special moves much more weight if they were better designed. No voice acting.
Overall - 7/10 - It's easy to pick up and, if you like these types of games, a great timekiller that you'll probably be going back to again and again. It's still in active development, so I'm sure many improvements will be coming in the future. Buying this game full price is worth it, but if you're unsure then go ahead and wait for a sale.

This is a cool little indie effort in the tradition of head-to-head puzzle battle games like Super Puzzle Fighter II Turbo, Puyo Puyo, Panel de Pon, and especially Tetris Battle Gaiden. I’m recommending this right now – it’s currently in early access and probably will be for a long while - because I think it has tons of potential. The puzzle action is solid (though it’s a little stiff at times), the attack animations are quite cool, the character designs are very memorable, I like all of the different special powers, and the whole experience is definitely fun. Spaera doesn’t try to redesign the wheel, and that’s okay: the designers have mostly taken some cool stuff from classic games in the genre and put it into an attractive, cheerful package. I think that puzzle battle games are a relatively untapped genre that could really blow up on Steam. If Spaera’s designers can capitalize on this strong start and polish it into something excellent, the game could be at the forefront of a renewed interest in the genre.
It must absolutely be said that this game is clearly a huge work in progress. The presentation needs a lot of polish and work, there are bugs that need to be ironed out, and the story mode hasn’t been implemented yet. The biggest thing the game needs is a training mode. What do all of the special blocks do? What’s the best situation to use my character’s special powers? How do I use them in the first place? You’re just kind of thrown into the game and you have to figure it out. I would win a match and nod to myself, thinking: "Yeah, I have no idea what I'm doing." Be aware that, if you do put down your money and buy this game, it's in a very, very early stage and it's going to need to go through a good deal of development. You're going to be a bit lost and there won't be very many people to play against online (I saw only four unique users over the course of playing for a couple of hours) and the whole thing needs polish. But if you're willing to pay for potential, I think that this is worth checking out.
As an aside, I think that the name is really bad - it needs at least a subtitle that lets you know this is a puzzle game. Even the library image could use a few falling blocks over the characters' heads. Otherwise, if I'm just scrolling through Steam and I like puzzle games, why would I stop and look at this?

Game is fun, but limited. All you can really do is play multiplayer against CPU's or other players. No tutorial(as i'm writing this, but one is planned soon.), no storyline(says story but it's just VS matches atm.). It's basically a unique Tetris where you get spells to cast against your opponents. Trailer of the game pretty much shows all the gameplay.
Four-queue view is kind of a rather broken component, you can see too far ahead ruining the competitiveness of the game. This could be argued later on that it's better when characters are more balanced.. but with an orb system that let's you gather them up for spells to cast on opponents that are somewhat game-breaking, it's something an early release shouldn't have quite yet. For a more ideal and fun experience, a two-queue for this unique style of game would be pretty sufficient and create an ideal balance.
I would only recommend getting this in a bundle or 75% off until these kind of things are fixed.
Lots of random little bugs but still very playable... just isn't a whole lot to do and I have yet to see more than 12 to 13 players online at once, so it's not exactly thriving atm. Usually does have at least one or two people to play at all hours of the day though, but the match-making system currently matches you with anyone, most likely due to the limited amount of players.
Note: Community is pretty hostile if you try to disagree with them on game mechanics, so be careful. Most I talk to though are pretty chill, but it's kind of a close-knit community atm that doesn't like differing opinions.
TLDR:Fun game, broken four-queue, not much to do other than multiplayer, kind of hostile community at times.

Basically, it's Minecraft in space.
It's similar principles to many resource gathering games - establish a base, mine for resources, watch out for perils etc. The problem is, its incredibly addictive and relaxing.
There's no real pressure (apart from running out of oxygen) and you get to wander and explore fascinating planets.
As it's still very early access please take the following points with that in mind:
There isn't enough notable differences between the planets so exploring tends to get slightly monotonous after a while (but still thoroughly stress free). A little more diversity would certain aid in exploring.
So far, there's only a few modules to research and work with, I'm pretty sure this will improve over time and at the moment it's fun and functional.
The bugs I've come across are minor and relatively pain free, its so far never been game breaking.
Astroneer is such great potential and I have no regrets about recommending that people buy it, play it and enjoy it. It's a game made with a lot of heart.

It looks absolutely great, mechanics are fun and there's lots of potential in expanding the systems already in the game right now.
Obviously the game could use a little more content but since we're in early access i have high hopes for what is to come.
Performance-wise the game runs great until you start massively expanding your bases on multiple planets, needs some tweaking.
If you're looking for something captivating, relaxing and really good-looking... buy this right now.

The game is "early access" so I'll give it the benefit of the doubt that the unfullfilling single player experience will improve, but even if it does there's simply nothing here that you haven't seen before, and it's not any better. If you absolutely love this style of game (vs. match geared rather than single player puzzle) and have already tapped out other options then by all means give this a go, but I just didn't see anything here that would give me cause to reccomend it.

First off, don't take my word for it!
Get the game and try it for yourself to make up your own mind.
I'm not much of a campaign person and haven't played most of it and am therefore not going to touch it in my review.
Cons:
• Auto Lights when building foundation is on by default, and I can find no way to change the default setting for it.
• Logic system still has some behaviour that belongs nowhere but in a early access game.
• I don't think anyone is going to fix the remaining early access like problems.
I've more then once spent an hour too many trying to figure out why a logic circuit I made didn't do its job only to conclude that the behaviour could be blamed on the game itself after going so far as to make an exact replica of the logic system and seeing it work..
But my main source of frustration from this game is the "Auto Lights" function.
It has literally ruined games for me when i forgot to turn it off before building a large enough "foundation" overwriting my save after.
Pros:
• I get to satisfy my OCD like need to perfect automated systems.
• Several additional fun challange settings when starting a new sandbox game.
• Auto Lights CAN be turned off manually every time you are about to build a foundation.
• You may just learn why antisocial behaviour is a bad thing for all parties involved.
• Great feel to most of the management options.
Prison Architect is to be quite honest my favorite management game simply because of the prison twist, but the most fun part I think was exploring how the game works.
After having figured out how the game works, figuring out new ways to keep prisoners from escaping, killing eachother, or getting their hands on contraband is what makes it fun for me.
Some of the best features for doing that are however quite advanced and not quite as stable as I would like them to be, but well worth the time dealing with.
Very fun game, recommended, but PLEASE FIX PATHFINDING ISSUES!!!

Argh. This is one of those games. The would-be greats, the ones that could have, should have been good, but for whatever reason or other just didn’t end up being. These tend to upset me more than just outright bad games, since it seems so easy to look at things that could have been changed to make it great. Nefarious has a lot of those.
You play as Crow, latest in a line of bird-themed sky pirates whose MO is kidnapping princesses. His typical target is Princess Mayapple, but is always foiled by her kingdom’s hero, Mack. At the end of the game’s tutorial level, though, Mack decides to throw in the towel by breaking up with Mayapple, since in his own words she sees Crow more than he does. It’s a good introduction to the game and decently humorous.
Even though he’s not used to actually winning, Crow decides to go whole hog with the opportunity, and steal four more princesses to power a doomsday device and take over the world. Each resides in a different themed kingdom with its own gimmick, and you have to bust through their security, kidnap them, and make it back out. You do this through platforming, and this is where the game unfortunately starts to become lack-luster.
Crow’s arsenal consists of a metal gauntlet he can either punch people with, or fire grenades out of. You can do these in any direction you want, although bizarrely your punch is right click on a mouse and the grenades are bound to the left, which seems really backwards. Now, even though you’re the villain (a very silly, essentially harmless villain, but one nonetheless) in the story, it never felt to me like that factored into the gameplay much. These two attacks are pretty much all Crow has, and he ends up feeling weaker than many heroes from similar games: Mega Man and Shovel Knight have a whole arsenal of weapons by the end of their games, Kirby has whatever power you want to have, Mario is a deft acrobatic, Shantae can shapeshift into a ton of different forms, and that’s only a few examples. Crow doesn’t really have anything unique of his own, and that would be bad enough if he were just the hero, but the idea of most villains is that they’re set up as superior to the hero, a real obstacle.
Which Crow still sort of is, but only because the game is so easy. You can breeze through the stages pretty easily, and most enemies are ineffectual. You start with three heart containers, and damage typically comes in halves. Health drops very often, and you can buy three more hearts inexpensively, letting Crow take up to twelve hits before expiring. All death does anyway is make you drop a bit of your money, Shovel Knight style.
Midway into each stage, you kidnap that world’s princess, and gain an ability from each of them (except for Mayapple since her kingdom’s the tutorial). This is where something interesting could have come into play, but I found it a letdown. The first, a bug princess, gives you a hover-jump, which isn’t bad but has been done before. The second, a dwarf, turns the rest of the level into an auto-scroller after she decides to make Crow into her steed. I actually really liked the demon kingdom’s gimmick, where you send out a wave of fire upon throwing a grenade which hardens into a platform, but you hardly use it. Once you bring a princess back to the ship you don’t use their ability again, so none of their mechanics feel as fleshed out as they could be.
Before that, though, you have to deal with the heroes protecting them. In theory this is where Crow’s villainy comes more into play, as instead of fighting them on foot you hop into one of his robots, flipping the perspective around. That’s a great idea, but the devil lies in the execution. The first of these places you in what’s basically the wrecking ball hovercraft Doctor Robotnik used in the very first Sonic boss fight. Instead of it working like that game, though, you’re fighting with the physics engine to swing the ball at a fairly small target, sort of spoiling the homage. In the second, you’re in a giant robot (I assume also a Robotnik reference, in this case to his final fight in Sonic 3 & Knuckles) trying to pound a dwarf with its fists, but your movement is limited to jerking the body back and forth, and punching at the same two spots. It’s clumsy, and nowhere near as enjoyable as I imagine they hoped. The two guys you fight also have clear patterns and vulnerability periods, so they don’t really feel like you’re fighting something controlled by the player - compare it to Shovel Knight’s boss fight in Plague Knight’s campaign, where he has tactics for every situation and uses his full arsenal of weaponry.
A lot of other reviews of this game praise the characters, and here I sort of have to disagree. The princesses you kidnap are pretty one note, and while Crow himself is a decent character, he’s the same kind of ‘laughable bad guy’ I’ve seen in plenty of other media. It’s not anything new, and that’s actually true on Steam as well, since Plague Knight (I'm sorry for bringing that game up so much in this review) pretty much does everything Crow does but with much better gameplay. I was particularly disappointed with the heroes you fight, since they're practically non-entities aside from Mack and only show up for their fights. It feels like they could have been a more constant premise, although that would probably take more levels for each kingdom.
Overall Nefarious could have been a classic, but unfortunately the gimmick seems to have overshadowed having really good, or even just solid gameplay, and you can’t get away with not having that in a platform game.
