I've a casual fan of Formula 1 racing for a while, but my computer can't run F1 2017 and paying full price for an older game in the franchise seemed like a silly idea to me. I got this game from a Humble Bundle I paid $1 for. This game quickly won me over.
F1 2012 is an engrossing racing experience. The physics are solid, and the graphics hold up extremely well despite their age. The game really challenges you to push your car and driving ability to the limits, and it is a rewarding experience when you place well. Players who aren't used to racing sims or open wheel racing might struggle or feel overwhelmed, but there are a multitude of difficulty settings and driving aids that make for a relatively forgiving game (depending on your settings). No matter your skill level, you can set this game up so that the driving is enjoyable and the racing is competitive.
The game does have some drawbacks, but many of them are just facts of life when buying an older game in a franchise like this. The drivers/cars are out of date, and the graphics aren't as good as the newest titles. However, anyone considering buying this game already expects this. My biggest legitimate gripes are the agressive AI and the inconsistent penalty system, but these are nowhere near as bad as some other reviewers suggest.
If you're a fan of formula 1 or racing sims, this game is definitely worth picking up on sale (or maybe even full price) if your system can't run the newer F1 games. Just make sure you're willing to dedicate some time to playing the career mode and improving your driving skills to get the most enjoyment out of the game. F1 2012 captures so much of the complexity, challenge, and excitement of F1 racing, and that makes it a worthwhile game in my opinion.

Welcome to hell!  You are the Devil who has decided to try his hand at running an apartment building.  And catering to these monsters is no easy task.  There are monsters who love to say they are broke and skip out on rent.  You have monsters who can't stand another race of monsters and become increasingly dissatisfied with their living conditions if they stick around.  Some monsters just won't quit asking for upgrades to their apartment... like The Devil is made of money.  On top of all those picky renters, there are pesky groups that try to take down the apartment building and The Devil himself.  How dare they try to destroy the ruler of real estate hell!  Thankfully your renters feel the same way and will fight off incoming enemies, while you continue to strengthen your apartment empire.  You get to watch your renters find mates, have kids, and if they live long enough, you get to see them strike out on their own.  I have to say this is probably the cutest tower defense game, and it was pretty fun to play!  While the strategy genre is not something I am wonderful at, it was fun enough to play at a casual level.  Definitely worth picking up, whether it is full price or if you catch it on a sale.

I usualy don't write reviews about steam games unless they effect me personaly as a standout above the rest. Saying that Ori and the Blind Forest is a "good game" is a tremendous understatement. For this game not only defies expectations, but exceeds them in so many ways. This game has a little something for everyone. Someone interested in a casual game for a great story. Someone who wants to spend lots of hours perfecting their speedrun times. Someone who wants to listen to a stellar soundtrack. Or maybe just someone who wants to look at some amazing visuals. Whatever you could possibly want out of a game Ori and the Blind Forest delivers in ten fold.
Most of the deaths in the game you experience are your fault. The game can expect alot from you at times with all the difrent abilites to learn and I must admit even I felt frustrated at some of the more hard to learn abilites. But after you take a breather and work through them so that it feels natrual to preform them, it is like you are controlling the charcter yourself. When the moment comes that you fully master the control, it feels great to leap and jump from one platform to another with ease.
Now even though this game is labeled under the cute category on Steam. It can be far from it at times. That's not to say this aspect is a flaw but I want to take it a step further. I dare to say that even though a child like enviroment and cute charcters. This game treats you like an adult. With no  real villan, Ori and the Blind Forest excells in pulling your heart strings and creating a story unlikely to be seen in "cute" type of games, no offense to "cute" games.
In my eyes Ori and the Blind Forest will forever hold in my heart as not only a great game, but a masterpiece, and I think everyone should have a chance to play it in at least one point or another. Enough said this game is worth so much more than the asking price.

The Main Game & Campaign
I have no idea why I havent reviewed this game yet, however, in my opinion, it is one of the underrated Batman games in the Rocksteady Arkham Batman series. I don't remember the story to its full extent, because I haven't played the campaign since I beat it years ago. However, I remember enjoying it and having plenty of fun. It had Deathstroke, Joker, and first time encounters with him, which was interesting. Also after you have beaten the game there is plenty of side stuff to do with Deadshot, Anarky, Mad Hatter, Riddler... ETC

The Multiplayer
The mode described below is called Inv Predator Mode or something like that.
This gets its own SEPERATE paragraph because it is so great and underrated. Not nearly enough people play it and its very enjoyable. Its fairly hard to find matches, but when you do, it is a real treat. You either play as a thug of Bane or Joker, defending yourself with a assault rifle, shotguns, other primary weapons, grenades, and drones that BLOW up or KILL the opposing thug or Batman & Robin. You have to take control of the area and be cautious, watching for the opposing thugs and those caped crusaders! Or, you can play as Batman or Robin, and you must build fear upon both thug teams to win, and to defend the area from control of the thugs. Once again, this is extremely fun and albeit being fairly difficult, it makes for a thrilling, unique Batman experience. There is another mode, but not as popular, called the Hunter & Hunted, but I have no clue of what its about because I never had the opportunity to play it.
Edit 1:After some research however, I found that in the Hunter & Hunted mode there are 3 Bane and 3 Joker thugs, and they throw Batman in the mix. Its a sort of free-for-all. Everyone has only one life aswell.
Conclusion
Batman: Arkham Origins is a unique, underrated, and fun filled entry into the Rocksteady Arkham Batman series, and the online mode only builds upon this overlooked and unique title. If you enjoy the Rocksteady Arkham Batman series, you will certainly enjoy Batman: Arkham Origins!
Edit 2: Thanks to everyone that thinks this review is helpful, even though it was written in a matter of minutes and I was dumb enough to write this despite totally forgetting the whole story of the game!

This is a reimagining of the Devil May Cry franchise and I have played the 4 games of the main series yet still enjoyed this title for it's own appeal. So many of the negative reviews both on here and online just seem to be bitter gamers upset that it appears like Capcom has scrapped the original series, characters they know from the original titles are seen and have altered stories/personalities/looks or whatever else they are comparing to those games. I saw the Ninja Theory Reboot as just that, a reimagining and I did enjoy the game.
Pros:
The gameplay was just what I would expect from a hack and slash title, it felt smooth and the combos were more simplified than in many other games in the genre making the learning curve easier but diverse enough that you aren't using the exact same OP combo repeatedly. The angel and demon abilities were a nice touch needing the player to switch based on the scenario adding a unique gameplay that makes the game more intense especially on higher difficulty levels. I loved the level design throughout the game, the first few times through it was great fun exploring all the nooks and crannies in detail. The story, attitudes and personalities of characters may have been irritating and cliche throughout the game but by the end of the game it did feel like Dante & Virgil had evolved from the bratty teenage typical drama idiots into personalities that could very well match the personallities from the original series if a sequel to this game was made.
Cons:
I felt the story was almost rushed, I would have liked to see more background info on characters and lore in the game but I play a lot of RPGs so I am a bit biased there. While I did say they evolved by the game's end it was frustrating watching the childish antics of these two powerful beings acting like high schoolers for much of the game. Kat was a nice addition and it would have been nice seeing a DLC showing her and Vergils relationship in greater detail in the game itself. I didn't like Dante's look at first but it had nothing to do with the hair (after unlocking black hair Dante in DMC4 I used that for example), it was the fact his look in my opinion did't match the annoying personality but the look also evolved which was a clever way to make him likeable by the game's end. The combat difficulty of enemies was too simplistic once you figure out how to fight each new encounter (with the exception of the Vergil fight & Hollow Vergil in the DLC, those guys are cheap as on HOH & HAH). Finally the graphics were fine considering how fast paced the gameplay is but considering how recent it is I was surprised at the quality of the textures at times.
Summary:
A great hack and slash title that doesn't deserve the negative reviews, if it was an original concept I doubt 80% of those hate comments would even exist. I defintely would recommend the title for those new to the hack and slash genre, those who like a mix of fast paced gameplay with interesting enough story and love a grindy game you can play while doing something else at the same time. I would actually be curious to see a sequel to this title and I do feel it held it's own as a whole package but Ninja Theory original hack and slash Hellblade should do the genre justice without enraging the DMC fanbase again.

Ninja Theory's Devil May Cry is the Fifth installment if the Devil May Cry series, serving as a reboot. The game's story focuses on Dante (note that it is not the same Dante from previous installments) a young man who is a Nephilim: half-angel, hald-demon. He teams up with his twin brother Vergil on a quest defeat the Demon King Mundus who murdered their mother and condemned their father to banishment. Players can still use Dante's iconic weapons such as the Rebellion greatsword and the signature handguns Ebony and Ivory. The games has an okay story, not as good the original, but this has the best gameplay of the series. The sword gameplay and combo feels great and rewarding.

TLDR: Currently 6/10 Potential 9/10 - For a free game, well worth it.
This game is pretty unique in my opinion. It has elements unique to several game styles. You run around and hulk smash with your troll, have to manage your resources and workers like banished yet still having to defend your castle at the same time.
There are a few minor annoying bugs such as mobs on occasion spawning outside the map forcing you to surrender the battle. When it happens in survival, this causes you to lose obviously but in endless or the campaign, it's really nothing major other than losing loot for the round. Not a biggie.
The pathfinding for your troll is a bit clunky, sometimes he can't "find" his way to a wide open spot in a field and runs in circles. Still, not a biggie, just keep clicking.
I like how this is a free game with the only DLC option is for skins only. No pay to win.
I have not tried out the twitch stream interacting yet, but that feature looks pretty cool even just in concept, never seen that before.
This game does have a huge ammount of room for improvement as well. I can picture a ton of more things that could be put in. New buildings, higher upgrade levels, new troll types and/or abilities, etc.
All in all, well worth the fun!

Visually stunning - most times screenshots are showing just those "best looking" locations so the game sells well. Here it is the same, problem is - every location is "best looking". There's not even one second without being thrilled about amount of hard work game creators have put into it.

If You haven't bought this game yet then honestly, do it.

A perfect quintessential platforming experience.
The first thing that draws the eye to
is its beautiful art, and indeed playing this game is a feast for the senses, a 10 out of 10 on presentation alone. All the environments are gorgeously contructed and filled with luscious vibrant colours, the soundtrack is truly amazing and evocative, and the character animation is so fluid that controlling little Ori feels like a joy. All these elements combine to tell a simple but surprisingly emotional story that's reminiscent of early Ghibli movies, instilling a sense of awe for nature and having some earnestly moving moments.
When it comes to platforming the thing I appreciate the most is having a free sense of movement when controlling my character, and
more than delivers on that front. While it may not seem so at first, once you've unlocked enough abilities Ori can freely double jump, climb walls, air glide, propel herself through enemy projectiles, and just generally cavort though the air like a magic acrobat, with the controls being so responsive that navigating though levels feels both very entertaining and challenging. (And I'm not kidding about the challenging part, it really does get harder later on so be warned.) Plus there are enough secret nooks and crannies, locked paths, and three kinds of collectibles/upgrades to find, to make exploring the entirety of a map feel suitably metroidvania-y and keep you occupied.
As for the combat, the game mixes up things a little: instead of your own character spinning around stunning enemies, you attack through your little fairy companion. What this basically boils down to is smashing the attack button while trying to dodge enemy attacks at the same time, so you do need a minimum of effort to win fights. There are also special attacks you can unlock, and there's a decent enough variety of enemies, although at points they cluster so close together and respawn so quickly that walking around and backtracking can be a bit of a chore. I also wish it wasn't so easy to die, because no matter how many health upgrades you have getting hit 3 times in a row always kills you, which I found super frustrating.
But the thing that's actually unique to this game is the checkpoint mechanic, where instead of having automatic savepoints you have to manually spend some energy and create one yourself. This can lead to interesting tactics, like choosing to keep your energy for special attacks and risk longer journeys, or sacrificing your energy for the sake of frequent checkpoints and health regeneration. And even though saving after every difficult sequence soon becomes a matter of habit, I definitely had a few face-palming moments when I realised just how long it had been since my last save, so it's another aspect to keep track of.
I honestly can't think of any complaints about the game, except maybe that I wish there was more of it! I could have easily and happily invested 20 and more hours in the game, but the story wraps up at around 8 or 9. Yet despite the low number it feels like a complete and satisfying game, and it's hard to begrudge the devs for the short playtime when the things you
get to experience were so lovingly made. (And to be fair there are also quite a few achievements to hunt for although I'm not gonna lie, some were way too masochistic for me. Beating the entire game with one life on perma-death? No thanks!)
In any case,
is one of the best in its genre (in my opinion second only to Rayman Legends) and definitely worth a play if you like those kind of games.

There is so much right with this game; customization, free-roam game play, thirperson shooter, all of which I like, but at the same time, so much wrong. Little has been added to the game in way of permenant additions, since the game has been acquired from realtime worlds. There have been seasonal events, sure, but other than that, not much else. 4 end game contacts a very long time ago, aside from that, the only regular updates are patches, to attempt to fix balance issues and performance issues and the whole lot, and to the infamous armas store (which is the game's premium shop where you can buy many things for real life monies.) I don't really agree with the way the game's premium shop works, and that's another major flaw to this game, for me. The community is just horrible. There is a clear lack of moderation in the chats and it is apparent as people often hold obscene coversations, or just spurt out vulgar comments to other players for no good reason. I'm not sure weather it's that the game attarcts the worst kind of people or rather it just brings out the worst in people, but there is just so much wrong here. Gameplay wise, the game is somewhat hit or miss. There are times where you can sit down and play and have a great time. Other times, not so much. There are alot of unbalanced aspects to gameplay that people will abuse just to gain a win. Weapons aren't at all balanced, there are clear 'good' and 'bad' weapons, which only further drags the game down.
I can go on and on with all the reasons I feel that this game is not worth playing, but in a way, I somewhat do reccomend the game to people. If you have a group of friends, this game may be for you, but to just anyone looking to play by themselves, I would recommend to stay away.
I feel that I have fully experienced all this game has to offer me, and no, I do not recommend this game.

Unholy Heights is a tower defence game developed by Petit Depotto and published by AGM Playism who are also known for publishing "LiEat" and "One Way Heroics". Unholy Heights at the current time of this review  is listed as GBP 2.79 on the store.
From what I have played of this game I love the art style and the amount of different play style's that you can employ.  The game has various different tower defence and simulation elements in it and requires a fair bit of thinking to it.  The art style is quite a cute quaint style and the music fits in well with the whole experience.
There is a great amount of freedom in the game play with you able to choose the monsters you want  to be able to move into into your apartment as well as take quests whenever they suit you.  There is a fair amount of tactical elements to the game with trying to keep all your monsters happy as well as being effective defenders against the adventures.
Unholy Heights is an excellent little time killer and a game that can easily be played on a laptop of an evening and a couple of hours could be spent on it. The game play is incredibly simple with you building up your home and filling it full of different kinds of monsters to defend against the adventurers. Once you have figured out how to defend against the waves of adventurers you have to try and keep all your different monsters happy and can even make them fall in love and get them jobs!
In my opinion for how cheap the game is listed I think it is definitely a brilliant pickup to your steam library if you like tower defence games or are looking for a game which is easy to get into and you could spend a fair amount of time on.

The only thing that I find a shame about it, is that there's no ending for the game and, at least for now, there're not achievements nor trading cards available. Either way, it'd be really cool if there'd be some in the future. Overall, it's a casual tycoon experience and the price is really affordable, if you pick it up for playing, I hope that you may enjoy it as much as I did.

In an attempt to be a prequel to the Arkham series, Origins fails as a game which is unforgivable. The game is plagued with technical issues that will never be fixed. For example: during the combats as Batman, you can throw Batarangs or use one of the special takedowns and you could almost send the enemies flying off which eliminate any sense of "hey, I'm Batman but I'm not killing". Some of the animations are difficult to recognize as they may have way more reach and have a chance to punch your character. Some enemies are introduced too quickly with barely any context.
There are performance issues on my machine such as loading hiccups and frame drops. Even Arkham Knight, a game that was broken on release, didn't have that many issues on my system which is quite incredible. Some texture qualities are completely pixelated and some grapple points (spots that you would believe that you can grapple up) don't even work. There are things you can't climb on despite being able to in other areas.
Most of the secondary missions are recycled from Arkham City as well as several upgrades. While it is interesting to climb up with the Dark Knight System, some of the abilities can only be acquired if you complete secondary missions, some of them involving the assassins. And in later objectives, especially on Hard Difficulty, you'll struggle and since Predator Challenges involving the Dark Knight System can only be accomplished during the main story, you may be unable to complete the entire log on your first run.
Which leads to the biggest problem: the story. In one of the infamous cinematics, "Black Mask" is meeting up with the remaining assassins. Two of them, displayed on monitors, are part of the secondary missions and you can complete them (and stop these assassins) before the meeting. This cinematic is also pre-rendered (badly compressed) which means that the game crashes with its story at this precise moment. Now, it wouldn't matter for me since I tend to ignore stories in games but this is a blatant case of game designer and game writer not working alongside to make sure that the game makes sense when it happens. And most of the story or deductions from Batman as he attempts to solve mysteries are done through expositions in cinematics instead of us figuring out all the details.
While I appreciate the voice talent behind this game, the deliveries are cringe-level. What a shame because you would expect Troy Baker to pull off an excellent Joker but comes off as someone who tries too hard to be the next Mark Hamill. While I may appreciate that he cracks up a laugh during almost every line, this comes off as forced. Roger Craig Smith makes the Dark Knight completely unlikable thanks to his constant anger. I think the only one who can get away with praise is J.B. Blanc as Bane. Outside of his boss battle, Blanc delivers a calm yet menacing Bane without sounding too cliché. To be honest, if the entire story was centered around Bane vs. Batman for this "Origins", this would have been more cohesive as Bane seems to be a bigger threat the entirety of the city. Oh and the lip-syncing is terrible to say the least.
None of the screenshots provided on this store page represents the actual game. You're better off with Arkham Asylum if you're fresh into the series. Yet again, the game breaks the continuity by introducing gadgets that were never used IN Asylum such as the "sticky" grenade or the Grapnel Boost from Arkham City (Accelerator in Origins because why not). The Remote Claw you earn early in the game is basically the only new gadget but replaces the Line Launcher that has been limited in that regard. Oh and navigating this empty city made me miss the Batmobile from Arkham Knight which is quite special.
This game is the pure defition of a cash-in. Unless you need that Arkham experience, you can find better in Shadow of Mordor.

Ever played Batman Arkham Asylum or Batman Arkham City? if you did, you will pretty much remember how well the fighting system for this game is; Arkham Asylum the first game of the Arkham series, providing you with a Batman story in where Batman already known what is he doing, fighting crime and doing Batman stuff. But today we are talking about Arkham Origins which is not a continuation of Arkham City which was the second of the series, but like the name suggests is a prequel and it has a story of the first years of Batman being Batman.
One thing to keep in mind is that this game was not developed by Rocksteady Studios like the first too, but rather by Warner Bros Studios, therefore you cannot expect the same quality of game you had with the first two. They re-used a lot of assets of the previous games, specially the second game and added a few new things here and there, but they are really minimal.
As mentioned before the story in this game covers the first years of Batman being or doing Batman stuff; you will be able to tell why those are his first years in like the first 30 minutes of the game. I'll not disclose more detail about the story as I do not want to spoil it for you, but in my opinion can say the story is well done and entertaining. Another thing to mention, the story does not take place in the Arkham Asylum or the prison city the two previous game did, this time you are in Gotham City and being fair, if you played the second game you will find the map very familiar to what Arkham City was, of course, few new things here and there but nothing really amazing.
If you played the previous games you will not have any difficulty to get used to the controls nor the game mechanics like the fighting system or the detective work you do during the story. A few improvements here and there when it comes to the fighting system, is little more forgiving than the previous games, but you can also use the new items to make your combos more interesting and satisfying when facing the bad guys... the detective parts of the story were also enhanced, giving you the feeling of actually being the "world's greatest detective".
Yes, you read this right, there is a experience system included with this game in where you can get more fighting moves for Batman or just get extra abilities for some if not all of the gadgets which become useful as you progress through the game. You get experience by completing either the main content or the side content. Not really hard to level up at all, as long as you move with the story you will earn the sufficient experience to upgrade anything you need.
Fast Travel via the Batwing has been added to the game, of course you have to unlock the points where you can fast travel, but it makes really simply to move around Gotham once you have progressed through the story. Of course, you can still glide and use Batman's grappling hook to move around.
Like the previous game there is side content in the game which are pretty much little stories inside Gotham to expand even more with the Batman's Universe lore. Side content is taken as different cases Batman has to solve and each case is around 4 or 5 parts long. There is plenty of content to go around. Also, after you finish the game like the previous, you have the option to do New Game Plus, keeping everything you had from the game (excluding the gadgets you have to get in certain parts of the story); now the difference with this game is there is a new mode after you complete new game plus, which is the "I am the night" mode and it is pretty much, new game plus (enemies hit faster, no warning signs and you take more damage) but you have only one life to complete the main story, if you die you have to start all over again; of course, there is an achievement tied to this and have to say, you have to be really careful, specially with some of the boss fight to avoid dying in the most dumb way, like I did when I was going for the achievement... was like at 80% of completing game when a silly mistake in a boss fight made Batman die and thus had to start over.
Yes, this game has a multiplayer mode too. To be honest, I didn't played it too much, just tested a few times. But it is a competitive game mode in where you get into one of the three teams, the Heroes (Batman or Robin), the Joker gang or Bain's gang. You can level up your character and with levels you can get more perks and stuff during matches.
All in all, this is quite a good game if you like Batman or if you did like the previous games; even if you were expecting the same voice actors from the first and second game, the guys who did the characters voices do a pretty good job. Also, if you like kicking butts the Batman way, you can just get into the game to either free roam around Gotham City and get some of them or there are challenges to do so; like I mentioned before, there is a plenty of content to complete in this game and even a multiplayer mode if you like that kind of thing.

F1 2012 season was one of the best seasons in recent time with final race deciding Championship. In 2012 Vettel broke the record for the most pit-stops in the season
and equaled most races wins in a single season with Schumacher
In addition to seeing
, the 2012 season broke several records. The calendar for the season included twenty races, breaking the previous record of nineteen, which was first set in 2005. Six current or former World Drivers' Champions
started the season, breaking the record of five established in  The season also saw the return of Kimi Raikkonen, the
who finished 3rd at the end.
Fourth in installment from Codemasters game is pretty decent. Graphics are good even compared to some newer version of F1 games. The game features 20 circuits and 24 drivers battling for Championship title. Race through famous circuits such as Monaco, Spa, Monza, and Intergalos and become next World Champion. As you probably heard AI in this game aren't too much competitive compared to older versions, in fact in some cases they will let you overtake them, so I recommend You to search for some mods on the internet in order to have competitive cars to race against. Compare to some older versions F1 2012 is pretty decent and far better than F1 2011, there is some lack when it comes to comparing to F1 2010, which had very competitive AI cars but it had too much of an understeer. Although it's still enjoyable to play with new features such as Championship mode and Season Challenge.
Before You start a career you need to complete Young driver's test, It takes about 15-20 minutes after that you have been given few teams to choose between. Once you have chosen team You are given 7 seasons of career gameplay. Complete Team objectives, finishing at the top positions. beat Your Teammate and Your rival and completing R&D Objectives will help you get recognized from top tier teams. Some teams like Red Bull can recognize You faster than other teams like Mclaren or Mercedes. Race Your way to the top and beat top tier teams to win World Championship titles and Constructor's title.
You choose to start a team, depends on difficulty, if you choose easy you will be able to pick any team, If you choose hard, you will start will low tier teams. In Season Challenge you pick your rivals and try to beat them in best of 3, if you score 2 wins you will get a contract from that team, if you accept contract You will replace that driver and You gonna pick next rival. Season Challenge has only 10 circuits, 10 less than career and in that time You must beat all rivals you have chosen. There is One-Shot qualifying and Race is only 5 laps long, tyre wear is not affected!
Here You need to beat 7 World Champions from recent time, Kimi, Hamilton, Button, Vettel, Alonso, and Schumacher. Once You have beaten them all in their own challenges You are going to the Ultimate race where You are going to race them all at the Austin. Choosing difficulty will impact the medal you get, e.i. If you choose hard you will get a gold medal.
In Time Attack you have 6 different circuits, Valencia, Silverstone, Hockenheim, Suzuka, New Delhi and Austin.There You must beat time to get medals, better time better medal.
You try to beat Your own team at any circuit.
For the first time, You can do Online Co-Op where you and your friend battle to win DC, CC. You also have ranks, you get exp by racing, if you had clean lap you will receive 5 exp, If you finish where your team wanted You to finish you will also get additional Exp, but if you collide with other people or finish below team expectations You will lose exp.
F1 2012 is a great game, game graphics and pretty good and engine sound is well better than those V6 engines. The game is worth buying if You are into F1 or like racing games.

Though a relatively short game depending on how much you love it, OTA is a good game with interesting concepts but many ways to improve. The graphics are surprisingly good for a game running on Unity despite the minor performance problem I have encountered and has a gameplay reminiscent of an RTS game I have played long ago (and have forgotten the title). I like the game because it's somewhat an RTS(in a strange direction, you be the judge) and the combat is pretty epic especially when your troll is at max level.
To sum up the gameplay, it's like TD but the castle you are defending is at the center, improving it over time with resources and defending it with a troll that can level up and some orcs that you can hire. You manage your goblin resource (engineer/multiple resource gathering) via slider and do as much stuff as you can before the next wave attacks your castle. The game has inconsistent difficulty issues however, as your troll/fortress is hammered early on especially on harder difficulties and there is barely any way to get out of it especially when you are a big slow troll. My only advice is focus on cheap buildings first that adds your goblins and construct those towers and upgrade walls fast. Very short experience, but for free the game is pretty good.

One bright and sunny morning, Meat Boy left his home in Sunnyville, Meatland. Sunnyville was, coincidentally, a bright and sunny town. The people barked loudly, the dogs were nice, chickens squealed with laughter, and children bawked and layed eggs. All was well in Sunnyville.
Meat Boy ran quickly down the block three houses to meet his pink friend, Bandage Girl. The two were infinitely happy to see each other and made out in front of her house for the next few months. Finally, after Meat Boy had grown a beard and Bandage Girl had somehow died and resurrected three times, they came to the conclusion that they should spend the rest of their time together out in the forest, alone.
You're probably noticing that some things are wrong with Sunnyville; indeed, the people and dogs, and children and chickens were all getting mixed up, and somehow Meat Boy and Bandage girl were able to make out for an extremely long period of time. These aren't the only things wrong with Sunnyville, however; what may be sunny side up can also have a rather dark side to it; one may call it the Dark World of that place.
The dark side of Sunnyville was the ominous intruder Dr. Fetus, a superbly well named fetus inside a jar wearing apparel that gives him the distinct look of someone with a Dr. before their name. Dr. Fetus was, for unkown reasons, obsessed with Bandage Girl and so kidnapped her right before Meat Boy's eyes, teleporting into an alternate dimension where Doctor's and fetuses roam free, yelling at each other for stereotypes and throwing mooing bowler hats at everything that moves. This is where Meat Boy's journey begins.
It just so happens that Dr. Fetus leaves Bandage girl at various places within the forest, and that just when Meat Boy reaches her, Dr. Fetus swoops down and teleports her somewhere else. Super Meat Boy depicts this and the rest of his journey, though don't ask me why they named him Super, since he can't even save his girlfriend from Dr. Fetus for a good 20 hours. Anyway, this goes on and Meat Boy follows his girlfriend through different places, out of Sunnyville, and even into the depths of hell.
It should also be noted that throughout his loyal journey, Meat Boy encounters various bosses, most of which are ignorant pieces of crap that have no respect for life, especially Meat Boy's. When he finally reaches the end of his journey, the "game" ends and you receive a little black window in the bottom right hand corner of your screen telling you you got something for it. However, you are basking too much in your own ego to care at that point, so just forget about it.
However, Meat Boy's journey teaches us many a valuable lesson. For example: make sure to save up on cash, cause you'll be buying new controllers after your old ones go out the window. Resist the temptation to sue Edmund for trashing your home just from your own rage. Go play some MMOGs (which, by the way, stands for My Meat [Boy] Of Glory, pronounced MOG, and should not be confused with MAUG, which means nothing), because diehard platformers like this one are so good they're bad, and vice versa. And listen to game descriptions; "a tough as nails platformer" is pretty accurate. It's also sharp as nails, which you'll learn when you stick a couple in your eyes after playing this.
If you've made it this far into the review, CONGRATULATIONS! You've acquired a hard-earned, 110% legit, totally-not-found-from-some-dumpster-behind-your-local-taco-bell (some sketchy stuff going on behind those restaurants), Meat Boy PUPPY STICKER! Anyway, <Insert witty closing comment here>, and I'll see you next time, on: FOX News! The most reliable and random news channel on cable!

If you want an in-depth review that isn't extremely lengthy but covers what you'll probably want to know, continue reading.
Let me start off by saying that I played this game when it's Beta released from it's original developers, Real Time Worlds. They went under and the game shut down. GamersFirst picked the game up and transformed it into a Free 2 Play game. I couldn't be more happy to see it return as I enjoyed the game very much during its initial release and having it now be a F2P game could make it even better.
This happened in some ways, and some not so much. The gameplay definitely won't appeal to everyone, but with it being a F2P game, may as well try it out, right? Before you do, maybe this review will help you decide.
First off, the game's customization is awesome. I haven't seen any other game like it. There's a symbol creator that you can, if you have a wide enough imagination, literally create anything you want with the provided shapes, pre-made graphics, letters, etc. You can warp the decals, rezise, color, fade and rotate them to your liking. When you're satisfied with your symbol, you can save it and place it on your character's clothing, on your character's skin as a tattoo, or on your vehicle. This, on top of the character customization (much like the SIMS, with height, weight, facial features customizer) really allows you to be what ever kind of character you want in the game. Like any Free 2 Play game, you'll have to pay to unlock higher tier items or more symbol layer slots to create more advanced graphics for your character. A free account is not limited enough to make it not worth while; give it a try!
Moving on to the initial startup experience. You'll be promted with a login screen when you load up the game. You'll need to sign in through your GamersFirst account or log in through Steam. Once you're in, you'll get to the character selection window and select your character. You'll then be prompted with a district selection window. Clicking one of the large tiles will auto select a district for you. This typically isn't the best solution to use once you are used to the game. I suggest going to the District selection tab for a more advanced search of where to play. Most instances are limited to 90 or 100 players. This is a pretty decent amount of players per instance in my opinion. When you've found an instance to connect to, you'll be sent in and spawn shortly in the map.
Moving on to the gameplay. Most people will argue that the gameplay is horribly unbalanced and that it's a heavily Pay 2 Win (P2W) game. While some areas are unbalanced, it's not completely unplayable otherwise there wouldn't be anyone playing it. As for P2W, this is not the case. There is a marketplace called ARMAS. You buy permanent weapons from this marketplace for real money. These weapons can be created using in-game cash earned from missions and bought through contacts. Each weapon can have up to 3 modifications put into it to advance it's abilities. If anything, the paid weapons from ARMAS just create less of a hassle, saves time and allow newbie players to get on a level somewhat even with the more advanced players. The gameplay is definitely different than most games. As I'm sure you've seen by now, it's a third-person shooter, which has its ups and downs. You can wall peak without having the enemy know, so if they're coming around a corner at you, you have the full upper hand on them, unless they decide to run back and forth and you miss every shot and they happen to kill you first (which happens a lot). Overall, the gameplay is decent and I've enjoyed it over the years I've played this game.
Overall, I recommend that you at least try this game. Don't give up straight away because you can't kill anyone, that's going to happen if you're a newbie player. Try grouping up with some higher level players or get a few friends to join in and work as a team. Use voice communication and work together to defeat the opposition. This game relies heavily on great teamwork.

Seriously probably my favorite game on Steam right now.  The game world is insanely fleshed out, with literally paragraphs of text about every imaginable part of the city.  The city really feels alive, with people walking around and the dynamic of other players that you see everywhere lending to the feeling of really being in San Paro, and as an Enforcer, really wanting to protect the city.  The combat is awesome, and is literally the favorite of any shooter I have played.  The third person view makes for some intense fights, with vantage points, corners and a well balanced team helping out immensly, and making acting as a team extremely important.  The community is rich, vibrant and involved, with many members making amazing customs designs for vehicles and contributing to the game culture and story by customizing themselves and their cars with really intricate, professional-looking and amazing designs.  The cars and guns are all very unique and cater to many different play styles, with an LMG feeling very different and using a much different strategy than shotguns, and having one of each is extremely handy.  Character modifications also help, with each strengthening the specializations you can have, but are not necessary to winning or to playing, as both the starting gun and car are actually good enough that you don't need to buy the next tiers if you don't want (many high-tier players still use the Star (the first gun) later in the game).  Yet each new car and gun feels very cool, and are great incentives for increasing levels.  Each new contact has a unique backstory, and the new items are actually exciting, as some of the coolest cars and guns can be a lot of fun to unlock and use for the first time, and each new (and more prestigious) contact that you couldn't talk to before seem cool and exciting, and makes the sense of progression extremely satisfying.  The whole game can be played without buying anything with real money or having premium, and the game is nowhere close to a pay to win, with each gun and car always being balanced by another, and almost all can be purchased with in-game cash in a very reasonable amount.  The game is very, very fair, and paying money is usually just for cool stuff that could be unlocked anyways, with the aesthetic value serving as the impetus, not the over-poweredness.  Almost all can be unlocked in game, and the higher-tier premium players are indistinguishable from those that are free to play, as both have the same benefits for the most part and most of the elite items are unlocked with high-level contacts.  Everything about this game is solid, well thought out and rich in both depth, story, and game feel, and the controls of driving and shooting are seamlessly integrated into what is my favorite game of all time.  I've had hundreds of hours just having fun with friends, driving around the streets of San Paro having a blast racing, shooting and delving deeper into the amazing world Reloaded Studios has created.  This game is amazing, and I love it.  I can only give it the highest possible recommendation.  If you're thinking about getting it, get it.  If you're not, still do.  This is the most solid game I have ever played, and is also the most fun.  I love APB :D

Having gotten the game despite a certain amount of negativity surrounding it -at least compared to the others in the Arkham series which itself appears to place Origins somehow outside of itself, despite repeatedly referencing and/or mimicking the events and gameplay introductions of this game in the later Knight instalment- I found myself enjoying the experience. Granted, Batman is a bit... brattier, one might say, at this early point in his personal development, but he's getting there, and perhaps that is in fact more interesting than him already being there. Decide for yourself.
The combat is kind of janky, for lack of a better word. It feels unresponsive and vaguely wrong in subtle ways, compared to the other instalments of the series. Apparently it was recreated from scratch by the new developers brought in by WBGames, in order to... well, I don't know, but it all seems to have boiled down to a pretty decent, if somewhat hollow Mad Max game being made with essentially the same, still-janky brawl mechanics, so mystery solved, I guess?
I digress. Arkham Origins is, to me, a mostly worthy addition to the series. The detective work is more fun than in any other Arkham game -you've got crime scene recreations in real time, the challenge of meticulously picking apart a moving three-dimensional scene and extracting insights; it's like the hyper-tech cop in Heavy Rain or something. Fun stuff, and it lends some nice heft to Da Bat's "World's Greatest Detective" title.
There are still thugs to artfully smack about, and without wanting to spoil, there is a pair of awesome gloves which are like coating your fists with distilled awesomesauce. Jankiness aside, it's still fun, the villains are colorful, the gliding feels special, plus you get to see the areas of Arkham City before they got all smashed up and smeared in dirt and grime! Along with some new areas.
Takes place on christmas eve and morning, too. So, the ultimate question becomes... "Do you want to spend christmas with Batman?"

Decent entry in the Batman series, that can basically be summed up as: Batman Year 2.  No bullet proof vest and ski masks for Bruce Wayne - you've got your assortment of gadgets, and nice-looking batsuit...you even have the Batwing which allows fast travel between sections of the city.  The only thing missing is the legend.  As you start out, the street criminals don't believe you exist, and the cops are treating you as another bad guy to get off the streets.
The story begins with a prison break, and as you battle your way through the cells, you learn that Black Mask has hired 8 assassins to kill the Batman.  These are faces you'll recognize both from the comics as well as other games in the series.  Killer Croc, Deadshot, Deathstroke, Bane, etc.  Each will pop up at various times in the story, often causing your real target to get away while you have to stop and deal with the latest threat.  Eventually, Batman triumphs, and like the previous games, you're able to go around and gather any collectibles and complete any side missions that you didn't complete the first time around.
The game takes place in Gotham in the middle of a snowstorm, and in addition to the story missions, you'll have the opportunity to stop crimes in progress, deal with Riddler challenges, stopping Anarky from blowing up the city, and even solving one of Gotham's oldest unsolved murders.  The map is much more compact that Arkham City, and being able to unlock fast travel points (and even return the Batcave!) is a nice addition.  The biggest addition to the series is the actual exmaination of crime scenes.  By finding and investigating distinct pieces of evidence, you're able to view a simulation of the crime and figure out what happened and what you need to do next.  This is the first time in the series that you feel like "The World's Greatest Detective".

This game is kind of a mixed bag for many people, however I feel it is honestly a very good game, about on par with Arkham Asylum, but not on the level of Arkham City.
First of all, it has by far the best boss battles in the series, bar none. Previously, the series' boss fights largely devolved into throwing a batarang at the 8 foot tall guy and dodging to the left. However in Origins, the boss fights throw in some real variety, like the counter-heavy Deathstroke fight, the combat endurance fight with Bane, and the urgent battle with Firefly. Of course, these are not on the same level as the Mr. Freeze or even the Ra's Al Guhl fight in some ways from Arkham City, but they are leagues ahead of the disgusting Bane and Joker fights in Asylum and literally every boss fight in Arkham Knight.
Secondly, I am a big fan of many of the enemies added to the series. The addition of Deathstroke was very welcome, as it finally introduced a character who is a physical equal to Batman. I also like this game's Riddler, as his character shows how his insecurities comcerning Batman makes him transition from blackmialing corrupt officials to kidnapping and murdering. Some of his motivations make little sense (like why he would leave his extortion files lying around the city) but his motivations are much better than those in Arkham Knight, in which he builds racetracks for no reason. This game also seeks to add new villains to the mythos and to not use already established characters as a crutch (as Arkham Knight does with the Joker). This game also has probably the best portrayal of James Gordon; I know that this gGordon is radically different than what Gordon is supposed to be like, but its the only time he has felt like a rational, fleshed out character. Asylum's version was done well, but didn't really give Gordon any chance to shine, Gordon basically was not even in City, and Knight's protrayal was almost offensively bad, as Gordon is basically a plot device wasting a talanted actor's time. I also loved Bane in this game; his motivations as a character are honestly dumb (as he wants to kill Batman to find "peace" somehow), but he is finally the character he should be, an intellectual equal and physical superior to Batman, a man who is able to
. The only problem with this is that the status quo needed to be returned by the end of the game, so it is conviently forgotten by a plot device. This "convienence" actually ends up working to the series' advantage though, as
. Also, many people cite The Joker as being a needless addition to the story and is completely different to the Joker in the other games; I completely disagree. The Joker shown in this game is one without a real purpose in the world, similar to Heath Ledger's Joker at the beginning of The Dark Knight; they both are searching for someone who percieves the world as they do (Batman), and are causing crimes to bring that person out of the shadows. Other than that, the only major difference between this Joker and that in the first two games is the voice actor.
I do have some MAJOR gripes with this game though, those being the game presenting almost no real challenge, and the simple fact that this game didn't bring as much innovation to the table as other games gameplay wise (other than the shock gloves). It may just be my familiarity with the series, but I was able to blast through the game on Hard dying twice (both times to snipers), and getting about halfway through NG+ dying once (as of time of this review). There was even one time where, when sneaking into the GCPD, I was crossing over a room with about 14
guards, and I decided to just jump down and see if I could defeat them, just for fun. And I did. Relatively easily too. I should have been killed almost instantly, but guns (other than snipers) barely do any damage once you upgrade your armor a bit. The combat essentialy boild down to batclawing enemies, jumping over some, and (by the end of the game) beating on someone until you can activate the shock gloves and KO 12 enemies in 30 seconds. On the subject of gadgets, this game basically adds nothing (other than the shock gloves). The glue grenade is the freeze grenade from City, the concussion detonators are a worse version of the REC, and the remote claw is a slight variation on the line launcher. There is one positive gameplay addition worth mentioning though, the matrial artist. It really shakes up combat (especially in NG+), as it forces players to pay attention to who they are fighting and not just check out during fights with less than 10 people. The addition of crimes in progress and crime scenes is very welcome as well, as they both tap into aspects of Batman that previous games hdan't explored, those being Batman's detective skills and fighting lower levels of crime. The crime scenes do largely turn into looking for the red triangle, but they at least try to tap into that aspect of Batman's character. I will admit that Arkham Knight did this particular aspect better, but Origins laid the groundwork, and Knight's system would not exist without the feedback from Origin's. Arkham Origin's side missions also all play into the main story of the game. Not to say that City's side missions were bad, but it adds a certain level of spectacle to the main story when you see how its impacts have led to various side missions, such as
.
All in all, this game is done well, but it's attempts at innovating the gameplay are largely redundant and make the game far less challenging. Its changes to characters and story are very welcome though, as they add layers of depth to characters and generally support the story. Still though, I'd much rather have a game that tried to do a lot and failed in places than a game that was completely by the numbers

I just spent 119 hours in this game getting all the achievements, including multiplayer. I'm a little burned out by it lol. I'd like to add that a decent chunk of this time, maybe 15-20 hours was from waiting in multiplayer lobbies and screwing around, along with entering the combat simulator way too early. I wasn't aware that your gadgets and unlocks carried on with you into the simulator, so I was trying to get these really high scores in the hardest way possible, thus leading to a large chunk of game time added.
But regardless, I enjoyed it a lot. The only other Batman game I've played is Arkham Asylum, and while I kind of liked the narrow scope of that more, I enjoyed the story and atmosphere a lot more in Origins.
So, the story itself was great. I like the reveal of
. All my complaints with the story are technical ones, I hated how the pre-rendered cutscenes were at some muddy resolution on my PC, and I especially hated the stifness of the NPCs (and Batman) when talking. I remember accepting it in Asylum because the game was the first in the series, and it's from 2009, etc etc...but man, Origins came out in 2013, and it's really off-putting to see stiff, motionless characters talking. It's even worse in the Cold, Cold Heart DLC, at some points its literally just mouths moving, and nothing else. There's a really good scene in the base game, where
that was really well done, and it baffled me why the rest of the game couldn't have moments like that during the cutscenes that weren't pre-rendered.
The amount of collectables in this game is also ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Like, just absolutely stupid. And the "challenge mode" features a bunch of maps that are all just stripped from the story, so it's not very exciting. On top of that, some of these challenges are just repeated over and over again. There's a "campaign mode" where it's just three of the previous challenges in a row. The multiplayer is also pretty bad and unnecessary. It's kind of a cool idea, but it's not something that's accessible, nor in-depth enough to warrant your time. I played it purely for 100% achievements.
In the end, despite it's shortcomings, I'd still say Arkham Origins is a good game, especially for the story and setting, and is worth playing through for those two items despite a lot of the negative backlash it has received. I'd give it a 7.0. The Season Pass isn't worth it, you should be able to get the only relevant DLC (Cold, Cold Heart) for cheaper, but I've seen all the Arkham games bundled together (minus Knight) with all add-ons for like 10$ USD so it's not much money.

If you don't have a TV and wireless controllers, use a projector 4 keyboards, or game controllers - they're $10 on ebay, or mix and match.

Well, let's begin with the things that are good about this game:
1) Is pretty.
2) Sounds nice.
Ok, now let's talk about how this game fails on every level.
1) Let's start with the less important stuff - The Story. My God.
I haven't finished the game, and I'm not going to, but from what I've seen so far...
Well the game starts you with 2 characters. You spend, like, 2 minutes with them and then one of them dies and the other one (the white furry thing that you play as) feels sad.
Oh no. How could this happen. I'm going to cry - better bring a bucket. Look how much I care about this lumbeing thing I've just met.
And the game really wants you to feel sad. Like, you spend the next minute or two trying to SLOWLY walk the white furry thing (TWFT for short) to the bloody checkpoint so you can start playing the game. Like... no! No, I don't care that it's friend\parent\whatever just died! I don't cae about this charcter! I've spent no time with it! Jesus Christ!
That's the only part that stood out to me becaue of how laughable it was. The rest is just generic.
2) Ok, jokes are over, let's actually talk about the Gameplay.
Combat: So, the good thing about the combat system in this game is that it's very unique. That's the only good thing I can say about it. Otherwise it's a total horror show.
So... you aren't exactly fighting - magical flying orb with not-exactly-apparent range does it for you. So you're running around your opponents while masing that "X" button... sounds fun? No? Because it's not.
Every fight is pretty much the same, there is no strategy, and every single enemy takes a billion hits and there is almost no way to increase your damage output. Basically, it's more fun to try and avoid enemies altogether. Seriously! It's more fun to try to beat the game as a "pacifist". Probably faster, too...
Platforming: So... this game takes platforming very seriously. It kinda tries to be Super Meat Boy, honestly. I wouldn't have a problem with that if it wasn't for two things:
a) TWFT kinda does whatever it wants sometimes. For exmple, if you hit the ledge just right it'll propell itself upwards and forwards (basically, it'll climb the ledge), despite you never telling it to... which is fun to look at, but NOT fun to control while in the middle of a platforming section!
b) "Oh, those are spikes. Ok. Cool. Wish I knew that before landing on them". You can't make a game that looks like this and make it a hardcore platformer! I can barely discern between what I can stand on and what I fall right through!
It's not always obvious what hurts you and what doesn't and even if you do figure it out, the hitboxes are very ambiguous.
Finally, the thing's movement is... weird in general. The speed at which it moves changes pretty much however it pleases. I cannot figure it out. But that is probably just a personal problem, I'm sure there's logic behind its movement...
Misc: So, apparently, in order to progress you have to spend experience points on buying certain skills. There is an obligatory exp spending. Woooooooow.
It wasn't a problem for me at all, because I was lucky to have purchased the right skill at just the right time, but I quickly realized that had I not taken that particular path, I'd have to GRIND. GRIND in an artsy platformer with really bad combat system. Jesus Christ Almighty...
Also, exploring is never worth it. It's actually NEVER worth it. Oh, you beat a really hard platforming section, spiced up by some tough enemies? That's great! You get... NOTHING. You'll need to come back later when you have upgrades that make this section a lot easier and make it possible to progress beyond this point. Stupid! You're so stupid! Look at your stupid face, you just wasted your time, for NOTHING!
That happened a LOT to me. After a certain point I just gave up and tried to follow "the main path" as much as possible.
Conclusion: It's not the worst game I've ever played, but there is no way I can recommend it.

To start, I am very on the fence about ABP Reloaded. The techniques used by Gamersfirst are not what I would expect from a dev, but I'm not them so I have no opinion from their POV.
The overall gameplay of it is quite fun and can bring you hours upon hours of fun...
Chasing after some criminals you just saw smash their van into a jewlery story and robbed it dry can be immense fun. Or perhaps you're the one who just mugged a drug dealer walking down the street, you now have to sell the drugs, and launder the cash all while avoiding the keen eye of the hackers you are playing against. Oops I meant cops... my bad.
Though it lacks in variety during your gaming experience (Your variety of objectives is quite limited). It is still a cops vs robbers game. Like when you were a child, only now it is virtual. The amount of detail though, is rather high. It has a built in "photoshop" where players can fully customize and design graphics for nearly any item you can aquire. The game has a built in community auction house for buying/trading your cars and guns or anything you want, between other players.
You have the ability to import your own music (Or you could when I played last), which is refreshing. Listening to whatever you want.
The graphics, depending on your hardware can range from sufferable to quite fantastic. It's no farcry 3 but with a quality PC you will have a hard time not enjoying yourself atleast a little. Not including bugs/glitches that come with the game, you will come across your fair share of hackers... It does ruin the experience. Not to mention... but i'm going to... Gamersfirst has consistently released patches that were... broken to say the least and I feel on a personal level, that the attitude the devs show towards the game has possibly scared some players away. It has done that to me in the past.
In my not-so-humble opinion, It feels to me as if the game tries to lure you in. Once you've invested enough time and effort into hittting a certain rank, that the only way to further yourself is to become a premium member... I mean why not, you get not only almost double the Exp/$ per mission, but you also get a 50% reduced cooldown on your abilites (Wait... you pay for that passive skill?) plus a whole bunch of other junk to sweeten the deal, which in return will make you stronger. But then you will also need the premium guns, to match your bad-assness, which don't come with the premium service... but atleast you get a 20% discount in the micro-transaction store, to intice you to spend more real life currency. Sweet deal eh? Nah... I don't reccomend you buy premium unless you are truly going to invest time into the game.
Customization - 8/10
Story - 5/10
Music - 9/10 (Import your own :))
Gameplay - 6/10
Graphics - 7/10
Overall I would recommend this game to anyone who has player cops vs robbers as a child and wants to expand that experience into a virtual one.

Really a gorgeous metroidvania-esque 2-D adventure game.The art design and music of this game is truly astounding. All that being said this game does have some weird issues.
The most annoying thing about this game is that it lacks clarity. As bright and colorful as this game maybe sometimes its difficult to tell where ori is as her model can blend into certain backgrounds. It only happens sometimes but when it does more then likely youre going to die or get wounded. The other major clarity issue is with enemy projectiles as they too can be difficult to spot at times because their colors blend in again with the background. Sometimes its also difficult to tell whether its an enemy projectile or your own fairy friend. Same thing can occasionally happen with environmental hazards like spikes etc. Ori's character model is also pretty small so some platforming puzzles get a bit annoying to finish.
The last problem I have with this game is that it relies a bit too much on DEATH. A lot of the levels are designed so that u have to depend on the save mechanic (wherein you leave behind a marker to which you will respawn upon dying) and actually dying several times in order to complete them. When I say dying several times I mean it! In 10 hrs of playing this game I died close to 400 times and that can get pretty frustrating. In reference I died close to 100 times in my 80hr playthrough of Dark Souls 3. One can always 'git gud' but I know for a fact lot of people just want to relax with a game like this.
In CONCLUSION, if you want a gorgeous art style, some nice orchestra music and really creative levels as well as abilities get Ori in the blind forest. If you're looking polished mechanics, combat more content and a bit less platforming get Hollow Knight instead.

I hate this game, but it's like a love to hate, hate to love kind of relationship. My kids and I have played it and let me tell you, It is so much easier with a controller. We worked together to figure out how to get past the obstacles and really it was fun. But man Team Meat sure knows how to frustrate you to no end. If you like challenges then this game is for you. I can say that this game does make you think how to map out your moves and you may try, fail, try and fail and try and fail many times to get past a level, but when you do beat it, it's worth it to say the least. It's a punishing game if you don't have good reflexes. I don't recommend it for people with carpal tunnel or anyone who is older like me, who can't act as fast as they used to. :D Because you do have to act fast with your mind and fingers. And if you're not patient, you'll be expressing words  you never knew existed...
TLDR:
Graphics: Cute and clear. The characters were amusing as well as the backgrounds.
Sound: Cute as well and matches the theme and story well.
Story: Well Meat Boy's girlfriend was kidnapped by the good ole Dr. and it's up to you to get her back. You have to get past obstacles, sometimes with good timing, luck and good reflexes but you do get the girl in the end.
Playability: Depends on who you ask. My kids had a better time at doing the levels where you had to go fast through it where I couldn't seem to react fast enough. It's not hard, just frustating sometimes. And it's not impossible. It's learn as you go. I did better with an XBox controller though, so that might be something to think about doing.
REplayability: We never touched this game again. Even though it was good. Like I said love to hate, hate to love.
Overall if you're not sure, watch gameplay videos on it from people who have played and see what you think. It's not as good as actually trying it out, but it will give you a feel on what type of game it is.
I recommend it to people who love challenges, because it will challenge you to no end. It's not a bad game, just not my typical type of game. I don't mean for this to sound like a negative review, because this game is just not my type of game as I said, but people who like to maybe punish themselves and love challenges well check it out because it will be your type of game.

The Apotheosis Project is a point-and-click adventure game where you play as two agents from a secret organization. The adventure begins as they find themselves unwilling participants in a secret project. During the course of the game, you can switch back and forth between the 2 playable characters to solve puzzles, interact with the environment in different ways, and each agent has their own personality and different take on different situations.
I didn't love this game, but I didn't completely hate it either. I enjoyed it enough to finish it, but I doubt I'll be going back for any missed achievements. I'd say it was a pretty bland 5/10. It would be easiest just to break it down into some quick pros and cons.
Pros:
- Looks great, nice UI, and ran smooth with no bugs.
- Story is well done and I really enjoyed the clever ending.
- Interesting point/score system and lots of secret achievements.
- Some humorous dialogue that got a laugh out of me.
- Length of 5 hours was good for the price.
Cons:
- With the exception of Aaron, the voice acting was terrible to the point of being distracting.
- Poor puzzle design, especially in Chapter 3 which was simply awful.
- Too much pixel hunting in some areas.
- Too much inventory clutter and unused items.
- The agents supposedly have "special powers" but it's only utilized a few times in the entire game.
Overall, it's a great story that is somewhat tarnished by horrible voice acting (I honestly recommend just turning it off) and some rather poor puzzle design. It's nothing exceptional, but it's not completely terrible. If anything, get it on a sale, and just play it once for the story.

I had no idea what to expect when I first got this game.
It turned out to be quite alright.
Project Apotheosis sounds puzzling. The game is a bit harder than it appears to be at first, because of how it's meant to be played.
In this game, two agents are controlled (it's up to the player to switch when desired/needed).
If one forgets about this, it's easy to get stuck (happened to me!).
It is advised to let both characters interact with the environment and examine any gathered items so as to progress.
Gathered items can also be handed over back-and-forth between the two of them when necessary.
Some objects can only be picked up by either of them, so it's important to be thorough!
According to the game logic, this is because both agents have their own speciality and personality (as in; one being more thorough in some way than the other).
Another thing I found really neat, was this 'follow' option, where one main character (automatically) follows the other, when this command is clicked (if this isn't activated, what happens is whichever character isn't controlled at that given time, stays behind).
Some elements of the game are a bit confusing (especially story-wise). It's just that I'm very keen on logic & consistency, so I really had to do my best to keep an open mind while playing this game.
It did however make sense, so I found it somewhat satisfying.
The music was quite fitting. I enjoyed the minimalistic, yet atmospheric effect.
Also any sound effects in game were very basic, but good enough.
There was one puzzle involving portals and 2 control panels that I didn't have the patience to solve without the use of a walkthru due to the lack of sound in game.
This puzzle is of the trial-and-error type, where you keep trying and trying till you find the right combination to unlock several portals (without any sound to confirm whether you got any of the combinations right, and that means running back and forth...).
As for the intro music... well I guess that's always a personal thing ey? I wasn't too fond of the vocals (classical, opera-style, quite dramatic), though I did like the music. It was a bit over the top for my taste.
And this goes for the voice-acting as well. Especially the female character (i.e. agent Penelope Barker), had me wanting to scratch my face in agony at times (I unfortunately found it rather mediocre, but not the worst I've heard).
Quite an odd accent as well, and the intonation was really off at times.
Some words seemed to be mispronounced (even Apotheosis). That was quite a downer. I have to admit though, that I found the voice-acting sounding a lot more natural as I progressed further. So it might have been a matter of the actors needing time to 'adjust' to their role.
On the brighter side; I did like the portrayal of the male character a lot more (i.e. agent Aaron Reid). I enjoyed his sense of humour. Quite dry. Just my thing :).
I guess these kind of details are a hit-or-miss. Either you like it, or you just don't. The game did seem to lack a bit of visual finesse. It seemed a bit rough. It was good enough for me, despite the fact it looked outdated for a game that was released in 2014. I was quite surprised by that.

Ori and the Blind Forest is absolutely stunning on all fronts.
Visually, the game is GORGEOUS. Each area is unique and interesting, which made me look forward to each new section of the game. The music is equally incredible, and I found myself moved to tears at how beautifully the visuals and audio compliment each other.
Gameplay-wise the controls for Ori are very tight and well-polished. Every time that I failed it was always because of how I was controlling the character, not because of an oversight in how the game was made. New skills are slowly added to your arsenal as you progress in the game, which keeps the gameplay fresh. Sometimes you'll even go back to an old area with your new abilities and think "oh! The characters were extremely charming, the story was moving, the enemies were varied, the platforming was fun and fair (although hard at some points!).

I really want to like this game, but I just don't.  Here is what's up:
+Music
The music is very good and suits the game really well.  I can see myself listening to the sound track outside of the game.
+Graphics
The game has some stunning visuals and all around looks great.
+Bash Mechanic
The bash mechanic is super fun.  This kept me playing when I might have otherwise stopped.
+Save System
They have a cool take on saving (except when you can't).
- Controls (PS4 controller)
To get my PS4 controller to work I had to specifically play the Definitive Edition and then go into a .txt file and remap keys.  I should not have to do this.  Also, and I'm not sure if this is a PS4 controller problem specifically, but when you get the abillity to super jump, doing so cancels your R2 press, meaning if you do this into wanting to grab a wall or float with the feather you have to unpress and press the button again.  This wouldn't be such a problem for me if not for the fact that you can otherwise hold R2 down and it works like you would expect.  This was the worst for me in the third shrine's finale.
- Unfair One Shots / Instant Kill Areas / Hidden Spikes / Enemies
This game has a ton of unfair one shots / instant kill areas with no explanation of how they work.  I literally died over 10 times in one place and didn't know why until I died in such a way that I could see that there were spikes hidden in an area you can't see until Ori's position reveals it.  It is a good thing you can save (almost) anywhere because it was stupid how often this happened to me.  I found on more than one occasion that enemies or projectiles blended into the world and I couldn't see what I was supposed to be dodging and what I was okay to collect.  Maybe this was a bigger issue because I was playing on hard so more things one shot me but damn if it wasn't frustrating.
- Linear
The game is sort of open world but you can't collect any power ups or do anything meaningful in an area until you're supposed to be there.  I struggled to explore areas a few times only to find out I could do literally nothing there and then had to struggle back out which bothers me immensely.
- Too many places where the game won't let you save
I don't have a problem with not being able to save when enemies are nearby, or when the ground is unstable, that is fine.  I think throughout my playthrough twice I got an error message saying that the zone wasn't safe so I couldn't save, and I thought that this was definitely due to them not being able to make sure you could spawn safely.  All of the other times this happened it just♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥me off.  Why make an amazing save system and then take it away when I literally want to use it the most.  Couple this with the instant death areas you can't see coming (like in the final section where you float upwards and meteors come down).  Although I think the shrine finales shouldn't let you save, the other problems I had in them prevented me from enjoying them.
- Three shrine finales
I think these might have been cooler if I didn't die so many times to things I didn't feel were my fault, like not being able to see something that isn't on the screen or the controls not doing what I want them to.  I had lots of deaths in this game that were 100% my fault but way, way too many I didn't feel were my fault.
I'll play a sequel hoping they fix what I hated but now that I'm done I'll never play this again.

Astroneer is a very relaxing space/planet survival game.
It's in super early access (pre alpha IIRC) right now, but the base game looks very nice, and plays well (for a while, check below for more info).  The devs are frequently squashing bugs, and bringing out updates, so at the moment the game's not the typical "early access but maybe we'll release maybe not".
With the current state it's in (as of this review), you can get upwards of 10 hours out of it, before you either run out of things to do, or the game decides to drop your FPS because of lack of optimization (it's only a couple of weeks into its current stage, so I'm giving it the benefit of the doubt) and you have to start again.
Thankfully the planets are all randomly generated, so one time you might spawn near lots of resin, and no compound, then the 2nd time it'll be the opposite.
The only downside for this game (apart from the optimization) would be the price point.  I don't think I ever feel comfortable paying $20USD ($30AUD+) for an early access game.  $10USD should be the max price, depending on where it's at in development.
If you can overlook that, then you'll definitely enjoy the game, I'm excited to see where it's going to go in the future, as it's got a great concept, and a great core as-is.
