20XX is a great game with great big flaws.
If you think me unfairly in favor of this game, I implore you to find my review of Enter the Gungeon. That game was so painful it made me bitterly against roguelikes.
To paraphrase the current US president: "The problem with Enter the Gungeon is not that it implemented rogue-like elements wrong, but that it implemented rogue-like elements faithfully."
20XX is different, better, and far more fun. This is because it removes the most terrible rogue-like element; 20XX removes torturing the player for no just or discernable reason and then removing your all progress in the game.
That being said, here some 20XX flaws:
-Moving platforms are sometimes too close vertically to jump in between them, or too closely packed together otherwise, causing many unnecessary falls. Some non-moving platforms also have this problem.
Examples include certain areas randomly found in the Fire Level (Agnisort I think it was called), the Sky Temple to a lesser extent, and the final level
-Your movement and jump stat bonuses will kill you. If you improve your speed too much, your character will fly off so fast they miss the platform you were aiming for. If you improve jump height too much, your character will accidentally slam into a spike or damage area. Movement needs to be consistent in a platformer, or it breaks the player's rythym.
-Minor art concerns. Not the style, but the animations bother me. The best example I have is when you stop walking. When you come to a halt, your upper body flings forwards slightly. It would make more since if the character stopped themselves with their legs, like happens in real life, but instead their upper body swings like a bobblehead for a moment. There are more examples of animations like this, but I don't have time to nitpick all of them.
Regardless of the above dialog, I will end this review with a sentiment many people here have clearly said and echoed.
"Don't get Mighty No. 9, get 20XX!"

I bought this during early access, played enough to know I liked it then shelfed it for its full release.
Three words:
Worth The Wait
If you liked Megaman X you'll like this. Normal difficulty is a bit on the easy side for those of us that cut our thumbs on the NES megaman titles. Even with this in mind 20XX is worth the price of admission. Randomized levels mean replay lasts as long as you want it to. Randomized bosses and subsequent upgrades mean you'll have much to challenge yourself with here. Tactics change drastically when for instance you don't have a double jump. Appropriate for both kids and adults.

Disappointed by a certain other Megaman-alike?
This game has a lot of what you want from a megaman X style game, with the replayability of a roguelite.
You've got standard "roguelike features", that is, permanent unlocks, procedural generation of levels, randomised order of content, and increasing difficulty as you progress.
Face it, when you were young you played megaman and were bad at it, so it took you a long time to beat it fully. Nowadays, you'd blitz megaman X in two days and drop it.
This adds enough random features that you've got an interesting challenge you can play repeatedly. It also increases difficulty as you get further into a run and offers you a choice of 3 of the remaining bosses to go after next, meaning there's no "easiest to hardest" or "boss weakness" ordering. Face your bugbear boss now, early game before he powers up, or collect your own arsenal to take him on later?
It's got dashing, jumping, wall climb jumps, boss weapons, charged attacks... and it doesn't have the awful combo dash score system of M#9.
It recognises the greatness of its forebears and uses them for nostalgia, BUT! It doesn't keep all features of the Megaman games - you can instead turn on some of the difficulty features as optional Skulls, such as "Instadeath Spikes", and you can increase difficulty in a granular manner with other skulls.

Astroneer is a very robust, immediately interesting execution of the "sandbox exploration" genre, I've been having an amazing time of exploring, discovering things, and making my own fun.
That last part is, I think, the most important. Any fun you get out of this game will be the fun you make for yourself.
This game is in pre-alpha, and is at the time of this review $20. This is a lot of money for an early access game. To be honest, if you have played this game for 5 hours you've more than likely seen 90% of the content on offer. There really isn't that much to the game at this stage in its development so if that worries you maybe wait.
As well, this game is very buggy, trying to use vehicles is a hassle, it's not uncommon for your character to phase into the ground, and idiots online are constantly using bugs and exploits to do increasingly stupid stuff (making podracers, getting infinite resources, etc)
That being said, the developers are constantly updating it and I've already put a ton of time into this game. I am finding it to be a lot of fun, and I can only imagine the shinanigans this game will get me into once I convince some of my friends to play it with me.
If you've been considering buying this game and are just looking for a review to verify your tastes, ask yourself if the above complaints matter and happy exploring!

Early Access Review; version 0.2.115.0
Astroneer, where do I begin? In the short playtime I have, I am lost for words about this game at the current point and the potential it has for greatness.
The game is inherently relaxing to play, the soundtrack is amazing and not only is it easy to plan ahead for what you're planning on doing next, it is very easy to get lost in exploration and what the game has to offer.
Of course, no early access game is without fault. So I will list the current cons.
Cons:
- Current bugs that I have encountered:
> Buggy spazzing out and flying off into the sunset
> Dying as soon as you respawn
> Burying yourself in the ground
> Falling through the world
> Sometimes the backpack refuses to pick up items from the dead body's backpack
- Lack of planets
- Little content at the current moment
- No way to change audio settings from max volume
- No graphics settings
- No 'real' flying (but this is planned on the trello)
The trello link:
This is a game that is more fun playing with friends as with the sandbox that the world gives you, you are able to do great and enjoyable things such as:
- Create a race track and race buggys
- Create a ski slope
- Dig to the center of the current planet
- Go joyriding around the planet
- And infinite possibilities
tl;dr: An early access games with it's share of bugs and glitches but that doesn't overshadow the enjoyable gameplay this space-exploration game provides.

A surprisingly fleshed out game.
It's a Landlord of Darkness's market, but some tenants, you'll find, are dirtbags that lose their job day one and stay home for the rest of their afterlives, begging for extensions on the rent; while others enter tenancy as lowly comicbook artists and end up being your welthiest, most combat ready, dependacy tenants.
The challenges to advance the game presented to you are a mix of medium to impossible difficulty. Don't expect to get anywhere without taking a few lumps.
All in all, a low attentiondemand game you can play for the most part while watching a show - but when you initiate a quest, it can take all the click-fu you've got!

text: this games physics engine is really accurate, and the depth in the mechanics when customizing your car is really good. The only downside to this game is the sensitivity in the steering. PLayng this game on a keyboard can be a challange at times because you have to judge perfectly the point where the apex of the corner and the time to steer into that apex; if you are too soon, you will understeer, and if you are too late, you will oversteer the corner. This sensitivity makes streemlining difficult too, because its really hard to maintain the colinear motion behind the car in front. This sensitivity does however make the game a lot more chalanging, and makes the F1 car feel nimble and makes chicanes a lot of fun.
